generated_text: Oh, did I ever tell you about's Dad's story when he took you and Sam to that Indian restaurant for my birthday? No, you didn't but I'm sure you will. You know, I've always remembered that because it was just so Dad! He and your partner went to pick the place, and he comes back and announces with a huge smile, "I've found the perfect Indian restaurant for your birthday! It's got a star for goodness!" But... ...it turned out it was a Michelin star, but not for Indian cuisine. It was for their French menu. He always seemed so proud, and we just had to laugh. He would. And the best part was, the curry they served us was still fantastic. He was right about that at least. I love that about him. He was so proud of his discoveries, no matter how random they were. Exactly. And now, speaking of family, have you given any more thought to our upcoming family gathering on the 20th? Not enough, I'm afraid. Where did you have in mind for this year? I was thinking maybe the botanical garden in the city center? They have such a lovely outdoor space for us to gather without too much hassle for you with the baby. That sounds lovely. And in terms of time? For the afternoon, I was thinking maybe 1pm to 5pm? It gives us enough time for a picnic, and the kids can play around. Sounds perfect, and if it’s in town, the baby will probably sleep through the drive there. And, if anyone needs a break, it should be relatively stress-free to find another adult to watch the baby for a bit. That's a great idea. You know, it's funny how we used to plan everything for our parents' outings, and now it's our turn. Absolutely. Speaking of which, have you talked with Dave about your plans to visit the relatives in Worthing next week? Not yet, actually. I just assumed he'd meet us there as planned. Make sure to confirm with him. And don't forget, if Dave can't make it, your parents are more than happy to help out there for a day if you need. Thanks... I'll text him today to confirm his schedule. Good, because I remember telling your mum about the plan and she was very excited for the whole family to meet up.

So, I hear you've been doing quite a bit of travelling in the EU recently. Yeah, it's been quite an adventure! I've been enjoying exploring the different cultures and landscapes that Europe has to offer. Really? Really – I mean, there's just so much diversity in such a relatively small area. For instance, the food – it varies so much from country to country, and often even within cities. And the history! Just walking through the streets and imagining all the things that have happened keeps me in awe. That does sound fascinating. Even the way people interact with each other is different, depending on where you are. In the north of Europe, the cultures can be a bit more reserved, whereas when you get down in the south, people are much more expressive. And the Balkans, that's a whole different world. Did you have any particularly interesting experiences? Let me think. Take your time. Alright, so I was in Naples recently. I'm a bit of a pizza and gelato fan, so I was excited to try as much as I could. I ended up visiting this small family-run pizzeria and they made this Neapolitan pizza that was unlike anything I've ever tasted. And the gesture – the way they served it for me was so warm and intimate. It felt like I was part of their family for the evening. That does sound lovely. Then, in Stockholm, I went through a park and came across this massive outdoor market that's only held a few times a year. There were all sorts of crafts and foods, but what really caught my attention was seeing these people weaving the traditional Swedish crafts right there in front of you. The intricacy and the patience of the process was mesmerizing. I ended up buying a few things to support the local craft. How long were you there? I think the whole trip was about three weeks. It was a bit rushed, but it was a good taste of what each place has to offer. I can imagine, but still so much to see. Did you face any language barriers? Some, but most places have catered well for English speakers, especially in tourism areas. Many younger people and those in the service industry do speak English, and I also tried to learn a few phrases in each language – just to show respect and also to help navigate a bit better.

So, after dinner, what do you think we should have for dessert? Hmm, maybe we can have some ice cream sundaes. You know, with the sprinkles and various sauces. Yeah or maybe just some plain old vanilla ice cream with chocolate sauce on top. Or maybe we make some brownies. Mom, can we make brownies? I'm not sure, I've been out all day and I'm still set for my dinner to even get digested properly. But maybe later. Can we play Monopoly after dessert? Again? We played it last week. And just like last week, you'll probably end up owning all the property and we'll be stuck with the utilities. That’s not fair! I’ll share some money with you this time. But then we’ll both end up with no money? No, no. You’ll have money and I’ll have money. I’m just saying we could maybe trade? Maybe give this house to you and you give me some money? Ah, I see. You’re becoming quite the budding entrepreneur. Starts at a young age, Mom. So can we do it then? Can we play Monopoly? Possibly, but after we finish dinner and have dessert, maybe as a group activity after? Yay! And we’ll definitely trade wisely this time. Okay, I’ll watch over your money for you, big brother. Watch out or I might just end up owning all the houses again. We won't let that happen this time. If we do Monopoly, can we play as characters from our favorite stories instead of just being rich business owners? That's an interesting idea. Maybe we can modify the rules a bit. We can make it a bit more playful. Like we're characters from Harry Potter and collecting different items or house points instead of money? That sounds awesome! And we can use pretend wands for Chance and Community Chest cards. I'm not sure how that'd work out with the property and rent stuff. But it can be fun. And when we pass Go, we could get a special magical reward or something. Well, that’s something we can think about. Like, if we land on a certain house, we have to do a little task or trivia question about the book instead of paying money. That could be fun, like what happened in such and such a book or who said what.

You know, driving down to the countryside this time of year is so much more bearable than usual, isn't it? Yeah, less traffic, more scenery. Speaking of which, have you considered where we're going for our holidays this year? Erm, no, not really. We need to catch up on some work things first, don't we? Your new project's due next month. Indeed. I'm actually thinking of using some consultants from the North next time. Seems like the North's got some fresh ideas that just won't grow out here in the South. Fresh ideas, huh? I think it's just different perspectives. From up North, you see things changing a bit slower, so maybe there's time to think things through a bit better. I hadn't looked at it like that before. Either way, it means my job's probably getting more interesting, which is all that matters. Speaking of job, how's the new one treating you? I heard it's pretty demanding. It can be intense, but I love the work. It's challenging and varied. Much different from the routine of being stuck in a office all day, which I think I would've ended up doing if I had stayed in university for another year. I know what you mean about routine. Sometimes I feel like I'm stuck in a bit of a routine myself. Like, the work's fine, but sometimes wish I could just go and see some different architecture across the country, get some inspiration, you know? So, you're having a bit of a functional successful life crisis? Something like that. Hey, what about those holiday plans? Wanna do something totally new this year, like maybe try out some volunteer work abroad? That could be really interesting. Always been interested in humanitarian work but never had the chance. Exactly! It'd be a deep dive into a different culture and people. Plus, could be just the break we need. Speaking of which, have you heard back from the NGO we looked at? Yeah, they offered us a spot. It's a month-long session in South Africa this summer. That sounds amazing! It’s completely new to both of us, so it'll be a bit of a jump, but how could we not do something like that? Right? Just make sure we're well-prepared.

Remember when we used to sit around and bemoan the gods for the state of the world and how we could never get ahead no matter how hard we tried? Yeah, we've had our fair share of that now, haven't we? Though I think we've given up praying for a miracle. It's not like our prayers would've been answered anyway right? Life never got any easier, just different. And here we are, all retired, still with nothing much better than before... I mean, we've got each other. That's something. I suppose that's true. We're lucky we've still got our health, our relationships, and the ability to just sit around and talk about our troubles. And even if we're out of work, we're not out of each other's lives. That's the most important thing. Plus, there's the little things that make life good. You couldn't pay me to give up my garden these days. I'm with you there. One moment you're cursing the slugs for eating your lettuce, the next you're sharing stories about how grand the sunflowers grew. Life's in the little things. And the odd time someone still comes around and gives you a bit of company, or the kids drop by with their families. That keeps things fresh. Doesn't it, Alice? Oh, I'm always happy when the young ones visit. Though sometimes I wonder what they see in our old, boring lives... Doesn't seem much to me, but to them, I suppose we're still just family. Well, in that case, we won't stop being the family we are. We've made our share of mistakes, faced our challenges, but here we are, still standing together. That counts for something, doesn't it? Definitely. We've had our ups and downs, but we've always managed to make do. And if I'm completely honest, there's a strange kind of peace in just living day by day, without fretting over what we don't have. You could say we've learned to appreciate what we do have. It's funny... when I was working, I used to think if I just had a bit more money or a bigger house, I'd be happier. But now I see it's not just about that.

So tell me about Honest Skincare. It's been a wild ride, really. I started it about a year ago. It's been a learning curve, particularly with all the various measurements and packaging sizes involved. I've just noticed the measurements, like the ml size of your products. It kind of threw me off because sometimes it's easier to understand the physical size of a bottle. Yeah, and I'm right there with you. Took me a while to get used to working with milliliters and keeps changing as I experiment with different formulations and sizes. You'd think it's just numbers, but it really makes a difference – especially for shipping. I used to teach math and sometimes I have students who just can't understand why converting between units is so important. But in your business, it really does affect the bottom line. Exactly. One time I ordered bottles that were a bit too small and I thought I'd be saving on shipping, but then realized that the cost difference barely covered the extra packaging resulting in sending more parcels. Now I try to keep the weights consistent. That makes sense. For me, teaching this is about bringing the concepts to life, showing how it applies in different contexts. Similarly, I'm applying this in my business. If I can get the packaging right, I reduce waste, make shipping more efficient, and the products look better on the shelves. It's amazing how a bit of thought on dimensions can make a big difference. And in teaching, getting students to see that is key too. Anytime they can relate it to real-life situations, they learn better. Same here! I've learned so much about marketing too. The way you present the products, the sizes on the label… it’s all part of the brand identity. Seems simple but it's really complicated. Definitely. The digital world doesn’t make it easier. You have to think about images on small screens, packaging that's appealing in 2D and 3D. Exactly. And then there’s making sure they’re all consistent across platforms, from your website to social media. I’ve spent hours just adjusting images to fit different dimensions just right. Reminds me of trying to find the perfect frame for an artwork. You know, most people think it’s about the painting itself, but the right frame makes or breaks it.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time during my first year teaching; it was chaos, Jeannie. The kids they don't listen, you think you've got control and then suddenly they're all out of the classroom and onto the playing field and I'm left standing there with one book in my hand and wondering how it all went so wrong. Ah, I remember your stories, you always had the best anecdotes. But how did you manage to gain control back? Well, it wasn’t easy, Jeannie. It took time, patience, and a bit of clever planning – always keep your best resource materials close by and never underestimate the power of a good cup of tea to calm down a chaotic situation. That’s so like you. And what about your own situation now? How's retirement treating you, are you finding it as fulfilling as you thought it would be? Honestly, it's been a mixed bag, Jeannie. I expected more structure or maybe something to fill the gaps left by teaching. But it's funny, once you retire, people expect you to suddenly have all the time in the world and be available 24/7 for grandkids, family stuff, the garden… It's nice, but sometimes I feel a little lost without my own classroom to manage. Lost? I wouldn't say you sounded 'lost', more like in transition. You always were so good at adjusting, even through all the years of changes in education and working conditions. And now, you have the time to focus on yourself and the things you love the most. Thanks for that, Jeannie. Maybe I just need to figure out what truly fulfills me now. As for changes in education, oh my, it's a whole different world now compared to when I started. Technology, curriculum shifts… It’s as if they're teaching kids to be mini researchers rather than just teaching a subject. You'd be surprised at how much of what you taught – research skills, critical thinking, problem-solving – is still fundamental. But yes, it's all about adaptability now, isn’t it? Absolutely. And it makes me proud to see. I do miss it sometimes, though. There’s something about standing in front of a class and seeing a concept click into place for a student – priceless. I know, I've felt that too. But there's still so much you can do from this side.

So, how was everyone's weekend? I heard Swindon's had some pretty chilly temperature; how are you coping with the cold at home? Oh, it's been freezing! I've had to double up on the jumpers and almost turn up the heating to max, but I kind of like the cozy atmosphere it gives to the house. Yeah, Newcastle's not much better. And to think that elderly folks might not be able to afford the extra heating... I had an old neighbour who said it was cheaper to wear even more keeps coming to mind. I've actually taken some time off from the workshop to deal with the cold. It's just too much to manage having to work with cold hands in your line of work when trying to make precise crafts. I've had to readjust some retirement thoughts from 'soon' to 'definitely next summer, fingers crossed'. Speaking of heating, have you thought about smart thermostats yet? They can learn your schedule and adjust temperatures accordingly, might save a little bit on bills. I'd never considered it. That could be really handy. I'll have to look into that. I've been relying on plenty of hot tea and mulberry jam for warmth. There's a mulberry tree in the back of my property. The jam makes a lovely gift at this time of year too. Sounds lovely! Have you got any mulberry recipes to share? I'd love to make my own jam next year, maybe even sell some as a craft in my shop. Sure, the key is to pick them when they're ripe but not overripe – you know, when they come off the stem easily. Then just mix the mulberries with equal parts sugar and lemon juice, cook it until it thickens and voilà! Right. Seems simple enough, I reckon that’ll be a lovely project. I'll jot that down. Mulberry jam is a unique gift idea and personally, I adore mulberries. Speaking of food, does anyone know any great recipe for making mulberry wine? I stumbled upon it online a while back but never got around to trying it. Mulberry wine can be a bit tricky because the fruit is quite delicate. You need to use a lot of fruit to get a good flavour and it needs to be very clean. I used to almost make it at my grandmother's.

Mum, Dad, everyone, thank you for having us over tonight. Dad, these steaks are amazing, as always. Thanks, sweetheart! I talked to Joe at the butcher down the road, and he sold me the best ones for this week. Really? I heard he's closed down his store and isn't selling meat anymore. That's a shame. Joe's always been a big help, especially when I've wanted something special for dinner. And how about that cutlery? This knife is a bit blunt. You okay with it, June? Oh, Bob, it's just the old set I used for thirty years. I wasn't planning to have anyone cut up a steak. You can always use my set if you'd like. My mother gave it to me for my last birthday and I think you might want it sharp. That's kind of you, dear, but no, the old set will do just fine. Besides, we're not carpentry here. Bob, or as much as it is rummaged through this house, we maybe need to get some new cutlery. You’re right about that, while the steak's good, the cutlery’s a bit of a massacre. A bit of a massacre? That's overdoing it, isn’t it? It’s just some cutlery. I could take a look for some cutlery when we're in town next. What do you all think? We could even make it a community affair… That's a great idea, Mum. Perhaps we could get something nice for you all as a present. Oh, no need for that, love. But it’s just the fact... We’re just fine, Bob. Just use this and we can deal with the world next week. But honestly, I was thinking changing the set up in here. New kitchen, updated everything. A new kitchen? That’s a big job. But not a bad idea either. It’s about time for some updates, isn’t it? Maybe we could consider that as a holiday project next year. It would be nice for you both, and it could even be a communal effort. Maybe set up a weekend or two over the holidays. Yeah, like a family project. Could include all of us. Well, I wasn’t expecting to talk about a new kitchen here tonight, but I suppose it’s never too early to start planning. Planning?

Oh, did I tell you about the job interview I had today? It nearly made me consider resigning from my current place! Mummy, you're not quitting your job are you? No, no, darling. Just the company seemed so disorganized and the interview itself was a bit chaotic. It made me wish I could just skip all of it and be on a nice ski trip instead. Skiing? When is that? Well, we're planning to go in two weeks. We're all really excited, aren't we? I just have to make sure everything is ready. So, can I help pack? Ah, that's sweet of you, but it might be a bit too early yet. But you can help pick the clothes and your favorite toys to take with us, okay? Yay! I can help with that. That's my girl. So, what about the interview then? Was it scary? A bit, but I actually ended up enjoying it more than I thought. It wasn't what the job was exactly but the people seemed nice. Like who? There was this one lady named Sarah in Marketing. She really understands the importance of teamwork and creativity, and it was nice to see that they value these things even when the system doesn't always support it. Do you have to choose between your job and skiing, mummy? No, no, don't worry. I won't have to make a choice. The ski trip is just a holiday. Jobs are for money and working, but holidays are for fun and family. So, can we go skiing on my Birthday? Your Birthday would be in a few weeks. I know it's not when we're planning to go, but maybe we can find a way to celebrate it then in a fun way? That would be so cool! It definitely would. Now, shall we talk to Daddy about everything after dinner? Yeah! [Conversation wraps up with the usual dinner chit-chat and clinking glasses for any announcements or special topics that family members share, though the specific details would be shorter and more conversational.] You know, mummy, can we play that game at the ski resort where we throw little discs? Sure, we can try that. It's called Disc Golf, right? I think we can fit that in somewhere too. Yeah, sounds like fun. The resort has a great course.

So, I hear you took over the lead vocals in the school's upcoming choir recital today. How did that go? Honestly, I was so nervous! But everyone was really supportive. We're doing a range of songs from pop classics to traditional English folk. It's supposed to be fun and engaging for the audience. That sounds great! I hope you get into the swing of it soon. I've heard you can ruin a song with enthusiasm... or bring it to life! True. Anyway, how was your maths lesson? Terrible! We started on quadratic equations today and I just had no idea what to do. Ms. Clark wasn't very helpful either, just said to try harder. You can always ask me or we can go through it together. I kind of get it now after doing all the past papers. That would be amazing, thanks. You're a lifesaver in maths. No problem. And did you hear Ms. Davis's announcement about the next term's food tech project? Apparently, we get to pick this time. Yeah! I'm thinking of trying to make some Spanish tapas. How about you? I was thinking of doing a traditional English dish. Maybe fish and chips or something simple, but appealing. That's a good idea, nice and easy but still interesting. I feel like we always choose the tricky things and waste time on details. For sure. Although I'm excited about Spanish. I'm hoping our teacher continues with the theme-based lessons. It really helps to contextualize the language for me. Yeah, that's one of my favorite subjects now. I kind of miss the days when we did only the basics, but it’s fun to be able to hold simple conversations now. Same. Speaking of skills, did you hear there's a job fair coming next month? No, when is it? It's on the 27th, and I'm thinking of checking it out. There are supposed to be people from local businesses looking for part-time jobs. Might be good for the holidays or later on. That would be such an experience. Maybe we can go together. For sure. We could just go and see what job postings catch our eye and what we might be interested in doing. Even if we're too young for most jobs, it's still worth checking out. Exactly!

So, I was browsing Rotten Tomatoes yesterday and came across that new film adaptation of "Dracula," you know, the one based on the novel. Have you seen it? No, I haven't but I've heard mixed reviews about it. That's what I found too – some people love it for its atmospheric and faithful portrayal of the original story, while others say it's too slow and lacks the modern sensibilities they were hoping for. I see. Film adaptations can be tricky like that. It's hard to please everyone. Exactly! But have you ever watched the Nosferatu from the 1920s? It's such a classic, and I think it really captures the essence of the original novel. Nosferatu? I read about it in a film study class but never got around to watching it. It's old, isn't it? Like, talkies or silent? Silent, yes. It's a German Expressionist film, so it's all about the visuals and the atmosphere. And it's got a haunting soundtrack, even though it's silent film era. I’m more of a modern cinema kind of person, but silent films do have their charm. Maybe I'll watch it this weekend. Definitely recommend it. It sets the tone for all the Dracula films that came after. And if you like the atmospheric stuff, maybe we can watch it together? Maybe with some snacks. That sounds great! And maybe we can talk about it afterwards, like, analyse it? Analyze it? You're making me sound like I know what I'm talking about. Well, you do seem quite knowledgeable about films! Thank you! But the point is less about analyzing and more about enjoying together. We could also watch the newer one after and compare. If you think I can sit through a classic silent film first. I think you’ll enjoy it. It's only an hour and a half, and you can always pause for a snack break. Plus, I can tell you all about it beforehand so you're not completely in the dark. Fair enough! This seems like a plan. So, are we cleared for a film marathon this weekend then? Absolutely! I'll pick the snacks. We can also watch another film we both like if you're feeling adventurous. I'm up for adventure. Always a good idea to mix it up. Perfect! I'll send you a list of some... atmospheric and modern films we could choose from.

Mum, I was thinking that weekend. I need to finalize plans with Nataly. We still don't have a set date for the hen do. Thought maybe the weekend after next? Mm, right. You've been really busy with work and all these exams the kids have been preparing for – do you have some time free then? I think so, yeah. I've been organizing my schedule and it should clear up then. I'm just hoping the weather holds. I'd hate to have everything planned inside for once. But even if it is raining, it'll still be fun. You'll need to book a venue, though. Right, I'll need to check out some options. You've been thinking of somewhere near water, right? Yeah, we liked places with big windows or outdoor areas. And hopefully, they'll have a couple of rooms available if the whole gang can't fit in one. That sounds challenging, but we'll manage. How many are you thinking? Well, Nataly said she might be able to ask a couple of her mates, so maybe around ten? I haven't finalized it with her yet. Ten is quite a lot. You might have to get creative with the venue then. Good thing they're adults; the party games can be a bit more interesting. Haha, true. Anyway, you're already arranging the nice weather. I wish I could. Next, isn't in my book, unfortunately. But you never know, we might get a good window. That's all I need - a nice window of good weather! I'll start looking at venues this week, then. Any preferences? Somewhere less fancy would be good; we don't want a black tie, just a fun time. I noticed a fun pub with a big garden on my way home last week. It might be worth checking out. That could work wonders. I'll make a few calls. What’s the budget looking like? Nataly’s been chatting some general numbers around. Maybe £50-£70 per head? But we can fit that into it. That should be doable. I’ll look for options. You could even float the idea of a themed party, just for fun. Oh, I like that! Not overly done but just a little fun twist. Something like retro or “In the future” since Nataly likes Sci-Fi. Retro could be fun.

I've decided I need a new wardrobe. I discovered today that nearly every piece of clothing I own is at least five years old. Five years? I need to check my own closet. I'm sure I have stuff even older than that. It kind of dawned on me when I was shopping last week. Like, I've worn the same three pairs of trousers to work every week for what feels like an eternity. That's probably for the best though, right? You know, environmental reasons. Reduce, reuse, right? Absolutely! Even lazy environmentalism is better than nothing, right? Though today I saw this cute shop near our flat. They have trendy but sustainable clothing. Oh, actually, while we're at it—do you want to do some shopping this weekend? We could make a day out of it, see the town, grab some lunch. That sounds like a plan. I could really use some new summer tops and maybe grab a few professional pieces. You know for the next few lectures. Yeah, sounds good to me. I could do with some new formal shirts for work myself. And maybe we can find some affordable, eco-friendly options too. Exactly. We should check if they have a weekend sale or something. I also really need some new shoes. My current ones are falling apart. Your shoes always seem to last a year longer than they should. I've lost count of how many times I've seen you scouring the clearance racks. Well, that's one skill I've honed over the years . I might even treat myself to some new boots. I saw some nice ones online recently. Nice boots would be good, especially if we’re doing more outdoor activities. Exactly! You were right to recommend those hikes last time we were discussing our trip plans next summer. I’ve been meaning to get more into hiking. Yeah, I think it would be great for us to do it together. We should talk more about the trip. Let's say we do set aside a few days. We need to check the weather, find some good trails... Definitely. We can start making a rough plan. I could use the exercise, and it'll be a nice change of pace from work. You know how intense these semesters can get, especially when you're teaching new courses. Totally. We're both under so much pressure during term time.

So, I thought we could keep the photoshoot date for Saturday's afternoon. Grace has today off; she's been super reliable when it comes to babysitting the kids, so that's the best window we've got. Sure, that works for me and the kids. But we need to get Ben on board because his haircut is today isn't it? I hope he won't be too tired or grumpy after that. I'm sure he'll be fine. I bought a few new books he hasn’t read yet — that might keeps his spirits up alongside a nice treat when he gets home. Good idea! And I’ve been thinking about baking some cookies since we’ll have some extra time this afternoon. That is a sweet gesture. Everyone seems to relax in the kitchen when there’s something fragrant and homemade on the go. Exactly! Maybe we’ll even get the girls involved with decorating. It’s creative and keeps them occupied. Right! And afterwards we can get them all set up for the photoshoot in the garden, while we still have daylight. Oh, perfect. We should also plan dinner for all of us. Not anything too fancy, but just fun and easy. I can cook up some pasta. That sounds great to me. And I can pick up some ice cream on the way back from Ben's haircut. A nice way to end the day. Ben is going to love that. Thank you for doing that. No problem. So, let’s confirm: photoshoot in the garden on Saturday, followed by a family dinner and ice cream treat. And how are we doing for refreshments and snacks during the shoot? Anything in particular you or the kids would like? The kids love lemonade, and a few sandwiches would be nice. Good choices. And maybe some juice boxes for the small hands? We can do that. I’ll also grab some fruit to make it a bit healthier. Good plan. Let’s also think about what’s the best attire for photos. Should everyone wear bright colors? Bright colors would be so cute, but also, if we’re capturing outdoors light, maybe neutrals would work better with the sunlight and background. That makes sense. We just need to make sure they all look comfortable and we don’t overwhelm anyone. Comfortable is key. Especially with Ben still thinking about his haircut.

Ugh I can't believe how much of a struggle it's been getting to these university canteens these past two weeks. The queues and everything. Oh yeah, unreal! I mean, I love that we've got actual canteen food now and all, but this is a bit much. And isn't it weird how everything is totally different from the year before? Completely! Like, where did all the good food go? Last year, there were so many options. Right? I mean, at least they've got decent coffee now. True. I heard about a decent coffee place just outside campus by the river. They say the barista is amazing. That would be amazing. I read online about some places in Kingston but I never get the chance to check them out. Exactly! Maybe we should plan a coffee outing with our group? That sounds great! What about over the weekend? And we could grab some lunch or something. And maybe watch a film or something. A gang movie would be so good this time of year. A gang movie? That’s not the vibe most of our group would go for. Oh, I was thinking more like Knives Out or something. It's not exactly a gang movie, but it's detective thriller. Should fit the mood. Aha, Knives Out! That is silly and fun! Yeah, definitely worth doing. I'm pretty sure everyone would be down for that. I don't think anyone would say no to laughing it off with some great coffee and that movie. Except maybe Emily. She’s super busy with her uni work right now. Oh right, her final project. I saw her the other day. She said she’s stressing a bit. Yes, poor Emily. We really should support her in some way. Yeah, maybe we can all chip in for a study buddy or something over the weekend. That’s a great idea! Either way, it looks like we've got a solid plan on our hands. So, how is everything going with the little one? Oh, you know. It's been quite an adventure. The feeding thing has been a bit of a challenge though. Good morning everyone. How are we all feeling today? I'm good thanks. Hope you all had a good rest last night. Ah, I was browsing on the internet yesterday and came across an interesting online shop. They sell various novelty items, but what caught my eye was a rat puppet. Oh, that sounds quite amusing. Let’s say we all go and make a day of it, take advantage of the bus travel too. The bus! You remind me, the other day I was thinking about the changes in fare systems and almost didn’t make my trip in time.

So, I was browsing on the internet yesterday and came across an article about how Venice has changed over the years. Have you seen that? Oh, talked about that recently. What was your thought on it? Well, I was surprised by how the number of tourists has affected the city. I mean, I'd seen pictures of the empty canals but I never realized the impact until I saw some real data and images. Yeah, I've heard about that. The sheer volume of visitors has caused a lot of issues like erosion, pollution, and overcrowding. It's kind of sad really. It is. It feels like the spirit of Venice is slowly fading away. I used to love the idea of Venice being so unique, like no other city. It still is in many ways though. There's still the old architecture, the little bars and restaurants that serve traditional Venetian foods. It's just a shame there's so many tourists now that you sometimes can't even move in some areas. Right? And the prices are crazy now. It's not so much the locals that businesses accommodate any longer or even the old-style restaurants that serve real Venetian dishes. I mean, you see so many pasta and pizza places that could be anywhere in Italy, not just specifically Venetian. Exactly. The food in Venice used to be quite specific and so good because the ingredients were fresh and local. Now, you can't tell the difference from anywhere else in Italy or even elsewhere in Europe. There is one place I found online that recommends really good, authentic food though. Apparently, they serve a traditional dish called "Fegato alla Veneziana" which is Venetian-style liver and onions. [laughs] Yes, that's a classic. I haven't had that in ages. But the article also mentioned that side of commerce; they talked about how a few families, they've been running these local businesses for generations, but it's getting harder for them to compete or even maintain their old way of life with tourism in the way it is. Yeah, and that's scary on a personal level. I mean, I wouldn't want to lose that unique character for the sake of tourism. Absolutely. Tourism, when managed well, can be a positive for a city like Venice, but when it's allowed to overrun, it's counterproductive.

So, I hear you've seen Tom again. Yeah, we met up for a drink. Old times. Was it awkward? Not really. It's been long enough. We just talked about old times and now, how we've changed. Cool. So, I hear you've seen some of the latest developments regarding bollards in our area. I've heard they're causing quite the stir. Oh yes. Bollards! They've become a bit of a controversial topic here in Lambeth. People have all sorts of opinions about them – do they help or hinder the flow of traffic? Indeed, and the council seems to be in a bit of a pickle about where and how to place them. Now, moving on to somewhat related topics, how was your recent trip to the British Library? Are you still working on your book? Oh, the Library is always a pleasure. I've been conducting research for my book, gathering information from some very interesting archives. The Spanish archives were particularly fascinating, speaking to Phillip II's efforts to marry Mary Tudor. You can imagine the political maneuvering involved - quite a story! That must have been a most interesting experience! I did hear about your findings at a recent lecture. It’s remarkable how much historical detail can be unearthed through such meticulous research. And it seems Spain was never without its share of drama, was it? Indeed! For instance, Phillip's efforts to prevent the Spanish armada from sailing when he found out that Mary might not survive childbirth. It was a tense time, but the Habsburgs had a way of managing politics that’s quite unparalleled in modern times. It’s certainly quite different from how we deal with things today. The Spanish archives must be incredibly well preserved, especially considering the time periods you're researching. They are, and that’s a testament to the Spanish and their respect for historical documentation. But it doesn’t come without its challenges – the bureaucracy there is the real gem. As much as historians may praise the meticulous nature of certain archives, one’s own archival research can be less than romantic when measured against months of paperwork and permissions just to access. I can imagine! Our local bureaucracy can be challenging too, but at least we don’t have to deal with the ins and outs of Habsburg politics! Speaking of challenges, the local housing management has been on my nerves lately. The new landlord of several blocks around here seems completely out of touch. Complaints about maintenance and safety issues just fly over their heads, it seems. This isn’t new, alas. The struggle between the need for housing and the efficient delivery of services.

Yo, you hear about that new Marvel comic that came out? We've been waiting so long. Oh yeah! I bought it last weekend. That new character is so unreal! They've done a good job with the art this time. If we plan carefully, we could actually execute something real. But it won't be easy. Exactly that's...we'll have challenges, but we can work through them together. Plus, it's a skill in itself, right?

Right okay so I think it's time we started making some plans for Jonathan's birthday. Yeah! I was thinking maybe we could have a big dinner at home. That sounds lovely! So, I've been thinking about my GCSE options and I'm still not sure what to pick. Yeah, it's a tough decision, isn't it? What are you considering? Like the other day, I was listening to a podcast about bloggers and how they make money just by writing about what they like.

Ah, I hear that the wildlife in this area has been flourishing lately. I've noticed more birds and even some rabbits around here than I have in years. Oh, yes! It just shows how much the community cares. And the places of historical interest around here - they're doing an excellent job. Though sometimes I feel like they're a bit too much about the big names and not enough about the local lore. That's true. It's often the small, lesser-known stories and places that are just as interesting. I've been trying out some new history apps on my phone, they're actually really useful. Interesting, I might have to check those out. I've been meaning to learn more about this area's history. Yeah, apps are a godsend, aren't they? I'm still finding my way around using some of them though. It's like learning a whole new language sometimes. Oh, exactly! I tried to set up a new computer for my granddaughter and we’re trying to get all the software sorted. It's like trying to learn a new language doesn't come naturally to everyone it seems. I know exactly what you mean. Except, I've been meaning to design a course on basic computing for older folks. Seems like the demand is there. That's a great idea. I've seen a few courses pop up locally, but they're often quite expensive. Yeah, and then there's always the issue of accessibility. Not everyone has access to these resources. It's a shame. You'd think that with all these technological advancements, we'd also have more broadly available education on how to use them. And have you seen the new policy on retirement age and benefits? Again, it feels like those of us who are almost gone yet still quite active in the community are frequently overlooked.

I seen them educazhun systems's changed since I was a lad. Nowadays they teach 'em all about computers and whatnot, and they don't even seem to know their own times tables. Ha! That's true! I remember when a piece of chalk and a blackboard was all you needed! Well, times have changed that's for sure. I'm of the generation where computers started to creep into schools. But still, it's heartbreaking that some kids can't get their heads around simple stuff like maths. It's not just the curriculum, Bob. What with all the tests and league tables, schools are under so much pressure. It must be stressful to be a teacher. And the places of study now! I never saw a classroom look as fancy as what I see on TV. All those gadgets and screens, I'd be more interested in looking for a football to play with than thinking about a textbook! But these modern tools can be very helpful. Access to information's never been easier, Bob. So, it's not all bad. Aye, that's true. Still, I remember when a textbook's all we had. And they were passed around from generation to generation. Good hard work in those pages, I thought. And the wardrobes today? Some kids look like they've got more clothes than we had for the whole family, all lined up neatly in their own wardrobes... Can you remember John? Oh, Lord preserve me! All I had was one decent suit for Sunday, and the rest was "hand-me-downs" from my brothers and cousins! You'd think I was emperor if I had two pairs of the same socks. I remember, John. Our wardrobe was more like a pile. If you needed something, you just had to dig through the pile! But nowadays, changing the world takes place more on social media than anywhere else. Tweeting and posting every minor event in their lives. I'm sure in my day, if I had a headache, I just took a bit of patience and maybe an aspirin. Now, it's "tweeting my headache"! Yeah, and the "deliverymen" they all became! I mean, I got my first flat screen delivered. It was bigger than the TV we all sat around as kids thinking it was the biggest wonder of the world. Well, it’s certainly changed the way we communicate and order things.

I've made sure to put beans on's Dad's plate. He'll be chuffed. I talked to her about the tea and garlic bread. Are we still making that? Yeah and I'll bring the dessert tonight. We'll have questions for you all about your favorite foods when you were growing up, and now. You know, right? We never talk about food enough. And we never get to taste each other's cooking. Did she make it with spinach or just cabbage? Oh, it was always cabbage. Spinach was something fancy people ate. Mum, I can't believe how much of a difference it's made having you back in the kitchen. The food tastes like home again! Thanks, dear. It's the proper way to do things, I always said. We'd have a big roast every Sunday, and then... of course, there were always arguments about what to have with it. Speaker_5 keeps chucklesome alongside, nodding in agreement. Speaker_2, arranging plates on the table, chimes in. I used to love Sundays at my grandma's too. We used to go to Ronny's butcher in Bishop Auckland. He'd give us a bit of extra for free on his son's birthday. I never got as much as yours sounds like, but a Sunday roast was always a treat. Nowadays, it seems like nobody has time for it. Speaker_5, while adding a bit of condiment to his own plate, starts telling a story. Ah, come on, it wasn't so bad, was it, Dad? I remember my Aunty Elsie, she'd cook for a small army and expect all of us to be at her table by 1 o'clock sharp. And if you were five minutes late... Everyone laughs at the thought. Speaking of food, I tried this new recipe last week for shepherd's pie. I really liked it but I tweaked it a bit to make it healthier. You sure you won't try some? Speaker_3, intrigued: What did you put in it this time? Well, I used sweet potato so it's lower in carbs and also added some of the spinach that's been growing in your garden. So, I was browsing on LinkedIn yesterday and came across an idea about gamifying university study. Imagine students getting XP and levelling up based on the assignments they complete and the exams they pass. What are your thoughts on that? That's quite fascinating, isn't it? I kind of do something similar in my classes. I encourage the students to set up challenges and group exercises, but turning it into a game format could be brilliant. It could make learning more engaging, perhaps fracturing out those negative mind-sets towards traditional studying. Exactly. Plus, people love playing games. You get immediate feedback, satisfaction, and progress. It creates this intrinsic motivation to keep going. I think if we could introduce some kind of system that rewards students publicly for their achievements, it could even spur some friendly competition. That makes sense. But we'd have to make sure it's not isolating for those who aren't as progressed or perhaps have learning difficulties. It has to be inclusive, right? Totally. We could have different types of 'achievements' or 'badges' for different skills and competencies. So, while someone might struggle in one area, they could excel in another. Perhaps we could incorporate some AI tools to recognize these strengths and suggest personalised "quests" for improvement. Brilliant. And don't forget the portfolio aspect. Students can curate a digital portfolio of their achievements and reflect on what they've learned through the game format. That could be really powerful for future job applications or further studies, especially if it's linked to industry-based requirements or skills. For sure. It’s all about accreditation and transferable skills these days. I'd likely want us to involve industry partners to make the 'quests' relevant. Maybe even have companies sponsor or provide the 'quests' themselves based on the skills they need. That’s a whole other level. I just tried to crowdsource a similar project for my class on environmental science. The students worked on real-world problems within their local community. It was fantastic, really engaging and it got them interacting with the science on a deeper level. But sure, on a bigger scale, involving actual businesses could drive home that what they're learning is for 'real'. Sounds like we're on the same page. So, how do you see this evolving? For a real university-scale project, would we need software development, and if so, perhaps you could connect me with some of your students who might be interested in co-developing something like this.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that Halloween party Grace threw? It was a riot. Well, I've talked to her about the escape room we did for the party. You know, one of those mystery games where you have to solve puzzles to leave? We were all so engrossed and had such a good time. But then, the real fun began when we realized the timer was a bit wonky and we had to actually dismantle the box to get out. Are you serious?! That would have been so funny if I was there! Oh dear, I can imagine. Anyway, did your week at the new project go okay? How's everything coming along? Yeah, it’s been chaotic. There's so much to organize. Hence, my constant coffee intake. On the up side, I managed to squeeze in a fun retreat with some of the team last weekend. We spent the day in the countryside, doing these medieval cooking workshops. It was weirdly fun. So you took your gang out For a medieval cooking day? I'm curious, what did you make? We made some pretty basic stuff—like stew and flatbreads. But the best part was the okra stew. We were all so skeptical at first because okra can be kind of... slimy, right? But it turned out to be really good once you seasoned it right, and it's got this really rich flavor. Okra? That's a bit of a culinary adventure. But it proves that project management can be fun, kind of like food—it's all about understanding the right ingredients and how they come together. More like understanding the right timing and just leaving the project to simmer for a while. Speaking of food, have you checked out this new café near by? They have this amazing vegan cheesecake. No, I haven't. Vegan cheesecake, though? That’s the real test for any café. It’s surprisingly good, I assure you. And it's only five minutes from here. That sounds great! Maybe we can even go there for lunch this week. Perfect! I’m sure it'd be a nice little break from all the bureaucracy. Oh, and thinking ahead, have you thought about what you want to do for your birthday this year? We already started planning the birthday trip already. We're thinking about heading to the Lake District for a weekend.

Right, so I had a bit of an incident at the station's groceries store today. The self-service machines were down and I was clearly the only one who didn't have a smart phone to book a time slot. If the technology fails, without decent support, everyone gets frustrated, right? It wasn’t just frustrating, it was really demoralizing, standing around for an hour and a half. And to me, that’s a reflection of how we doesn’t value our time. I completely agree. As someone who works in this field, I see it all the time. The effect of poor decision-making or under-staffing can be really detrimental. The thing is, it wasn’t just the wait, it was the attitude from the staff. It’s as if they’re just following a script without really thinking about the customer experience. I was reading an article about how customer service should be a bit more empathetic. Like, sure, people say automation’s better and all but it can't always replace a kind word or a nod of understanding for the situation. Exactly! That checkout assistant seemed so robotic. Yeah, and the thing is, I've had similar experiences with other local services too, not just shops. It feels like there's a growing sense of impersonality. Impersonality. But at the end of the day, that’s often due to this ‘do it digitally... because we can’t afford to...’ mindset.

So, I was browsing on the internet yesterday and came across an interesting article about scientific methods. Like, I didn't know until I read this article that there are set stages for doing experiments even in fields like computer science and biology. It seems like these methods are really adaptable. That makes sense, I guess. I mean, if we're thinking logically and questioning our assumptions in our own research, we're using a bit of those methods anyway. Exactly! But the article also talked about the importance of peer review and collaboration. It said how these things are becoming even more important with the way research is changing, especially with so many international collaborations happening. But think of it this way, peer review is also really important for making sure the work is solid before it gets out there. I guess I just wish there was a quicker way to get feedback sometimes. Maybe there will be in the future! I mean, technology is changing everything, even things like how we share research and collaborate. I just tried to learn a bit of French for my translation studies course and it's really tough. I mean, language can be so nuanced, right? Oh totally! I struggle with changing the verb tenses in English sometimes, let alone a whole new language. Exactly! But in French, there’s like so many exceptions to each rule, it’s so confusing. Oh, I completely agree. But it’s so useful, and it’s cool to think about how much work goes into just being able to communicate in multiple languages.

So, I was at my sister’s yesterday and she was showing me this fascinating story she found online. It was about people who deliberately introduce spiders into their homes to deal with pest issues. You mean as a form of natural pest control? Exactly, like a kind of do-it-yourself pest control. Some cultures even do it and I find it totally bizarre, but others seem very into it. Well, I can see the logic, especially if someone is opposed to using chemical pesticides. But I wouldn’t want to have that many spiders running around my house. You know how it is, one spider okay, a colony not so much! Definitely. I can attest to that from my early years. My family and I lived in an old house for a while, and we had a little spider friend who lived behind the old grandfather clock. He was quite harmless and even helpful, I suppose you could say. Helpful? How? Well, in the way that he would catch those annoying moths that get into carpets and clothes. He was a spider, not a spider or a mite or whatever, but a proper cobweb spider. One day, he even caught a mouse, but that was a bit unsettling. A mouse? That's impressive. I wouldn’t think spiders could handle mice. It was a tiny one, probably a young mouse. Still, it showed his worth in catching pests. But I wouldn't want a bunch milling about for the same reason you mentioned – it's nice to have them around for the benefits but not have them overdo it. Mm… mice are another story altogether. Last year we had that problem with the mice; it was a nightmare. First, we tried using traps and it seemed to work for a while but then the numbers just grew. Eventually, I just had to call the pest control. I was experimenting with humane traps at first, thinking maybe we could relocate them but... Relocation’s a great idea in theory but can get tricky depending on where you're relocating them to and ensuring it's a natural habitat that can support them. Exactly, it can be a bit more involved than just catching them and letting them go elsewhere. And then of course there are the birds. Ah, you're bringing this into the mix now? How so? I love birds, but sometimes they can be a bit of a nuisance.

So, I hear that your mother was from Bristol? Yes, that's right. Bristol was my mother's hometown and where she spent most of her life. Fascinating. I've always found family connections quite interesting. Do you have any idea about your ancestors? We recently started putting together a family tree at home. Oh yes, I've been into that a lot. My family has been in Bristol for generations actually. We've got records dating back to the 1800s. There's an interesting story about a great-great-uncle who was a sailor, traveled all around the world before settling back in Bristol. That's amazing. I'd love to hear more about that. It must have been a bit of an adventure for the time. Yes, it was. They even kept a journal that has been passed down. One of my grandchildren is really interested in history, and we've been working with them to learn more about our roots. That's such a rewarding thing for kids to do. It gives them a sense of where they come from and what shapes who they are. Now that I'm a teacher, I'm always trying to connect historical learning to personal experiences. Exactly. My mother would love the way you’re teaching kids to connect with the past. Speaking of teaching, I remember your teaching career quite well. Ah, yes... A long career. I had to retire early due to health reasons, unfortunately. I'm so sorry to hear that. What was wrong? I had been dealing with cancer for a few years. It was quite the battle. I'm grateful for the time I had to give to my students and for my own family during that period. Cancer... that must have been incredibly tough. It was. But we tried to keep life as normal as possible for the children while my husband and I were going through it. My kids were very supportive, and my son even decided to study medicine because of it. That's inspiring. It’s moments like those that remind us of the impact we have on our children and the importance of our own influence. It does. And now, my retirement is a little bit busier because I'm helping my grandchildren with their school work and just being around for them. That sounds like a wonderful way to spend your time.

I keep thinking of that time we saw that hot air balloon just hovering over the field like it was just deciding what to do. Oh yeah, unreal! Made me feel like we were in a really lazy version of Up. Exactly! I've never been in a hot air balloon, but I've always wanted to. Now that you mention it, there's a place in Norwich that offers hot air balloon rides. Maybe we could plan something for our next trip home. That would be amazing! Definitely makes for a very unique picnic spot in your garden. Might just encourage the wildlife even more. Speaking of which, we haven't really seen many big animals around here - just a few deer and rabbits. It's amazing how quickly the wildlife moves out of the way before you notice them, though. Absolutely! We have these amazing experiences and it feels like it's so rare, but really, it's happening all the time. Like the time our dog, Ruby, chased a rabbit right into a field of high power lines. Oh my! That was chaos. We were praying she wouldn't come close to any of them. I was sure she'd get zapped, but she ran silly fast and in circles, as if she knew they were off limits. It’s always a reminder of why we need to be careful with her in areas where the fields are used for agriculture or have different types of equipment. Definitely. Speaking of equipment, the trip we took into the true wilderness was one of the most challenging yet unforgettable. The camping. I mean, we’re not exactly experienced campers. It's one thing to camp in a proper camp site but to rough it and not have any electricity or running water for days - that’s a different story. The money we spent on gear for that trip wasn’t trivial either. And for what? Two blissful nights of figuring out how to set up the tent in the dark. Blissful? Maybe... recover from exhaustion blissful. But it was still worth it. It gives us stories, I suppose. Though now I know there's a huge market for inflatable camping chairs and portable showers... True that. We're also talking about DIY camping glamping, really. What can I say, laziness and convenience know no bounds even when we're pretending to be outside enthusiasts.

Ah, I can't believe how much of a difference it's made to have these classes today. The sun is lovely and it's really lifted my mood. Yeah, the weather is quite nice for this time of year. I really miss training outdoors on the tennis courts though. You know, when we do face questions on this kind of thing at the job and it gets me thinking about the physical side of coaching, not just the technical aspect. True. I was just discussing that same thing in my teaching class. We're trying to implement more practical teaching methods, alongside the theory. Sometimes I think we get too caught up in the slides and the textbook and we forget the importance of immersing students in the language and having them experience it. Absolutely, it applies to both language and sports - you can't just read a book and expect to understand or do it yourself. I always tell my team that you have to physically experience the moves and the language to really grasp it. Exactly. It's the same when it comes to books, right? You can read all about it, but it's not until you really engage with or even teach it that you fully appreciate the depth of something. That's true. I've found the same with most things in life really. I love the 'How to Win Friends and Influence People,' for instance. You read it and think, 'This makes a lot of sense' but it's not until you're out in the world applying Dale Carnegie's principles that you see how much it can change your interactions and in turn, your life. I couldn't agree more. It’s similar to learning a language. Just reading doesn’t cut it - you've got to use it, even if you make mistakes. And that’s the beauty of teaching and coaching - you see the impact. My side of commerce, it's seeing people reach their goals, feel more confident, or just become healthier and happier. Oh absolutely, and for me, it’s seeing students grasp and then use concepts of language that they thought were too complex. It's incredibly rewarding. Absolutely, so gratifying. Although I will say in my experience, sometimes I have a rough day when it looks like nothing is sticking with a student or one of the staff members doesn't absorb a new technique right away, and it’s frustrating.

Right okay so I've been over the bill for this quarter and I've made some estimations. It looks like we're gonna be able to cut back on the heating a bit, so that's good news. Right, that's good. That's why I said we can afford a bit extra, it's not breaking the bank. And we could also see if the government has any schemes to help pay for it or lessen the blow? It’s often easier to replace them during the spring – less disruption when it's warmer. But if we get a better quote before winter, we might as well do it then. That way we’d save on the heating straight away for the coming winter. Exactly. So maybe in the next month or so we should see what we can find, and then make a decision. How about we discuss this again at dinner when the others come over? Might bring it up for everyone to weigh in. Good idea. I’ll make a little note for that conversation.

So, I've been thinking a lot about changing career paths and I've been looking into starting a small business of my own. It's not just about making money, though that wouldn't hurt. I've decided I need to lose some weight Dad. Look at this. It's been two weeks and I've lost five pounds. You should be proud of me! Well, my sister is thinking of organizing a family picnic in the local park. Seems like the weather's looking up, so that could be nice. That sounds fun! It's meant to encourage people to use the car parks instead of driving around trying to find free spots. Makes sense. I guess it could help if it reduced the amount of traffic in the town centre... True. But people are also talking about the cost. That might be a concern for some. Maybe they can have a discounted rate for locals.

So, I've been meaning to follow up on that social media idea you mentioned at our last family gathering. Oh yeah, the Twitter thing? Yeah, you had some great insights about using Twitter to engage with our audience. How have you been experimenting with it since then? It's been quite useful, actually. I started a Twitter account for the school about a month ago and we've already seen some engagement. People seem to actually want to hear about what we're doing here. That's interesting. You must get a lot of parents and local community members interested? Exactly. Even our students have started engaging with it, sharing pictures of class projects, that kind of thing. How do you handle the content? Is it just about sharing news from the school or do you try making it personal as well? It's a mix, really. We share official news and updates, but we also try to share things that might not traditionally go on a school's website—for example, if we're participating in a local event, or if there's something quirky or interesting happening in the classroom that day. We've found it helps build a more personal connection with our audience. I think most of our communications team is still hesitant to dive into social media. They're more comfortable with traditional newsletters and things like that. It can be daunting at first, but I think the key is to make it feel organic and authentic, rather than forced. And it can actually save a lot of time if you think about it—there are a lot of stakeholders who might not read a newsletter but would catch a tweet. Right. It’s also the immediacy of it. If something exciting happens, you can share it right away and get people buzzing before the next newsletter comes out. Exactly. Plus, the visuals. Sharing photos or even little videos can really capture people's attention. So, what about the management of it all? Do you have a team dealing with the account or is it mostly on you? I handle most of it, but I try to make sure there's some consistency by posting at broadly set times each day, usually around lunch and early afternoon. I've also started a small "tweet of the week" project with a few colleagues. One person per week gets to pick an interesting story or piece of news to share.

Oh my god I'm so annoyed, I've been running around today like crazy and now there's no food in the house! I don't know who ate all the pasta but I had dinner planned. Sorry about that! Right okay so I've been thinking. You remember Dave was saying he might have to come today. Oh yeah, I forgot to look at his voicemail. Better check it out then. Just, you know, for the meal questions. Sure, I'll do that now. Yeah that makes sense. He said something about actually looking into the train schedules if he comes. That sounds lovely, but we should make sure ANON is comfortable with that idea. Of course, we should check with her. Yeah, maybe a weekend? That would be nice. The bay's always nice, but I've heard there's a new seafood place we should try. Oh, really? That sounds like it could be a great dinner spot. Can they accommodate a large party? Then we'll make sure ANON is on board too, of course. Definitely, we wouldn't want to plan something she wouldn't enjoy. No, absolutely. Right, well I better check on the seafood place then. That would be great. Oh, and about the meal we're having today, did ANON say if she wanted something special? I think she's been craving some of her grandmother's recipe, but I'll double-check.

So, I've been trying to learn Spanish using this app, Duolingo. It's actually pretty good, but it's hard! I wish I had started earlier, back when my brain was more malleable. Ah, I had the same problem with trying to learn any language late in life! But, you know, it’s never too late and it’s something to keep the mind active. I took up a little bit of Catalan when I visited Barcelona, just to have a sense of accomplishment. Two languages? That’s impressive for anyone! Yeah, and it’s not just the languages themselves. It’s like seeing the world from a different perspective. I’ve always loved linguistics, just the way languages shape societies and cultures. Absolutely, speaking a bit of another language can really enhance your travel experiences. But from what I've observed - and even my son, who works in a multinational company, tells me - the younger generation seems to pick language learning more easily with all these apps and such. They’re exposed to it through media, games, you know, these global connections we have now. I know! I’ve even noticed that my grandkids pick up this sort of stuff so much quicker than we did at their age. Everything’s so accessible with the internet. Where did you get your exposure to Catalan? Oh, just a couple of trips to Barcelona over the years. It’s a bit different from Castillian Spanish, isn’t it? The people there seemed to always mix the two, but they’re very different languages in practice, right? Oh, absolutely, and they have their own culture and literature. It’s quite rich. I was surprised myself when I realized it wasn’t just "Spanish" that was spoken there. Yeah, and if I may offer some advice from a career in construction side of things, where we used to deal with international collaborations... having a second language, even a little bit, increases your market value. It proves you’ve had exposure to different cultures, which is really valued in today’s world. True. It also helps with things like restaurant ordering or basic interactions when abroad, though that was more of a motivation for me. But you're right about market value. It’s something I always encourage my students to consider. For me, it was more about enjoying the trip and being able to have basic conversations.

Right okay Dad I think this one might be worth looking at. We've got these two documents that don't quite match up. See if we can figure out which one is the most current. I'm old-school, I prefer to know exactly where my money is going. I get that, but with all the security measures now, online banking is actually quite safe. And it saves you a lot of time. Mm. Well, let's get through this or I'll never be done. So what's this about corpus linguistics? Oh, that's what we're doing at uni. We're basically building huge databases of spoken and written language. It helps us understand how language is used and how it's changing over time. Is that like a big dictionary? Well, not exactly. A dictionary is a snapshot in time, but a corpus is like recording all of the language in use all the time. It’s pretty cool stuff. So you're the one that’s always babbling about finding the next famous phrase? Kelly Brook’s tweet or something? More like looking at patterns and changes in language, Dad. In fact, there's a book that was recommended to me this year, it's...

Oh, did you see that?? We've hit traffic again today. It's like London's never gonna let us drive normally. Yeah, that's just life here. But hey, at least it gives us some time to catch up, right? So how was the day so far? Busy at the office, just usual papers and stuff. But right now, I'm just enjoying this road trip with you. Nice! You know, I've actually been meaning to ask... Actually, that's perfect. I was planning to stop at the next service station to grab some snacks. But man, these petrol stations... some of them could be a little cleaner, don't you think? Totally. So, dirty bathroom jokes aside, have you noticed this trend with bikers? Like, wherever there's a petrol station, there's always a biker. Yeah, it's like their little hangout. I guess it's because it's the perfect stop for a rider. You know, grab a snack, fuel up, and maybe refuel themselves, I suppose. Yeah, and they always seem to have these great Harley-Davidsons. Harley-Davidsons... I'm actually thinking of getting one myself. Don't you think it would be cool if one day we could have the same ride? Oh, I'd love that! But it'll be ages before we can even think about buying one. For now, we can just enjoy the view of others riding by. Yeah, I guess that's true. Speaking of which, I was on a video conference call for work today. My team’s working on a new project that requires us to re-engineer some of the existing infrastructure for sustainable energy uses. That sounds so useful! Sustainable energy could really make a difference here in England. Definitely. And you know, part of that project involves improving the efficiency of fuel consumption in vehicles. Maybe one day, we'll have electric or hybrid cars all over the roads here. Electric or hybrid... that's... kind of scary for the petrol industry, no? Maybe a bit. But it's progress, isn’t it? Plus, it’s still a bit early for worry. At least for now.

So, I hear you've been practicing your tennis more often recently. How have you been getting on with it? Yeah, it's been going alright. I played a match last Saturday and although I lost I felt a bit better about my serve. Still working on that though. Good on you for sticking with it and putting in the time. I remember when I was your age, I spent hours out on the courts trying to improve. There was nothing I loved more than a good game of tennis. And how about lessons with Dave? Are they helping at all? They are, yeah, actually. He's been giving me tips on my forehand and volley and I can really see the difference in my play. It just needs more practice, you know. And what about when you feel like you're not making progress or things just aren't going your way? That's a big part of it, I think - finding ways to cope when it gets tough. Hmm, that's something I've been struggling with. Sometimes I feel like I'm not improving and it's frustrating. But I guess it's like everything else in life - progress isn't always linear and it takes time and effort. Absolutely. And most importantly, it's all about the effort and the enjoyment. You're in this for the love of the game, not to make money or anything like that. It's a sport, remember. It's meant to be fun. Exactly, and it's not just about winning in the end, it's about the journey you're on. It teaches you about discipline, about working harder and smarter, and about resilience. Yeah, that makes sense. Thanks, you two. Just talking about this makes me feel more positive about it. That's the spirit. You know, I grew up playing racket sports too, and for me it was a huge learning experience. It taught me about skills development, about strategy, and about sportsmanship. And what's so great is that those skills translate into so many areas of life. Like in your current studies, or even in a job when you're older - the ability to handle challenges, to strategize, to work hard. Yeah, I can see that now. So keep at it, and don't be too hard on yourself if you're not improving as fast as you like.

Yo, I can't believe we're having to use these napkins. They look like underpants. [laughs] Ooo, they sure do! Maybe that’s because they’re from Aunt ANON. So, how was your week? It's been alright. Got through the marking and everything for the mocks. The new system they've brought in is quite comprehensive but the training was a bit rushed. So, I thought we could keep it simple for supper tonight. We've got some chicken. How about we just grill it and do some roasted veggies? Sounds good to me. As if people would actually say they're not good enough. Laughs I can imagine. So, what did they suggest today? Just more of the same, I think. More delegation, more strategic planning. The different pasta sauces they have. You’re sure you don’t want to cook then? Maybe later. We can get a takeaway, relax, and watch an episode of The Walking Dead or Trapped. Speaker_2 changing the subject: Speaking of relaxing, have we got a decent blender? No, not for smoothies or anything like that. I have a rough one that just about chops stuff up. But maybe layering with a nice sweater and those jeans would be good if it's chill.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time I was convinced today would be the day I’d finally learn what my soul mate looks like? You mean that long list you've been compiling for years? Yes, exactly! That list. It started as a joke but now I'm pretty sure my soul mate loves hiking, writes his own poetry, and has eyes so blue they make you wish you were a fractal just to see them properly. All the good deals are gone so early in the semester. Totally. You'll have no chance if you're not on top of things from day one. I swear, finding a place here's like trying to get into a sold-out gig. Did you guys hear that our friendly taxman needs a little more from us this year? Yeah, the government decided to increase the income thresholds. Guess we're not going to be seeing those extra pennies after all. Ugh, just when I thought freelancing might actually give me a chance to save. Now it's just for the fun of it, I suppose. For me, it's just about making ends meet until I find a part-time job that’ll actually pay the bills. Or until I graduate and get a proper job. Yeah, but the university is always so full of events, right? At least there’s something to look forward to besides exams. Oh, absolutely! Last week I went to see Manchester United play City. It was insane, but really fun. And then afterwards we’re always talking about the highlights, who scored and all that. Yeah, I wish I could've seen that. I'm more of a fan of the story-telling sessions, especially when Uncle Jack visits. He's got the most hilarious tales about our ancestors. I love those, they always teach me new words and phrases that I wouldn't normally use. Plus, it's nice to hear how people's accents have changed over time and how some pronunciations have been lost or changing. Accents, yeah. I always thought Norfolk sounded so...unique, especially when some of our friends speak. Norfolk? More like Norfolk Brokeblart. Haha! No, but honestly, some of the words are quite different. Or even just shopping. Over here, we just call it shopping. But sometimes when I’m with relatives in London, I’ll use words like “getting the shopping”.

Mum, can I please try that seafood pasta? Okay but make sure you like it before you order too much. Remember the last time? Yeah, and we still don't know what happened to the rest of that fish pie. Well, I'd like to say it ended up in my belly, but I didn't get any of it. Alright, alright. I'll split an order with you. Which one do you like? Umm, let me look... okay, this one here, yes. It looks good. You need to learn how to pick perfect plates from a menu. Thanks, Dad. And how was your day at school? Any important tests coming up? Yeah, Mr. Thompson said we need to start revising for the English GCSEs. I'm pretty nervous. Well, don't worry too much. You'll do fine. Just make sure you time yourself this time. You spent too long on some questions last time. I'm more worried about my university applications. I've got everything sent but don't know if I'll make the cut. You'll do great, keep focusing on your essay and studies. It's all about showcasing your passion for what you want to do. You're always stressing, Al. It happens to all of us. I know, it's just hard not to think that one wrong move or bad grade could ruin everything. We all go through that. More than worry about the result, focus on the process of application and learning. That'll take you further than getting anxious about acceptance or rejection. Absolutely right, David. There's always another opportunity if you keep trying and learning. Like Dad always says – there's always some bus to catch in life for another try. Exactly, Sam! And dogs too – just a bit more loyal. Dad, stop giving them business advice. Oh, we're a little business ourselves here, plus with the joys of mopeds. So, have you started thinking about getting a job? Sure, it's too young, but it never hurts... I already have a bit of a part-time job at the supermarket, just a bit like what mum did when she was younger. Maybe next year I might get a moped. Great idea, though make sure you stay safe at all times on that moped. Absolutely. Safety first. And as soon as you start earning, start saving. It's good to have a little nest egg for those unexpected university expenses.

I've got photos to show you from Cornwall. It was beautiful. The tin mines are truly something. Reminds me of the days when I worked at YHA volunteer. Oh, isn't it wonderful now? Yep! I just got back from teaching a day in Yorkshire and people couldn't believe the pace at which the history just unfolds. Teaching? That must be a challenge. But diverse too, right? Kids today, they're not like us... or are they? I mean, I taught a day care group last week... Oh, the stories I could tell. But back to your photos.
