From what I recall when I helped my dad set up his allotment, we did buy a few tools—like a spade, fork, some forks, cultivator for weeding, and a watering can. But some allotments do provide some tools or equipment if you're a first-time plot holder. However, it's definitely recommended to start buying those you think you’ll use often. And what about water? Do we need to bring our own or is there access? Usually there's a communal tap somewhere.

Yo, Lucy, did you hear about James and Emily?? We've been mates since school. Oh yeah! I heard they're deep into this relationship now. Yeah, right! They're literally inseparable now and I swear they even dress the same – always matching questions or some kind of code. Haha, they do look like twins sometimes, don't they? And the waffle about commitment? All very serious for their age! True. It's like they skipped right over fun flirty stages, straight to planning their wedding. I mean, I'm happy for them but sometimes I just want to tell them to stop acting like old married people! LOL, same! But maybe they're just on the same wavelength. Hence the stellar syncing. Perhaps. It's just... they sometimes make me feel old! Like, when did my childhood friends decide to pair up and plan futures? Well, adulthood creeps up on you, especially at uni. For me, it's more about focusing on my degree than relationships. Totally get that. I just hope they know that we're still here for them. Whether they're single, in a couple, or planning a family, right? Of course! And they keep asking us out for couple stuff – which is... nice I guess. But sometimes feels like an old crowd vibe when we all really just need to chillout. I know. It’s weird but needed. I don’t want our friendships to feel like it's now just "we two, you two". No way! We're here for all of you, in or out of love. More importantly, together as friends. Exactly. Speaking of which, did you see those plans for the Donny stag do? It's next month, right? Yeah! I saw the Facebook invite. It's going to be a laugh. Anyone plan on coming? Well, for me, it depends on my assignment load and if mum gives me the money. Oh, don't tell her too early! They always want to say no. Hah, you're right. Let's just see if we can fit it in. Yeah, and if not, just the usual pub night will do. How's your assignment? Struggling but it’s going. Want to maybe work on it this week together? Coffee... or ale depending on our progress...? Deal! Let's just make sure we don’t talk planning futures though, alright? Haha, perfect. No discussions about commitment or sacred youthful vows.

Yo, anyone got plans later or we sticking around? I'm probably still around, just been super busy with uni and stuff. Thought maybe grab pizza, hit up a few more quests on that new game though? Yeah, that game, the new one. I kind of regret spending money on it already haha. You playing and complaining at the same time as usual? Haha, absolutely. I'm still struggling with actually getting good at it. But damn, the graphics are next-level. Totally get it, graphics are insane. But yeah, pizza it is then, and more gaming? Even lazy Sunday gaming is better than sitting Idle. Agreed. I was just looking at online reviews to decide if I was stuck with it or there’s something better for me. Then I saw "Two hours of guided quests to help you build character strength!" Thought that sounded up my ally. Wait, so basically it's spoon-feeding you the best items and skills? I feel like these games are just getting easier and less challenging every year. I don’t know, maybe it’s me just getting old, but I found it pretty frustrating trying to figure out how to level up my character without spending extra money on guides and stuff. I wish they’d give you more of the good stuff for free. True story, the grind can be a bit much. But then again, without the grind, where's the achievement? Aka, no, I still hate the grind. Yeah, but it's the little secrets and tricks that you figure out and feel like you're part of the community doesn’t it? Like, it's not just about the progress but the community. You're right. And sometimes you discover these little quirks the game or player base has come up with - those are fun. Plus, the story of the game is actually really appealing if you're into that sort of thing. Yes! Like, if you really get into it, you start noticing the little details changing according to where you are, or the time of day. It's insane how advanced these games are getting. Plus, I love the way they handle multiplayer and community events, it's always something new happening. True, like the last huge event they did. It felt so real, like it was the apocalypse. And the way people collaborated, or just had fun going around messing with each other - those were highlights.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that film we saw last week? The one with all those ghosts and whatnot. You mean "The Ghost of Hamstead"? Is that what it was called? That’s the one! So, there was this one scene where this character walks into her room and there's a whole group of children ghosts! And the way the house suddenly gets really cold? That part was quite chilly. Yes, and the projector just blinks off, and then on again. It was so much like your old projector that had problems. Oh yes, that projector that just decided it wanted to take a break. Do you remember that one time we tried to watch something and it just stopped mid-scene? And we were all sitting there waiting for it to come back on, wondering if it was going to continue the plot or just end there forever. That was quite a moment. It wasn't so much the film that spooked me or even the projector. But the whole situation... this is a house that's been here for decades, and you never know what secrets the walls might tell if they could speak. Well, according to the film, we’re probably the safest place on earth. It seems like ghosts spend more time arguing about who gets the nice bedroom than causing trouble. Indeed. But, regarding films really, have you seen that new drama about family and all? What's it called? Oh, you mean "The Family's Secret"? It just came out in cinemas. It’s supposed to be pretty good. Haven’t seen it yet myself, but I heard the reviews were great. Really? I was thinking we might get a group together for a film night at our place. You could bring some popcorn and we can have a proper screening. Maybe even watch "The Ghost of Hamstead" again first to get everyone in the mood. Oh, that would be brilliant! Plus, I can show you some of the new recipes I’ve been trying out, as long as we don’t spoil our appetite too much with all the sweet treats. Alright, agreed! But popcorn is a must. No argument there. You know how much I love good cinema snacks. Don’t worry, I’ll make sure we have plenty. How about we set a date for next weekend? That way, everyone has time to clear their schedules... or at least pretend to.

So, I was browsing through those new magazines at the chemist's. Did you see those? They've got some really interesting language research articles about how dialect changes are being accelerated due to global communication. Yeah, I saw that. Wasn't it fascinating how the old, traditional Welsh dialect is being mixed with English in the newer generations? You've studied that for your research, right? Absolutely. It's so interesting to see language evolving especially when there's such a high level of cultural exchange and migration. Are you still working on that project? Yeah, actually. I've been applying for grants to fund further field research in communities where the dialect is really prominent. Did you guys see the new episode of The Undateables? Oh, that was fun! I love how they're breaking down those societal stigmas. Yeah, and it also shows how language can create barriers or bridges, right? The pairings last week were surprisingly insightful about communication beyond spoken dialects. I hope they continue exploring that aspect. So, are you up for playing some board games later? Absolutely! I've been meaning to try out that new one I bought – it's about building words in different languages. It should be a good challenge. Sounds interesting! Have you seen the new DVD for Friends? I keep hearing it's really well done. Yes, I actually got in an interview about it for a podcast I'm guesting on. I'm nervous but excited. I went to the spa last weekend. It was so relaxing! Ah, I need that. Ever since the deadline for editing that new magazine was so tight, I've just been so stressed. Spa day tomorrow then. Perfect! It'll be great to unwind. Yeah, I felt so pampered after all the treatments. That's what we need after our week of work and stress. And maybe later we can all go through that pile of DVDs and magazines together? Or even host a little board game night and invite some friends over. I love that idea, especially if we can find some new games to challenge each other. And I can tell you everything I've been learning from those language articles I’ve been editing. That’s a great idea! And don’t forget to bring the snacks. Chocolate, of course! Agreed! Maybe we can also make it a dinner thing and just hang out for the whole evening.

So, I thought we should talk about that washing machine first. We've been meaning to replace it for ages now. Yeah, it sounds like a priority. Was there something specific that made you think of this now? Well, it just suddenly stopped working a few days ago. At first, I thought maybe it was because of a faulty switch, but now I'm not so sure. And to top it off, I'm pretty sure it's beyond repair at this point. That sounds like a major inconvenience. Have you started researching new models yet? A bit, but to be honest, there's so many options out there that I'm kind of overwhelmed. I was thinking of looking into some of the online reviews to see what would be the best fit for us based on capacity, energy efficiency, and maybe some user-friendly features as well. Yeah, makes sense. Did you have a favorite brand in mind or a particular budget range? Not really. I'm open to suggestions. You're quite well-versed in these things, what do you think? Honestly? I’m more of a stickler for quality than a specific brand, but if I’m to recommend, I’d say look at the Samsung or the Bosch range. They’ve got good reputations and seem to balance features and price points well. However, the best advice I can give is to carefully consider how often you wash loads, whether you need specific programs for certain types of clothing, and if energy efficiency is a top priority for you because that can affect your decision too. That's helpful thanks. So, when I’m doing my research, things like that. Exactly. And might as well look at delivery and installation options because that can vary based on who you buy from. Also, I’ve been seeing some smart washing machines, they connect to WiFi. Do you think that's necessary? Not necessarily, but they can be quite convenient. For instance, you can start a wash cycle from your phone, so if you forget to set it before leaving the house, you can do it remotely. It’s also useful for getting notifications when cycles are finished or if there's a problem. But, it depends on how much you value those features and if you're comfortable with a smart home setup. I see. Alright, I’ll bear all this in mind.

Oh, did I ever tell you about the time we were looking for a house and we realized what northern prices are like after leaving London? Oh, yes you did. You were right though, it is really different isn't it? Absolutely, and do you remember how shocked we all were at the VW scandal? But even that couldn't have prepared us for the housing situation up here. True. I mean, house prices are almost laughable compared to how it was when we moved from Walsall to Birkenhead. Back then, even with my teacher's salary, we could afford a nice place. Exactly, and I used to commute from Birkenhead easily into Liverpool and it was even affordable. But up here, we're talking about places that cost a lot more than they even need to, just because they're in the north and not the south. Yes, and yet, the livelihood up here, the cost of living, the access to… well, it's good in many ways but it's shocking how much more you pay for those northern amenities compared to southern ones. Oh it is. We went round a few estate agents and even tried a few "for sale by owner" kind of deals, but the prices were still staggering. Like, St Bees over the water, it's gorgeous but you can't even touch a place without it costing you over a hundred thousand more than the equivalent in Birkenhead. And it isn't just the house itself really is it? It's location, the area, all those extras. I know what you mean. Even with all the beauty and charm up here in Cumbria, the economic situation seems to be… well, it’s hard to say it's fair. It’s strange because in theory, a house in the north of England should be a lot more affordable since living expenses can be lower. But it seems like house prices have just kept rising for no reason other than it being in the north. Right, it's especially ironic when you think of how much pressure it puts on people who grew up here but want to stay. Imagine having to choose between a lower cost of living in the north and being able to afford a house for your family. We're lucky in a way, because we could have saved up more if we weren't just starting to settle down here.

I've decided I'm going to move houses. To Grace's today. Well, well, talked about that for ages, you've finally plucked up the courage. Just don’t upset the staff at the B&B this time. Remember what happened the last time we went to Lincoln? Oh, I won’t this time, I promise. I learnt my lesson. And how was that keeps coming backwards and forwards with nothing else to do. You'll need to make some new friends there. True, true. Idle minds are the devil’s workshop. Though, to be fair, even then I was fairly well-behaved in retirement places. Behaving is going strong your stellar reputation as a polite pensioner! Indeed, your very politeness got you ensnared in that tax situation last year. Remember that? Well, that was more a matter or lack of understanding than any intent to cause trouble. Now that we're all "retired," how are our pensions looking? I know it's a sombre subject but let’s face it, it's a worry for all of us. Fair point, Judith. Mine hasn't been as generous as I hoped, especially after investing in silly things. Exactly my experience. What's with these "growth" plans? More like shrink doesn’t it? But it's not just about the money now, is it? It's about keeping active and engaged. Absolutely. I've done bits of childminding in retirement, a few days a week. Helps keep my mind sharp and I get to see the young ones grow up. Good for you Julie. While I might not be so active, changing hotels and B&Bs keeps things interesting. Well, for me, moving to new places has been my way of exploring. Plus, it’s so much easier than having to deal with all that computer rubbish. Ah yes, computers... I've just managed to figure out the basics. You put in what you want and sometimes, it gives you what you need. I’ve given up. I just call Mark whenever something goes wrong. He’s taken to referring to me as ‘Pleading Grandma’. That's good though. Having someone to rely on helps so much. Absolutely. And speaking of reliance, how’s your housing situation looking, Georgie? You were considering that housing development outside Norwich weren’t you? Yeah, the prospectors came around again. But to be honest, I'm still waiting to hear if there’s something I’d be interested in.

Yo, I can't believe what happened in biology today. What? You mean the new theory about evolution we learned about? Yeah, but it was so unreal. The way they're still making it controversial really gets to me. Biology and science aren't bipartisan issues, you know? Exactly! We're talking about hundreds of years of research. It's like people forget history sometimes. Plus, why the need to politicize everything? It's frustrating. True that. You know, alongside biology, something else in school really grinds my gears – the way people still bring up lazy stereotypes about gender roles. Oh yeah, that's been a pet peeve of mine since like forever. People saying, "Oh, you're good at maths? But you're a girl," or the reverse. It's so 1950s. It's more than just stereotypes though. It also comes down to sexism, racism, and all these things. And these prejudices get ingrained at such a young age. I know, right? Like, why? I mean this is the 21st century, come on people! The other day in class, this kid just started spouting this absurd comment about 'diversity' being the cause of all troubles. [laughs] Seriously? Well, at least it gives us a chance to call them out. It does but it also makes me wonder, how do we combat this? It's not just about arguing with each other but also about educating and having these conversations properly. True, it's about breaking down the systemic issues. For example, even the way we teach things in schools, sometimes it's just so Eurocentric. You look into the true origin of most scientific concepts and a lot of the times they came from non-Western cultures. Exactly. Like, we had this one project where we learned about ancient medicinal and scientific knowledge from areas like the Middle East and India. It's astounding how much we miss out on or credit to Western scientists out of ignorance or bias. And it’s not just history or science. Even in religion classes, we barely touch on non-Abrahamic religions. It’s like 99% focused on Christianity and Islam with the occasional anecdote about Buddhism or Hinduism. And let's not forget the topic of gender. I recently watched this YouTuber who advocates for gender neutrality and it was really eye-opening. The way they talked about pronouns and their experiences with gender identity... It made me realized how often schools treat this as taboo or hush-hush.

So, how was your operation? Did it go smoothly without any complications? Yeah, it went alright. They told me I've got to take these new tablets three times a day. It's just a pain to remember. Oh, the meds. I remember when you were younger, you used to have trouble remembering to take your daily vitamins. Yes, I guess some things don't change. Now, with your cleaning job, how's that treating you? It's a job, keeps me active, and it's essential work, you know. But sometimes it feels a bit rough on the body. Did you hear from Sarah lately? She's been trying acupuncture for her back. Yeah, but from what she said, acupuncture's not an exact science. She doesn't know if it's working or not yet. Ron, you know how Sarah is, always experimenting. Acupuncture, yoga, the next thing it'll be blacksmithing! That's my Sarah. So, how about the rugby on the telly last weekend? Did you guys catch any of it? The rugby? Yeah, the Wasps did alright. Still, I think the game was a bit slow. I miss the old days of faster play. Can we talk about something else? I’m trying to avoid all this tech-talk and sport talk right now. I'm sorry, love. Of course, what else would you like to talk about? How about your garden? Did you finally get the new roses planted that you picked up on your last trip to the nursery? Oh yes, they're looking beautiful. But I did have to get the greenhouse MOT'd before I could confidently plant them. And I still need to get new tyres on my car for the winter. That reminds me, my lorry used to need new tyres all the time. Good times. Yeah, well, I guess it's just part of owning a vehicle. Did you guys make those hospital appointments for next week? Yeah, cleared it with the reception. Hopefully, those will go smoothly and no delays this time. We can all do with those going smoothly. Always something hanging over you when you've got appointments like that. That's true, but you've got each other. You know how much I value that. I always say this when talking with Sarah... Don't get started on the importance of strong family ties or I’ll have to remind everyone why we're here today!

And remember, it's important to have empathy for everyone. Imagine how it would feel if someone was taking you from home without your parents, wouldn't that make you really sad and scared? Yes, Mummy... and it was hundreds and hundreds of years ago, so very long before we were even born. Do you remember when we read about Martin Luther King Jr? He fought for justice and equality for everyone, just like people still do today for different issues. Like when they took all the toys from the store? Close, like when someone is unfair to another person, we try to make it right. And wars... well, they're very complicated, but usually they happen because of disagreements between countries or sometimes even within a country. But we don't want disagreements! Exactly! That's why it's so important to talk things out and listen to each other, or even just talk to each other about how we're feeling. You both are doing so well learning about these big topics. These things are sad, but learning about them helps us understand the world better and how we can make it a more fair and kind place. It makes me sad... It does, doesn’t it? But remember, we can always do something in our own way to make a difference, even if it's just being kind to our friends and helping those who might need it. But it's not just about the people that were taken away, it's about the people who helped them, too. That's very thoughtful of you to point that out. There were a lot of people who helped the slaves escape. They were brave and were also fighting for justice. Just like we’ve learned about people who help others in need today. Like the firemen and police officers? Yes, exactly! Firefighters, police officers, but also doctors, people who work in charity and many others. They all help in different ways. Can we do something to help others, like a charity project? That's a wonderful idea! We could plan something together soon. Maybe we could collect toys for less fortunate children or even make some art to donate to a charity that helps those affected by war. I like that! Maybe we could even make a big picture for the charity shop wall with all of our friends helping out!

So, I was browsing TV shows yesterday and came across an old classic. Remember "Dad's Army"? Oh yeah! I haven't talked about that show in ages. I've got a feeling though that some younger folks might not understand the humour now, the war references might need some context. Exactly! You'd have to explain the whole narrative around the backdrop of World War II and the Home Guard. I've actually introduced it to some younger co-workers and I had to fill in a lot of blanks. But even so, it's still hilarious. I think some of those jokes are timeless. I remember when our dog used to try and "attack" me every time he heard a certain tune from the show and it'd make me laugh. And the characters, oh, the characters! They're so well-developed. And funnily enough, I've heard talk about remaking the show with more modern content. That would be an interesting experiment. But it might lose that same charm. I mean, it's not just about the humour, it's about the light-hearted yet poignant look at that period. We could have a debate about it! Definitely. I mean, they've remade other classics and I'm not sure it's always worked. Still, I could see the appeal if they managed to spin it well. Speaking of reboots, have you guys seen the current gossip about "Sherlock"? I hear they're thinking of doing a new series but with... really unusual characters? Shows are never going to stop "rebooting" I suppose. But they better keep that guy playing Sherlock... He kind of owns the character now. Yes, or just bring him back the way we know and love. More mystery-solving together with his trusty sidekick. On that note, did any of you catch the recent animal welfare documentary? Oh, yes! That one about the great apes and changing the world. It really made me sit up and think. It was touching. They highlighted the work done in these conservation projects and I was surprised just how much animals, particularly primates, can influence our thought on ethics and conservation. It's funny when you see how interconnected everything is. Just like our little household almost acts like a mini-community. We care for our pets and consider those we don't, even if they're far away.

Right okay let's get this over with. Yep. Yay. Alright sweetie, let me help you first. I need to do the silverware basket. That’s right – do you remember how this goes? Yep, I got this. Perfect. Speedy Stephenson right here. Now, you remember George Stephenson? Our very own railway engineer. Yeah, like Thomas the Tank Engine? No, no not like Thomas – but he’s kind of like the inventor of the modern train. Oh, really? Absolutely. He invented the first locomotive called the Rocket. And he’s from Derbyshire. Where's Derbyshire? It’s up north, near Wales. And his invention helped people travel faster and further. Exactly! Railways really changed the world. So, remember this is a bit like helping to connect people and things, even if it’s just the plates and cutlery. So we’re like the good guys making everything tidy and organised? Well, kind of. But today, we’re just doing the dishes, but ya know, it keeps our home train, our railway, running smoothly. Yeah, and it helps Granny, and all of us. I like helping doesn’t feel boring that way. Exactly! Just like finding the right track for our dishes, George Stephenson’s work helped find the right tracks for trains to move people and goods together. So are we good track layers today? Absolutely. You two are making this run smoothly. Thank you both. Can we read about George Stephenson later? Absolutely, after we finish. And Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets! After the dishes, we have a family book club. Yay! Now, this is the final station. Get those last few dishes in. Done! Well done. You two are our best railway engineers. We’re Team Railway Rescue! Yes! And I think that’s our job done for today. What’s next? Well, now we can relax a bit. Maybe play a game or watch a movie together? Can we watch Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone? Sure, after we get everything back in its place. I’d love that. Oh, can I put this back on the shelf? Go ahead. Just be careful, it’s a bit higher up. I’ll help you! Thanks. Alright, now that we’ve tidied up, let’s get into some magic and adventure. Yay! Great work today, Train Conductors. Thanks, Mrs. Teacher-Stephenson. That’s me. George Stephenson would be proud of our railway of dishes.

Yo, anyone hear about that new craze - supper clubs? We should have one. Oh, that would be fun! But I don't know much about it. You two are always into something new. Let’s look it up and plan one! Yep! Sounds great! I could bring a few Australian recipes to mix it up. That's a brilliant idea! Australians make some of the best dishes, don't they? Oh for sure! Speaking of recipes, have you guys tried Olive's new website? It's pretty cool, she's got a video for every lazy Sunday brunch recipe. Yeah I saw that. The mornings are so quick, just like the website is. It's actually really good for quick recipes. I've been making her summer salads. Exactly! So quick, I love it. What about you both, got any legal dramas? I just saw that episode of SVU where this girl got stalked through the Words With Friends app. That was crazy. Oh god, that was wild. We should be more careful about who we play with online. Indeed. I assumed we only matched with friends. Good thing they caught the guy though. Yeah, really unsettling. Though I used to have some interesting interactions with people from all over the world on WWF. Oh, but now you're always in study mode, right?  laughs  Alright, focus focus.  laughs  Just been busy with coursework but that episode proves you have to be careful even with something as seemingly innocuous as an app. Definitely. And let’s not forget about jobs – the baking's been crazy this week. I thought I was going to lose it. Ah, job stress. I’ve had my fair share of it too. Last week I had to deal with a customer who thought changing the milk to almond was a reasonable restaurant mistake. Well, that’s some reasonable thinking. Millennials.  winks  Gotta love ‘em. Back to food, are we having pasta for dinner? Sounds good to me. I could make the sauce real quick. Perfect, I can help with the cooking. We need to make it match the vibe of the supper club. Great, I'll prep whatever else you need while this is cooking. And don’t forget to chop the veggies into artful shapes – we’re aiming for that guest-worthy dish. Don’t worry, I got this. Though, remind me to get some tips from the WAHLE site again for presentation.

So, how was your weekend? It's been alright. Got some time to chill out at home. My kid was causing quite a ruckus, so that was fun. Ah, the usual weekend with kids. Exactly – always something. I've been trying to encourage her to learn some Russian though, and it's going... interestingly. She's picking it up bits of phrase here and there but mostly just repeats "Da, da, da!" and says she wants some "cheese keepsake." Cheese keepsake? That's adorable. Yeah, she heard I used that phrase once and now thinks it's a real Russian word. Kids can be so creative with languages. My daughter loves "hello" in all different languages. Hence, she says "Hola, Bonjour, Kak dela?" even though she's decided that sometimes it also means "where's my snack?". That's very useful. Do you also have to deal with English language quirks here or is it mainly the IT side? Both actually. We're a diverse school, so I find myself helping with translations during parents' evenings sometimes, while on the job, it's more about making sure the print jobs are running smoothly and troubleshooting when papers are jammed or whatever. Ah, the joys of IT. A paper jam can seem like the end of the world sometimes in an office, can't it? Definitely. And with the reprographics, it's like... doesn't matter what language, it's the same frustration when a job doesn't print right or the colour's off. Exactly. Seems universal. Speaking of, have you had a chance to check out that new café in town? They're supposed to have amazing Russian salads. Oh, really? That sounds interesting. Maybe we can grab lunch there soon? You'd have to take me on a tour though because – I confess – some of the names in these new places are often so confusing in English. Absolutely! I'd love that. We can show you the best dishes. And maybe this way, you can introduce me to some more English food that I should try. Always keen to expand my culinary horizons. Oh, there's a lot of that here. I've been introducing you to Sundays joints and fish and chips, but this might be a fun... cultural exchange of sorts. That sounds great! Let's make it a workweek lunch date then. Excellent! I'll bring a list.

Mum, can I please change the radio station to something else besides's this stupid classical music. It's too boring. Oh, sorry about that, dear. We've been listening to that station for years, and it’s nice background music now and then. But okay, go ahead and choose something else. She's got good taste, though. You might like that music one day, you know, especially when you're stressed out or trying to focus. Right now, I’m stressed out because I have to get this massive book back to the library. Like, lazy Sunday today was supposed to be all fun, but nope. It’s like that sometimes, but you know, the library is there to help you learn and grow. And maybe you can make an appointment to extend the due date if it's too much this week? Yeah, and also, your friends might want to study together, right? Maybe pair up for the boring bits and save some time. That’s not how that works. We’re supposed to study and do it ourselves, or else it’s cheating. But yeah, I’m sure we’re all waiting for study breaks. Alright, alright, we’re not trying to be the fun police. But let's talk about something fun for a sec while we’re driving. Hey, how was the new blanket we bought for Emma? She seems to love it. Oh, absolutely adores it! She’s been cuddled up under it every evening. I have to say the quality is really good for the price we paid. Yeah, I’ve seen some great ones in the store, too. They’re so soft and the designs are cute. Are we going to need another one soon? Not for quite a while, I think. But if we need it, we can easily grab a new one. You know, it's things like this that remind me how much things have advanced over the years. When we had kids, we didn't have all these convenient baby items, right? Oh, you're right! And now with all the technology and safety features, it’s a completely different world. I remember almost going crazy during my first child’s nap times because I had to keep checking if they were breathing. Now, there’s just the baby monitors for peace of mind. I heard about all that from you and your stories.

Mum, can I please play that new strategy game online first? Okay sweetie, just for a bit then. We need to discuss Christmas presents and travel plans first. You two are still deciding where to go for Christmas, or have you? Well, we were thinking maybe this year we could have a staycation and then maybe plan a trip for the summer. The cost of travelling has gone up so much and I'm not sure we can afford two big trips in one year. But Mum, how is that going to make me feel better about not going abroad this Christmas? I've been planning to visit Spain with my friends! I can see both sides of this. A staycation could be fun, like maybe going to London or visiting the UK coast. But we also need to balance our budget. I promise you we're still thinking about it. It's not decided yet, but we do need to be mindful of our finances. You know we want to make sure we have enough for your university fees next year and so on. I understand that, but I still feel really down about not going abroad this Christmas. It's just that it's been promised. I understand the sentiment. Let's talk about it more, but for now maybe we can plan something fun locally? We could even do a little holiday at home - we can decorate the house, have some good food, maybe even make a movie night? That sounds alright, but it's not the same as experiencing a different culture for Christmas. I get it, but there are also some amazing places to explore locally. We could take a train to Brighton or Cambridge... there's the university there too which would be interesting for you. Cambridge would be cool, but it's not the same as Spain. I know, I know. But we are looking at ways to make it special for you. Just because we're staying local doesn't mean it can't be exciting and memorable. And changing plans isn't about not valuing your feelings. It's about making do with what we have and being flexible. I'm sure we can come up with something that'll make you happy. Maybe later today we can look up ideas online? Just to get an idea. That's a great idea.

So, according to my class reading yesterday, if you've got any valuable resources in Minecraft like tin, copper, and iron, you're clearly well-stocked up for building and tool-making, right? Yeah! You can also craft other things, like candles, from those resources – do you remember how we made those gingerbread cones? Yeah! Like the story where "Pippi Longstocking makes the best gingerbread cones of all time!" Do you remember that, Eliza? That's how she used iron and sand to make her "Pippi Mix" in our adventure. Oh, that was such a fun story to read to them! But, dear ones, you have to remember that in our world, we have to dig up those metals – sometimes we have to work quite hard for them, unlike in Minecraft where they're just laying around everywhere. Exactly! So, did you know that in some parts of the world, iron is really very rare and valuable? That's why in stories and history, people travel very far to get it. I love the stories where people invent their own legends about where this metal or that metal comes from. Like how in some tales, gold is said to be the sun turned into metal by fairies while the sun was still shining. Isn’t that interesting? It really illustrates the importance and the mystery people associate with different materials. It's like in our world, people once believed that certain fabrics were only for certain people – like the very wealthy could wear silk because it was so rare and hard to make, and all that. Just like how we doesn’t wear silk everyday, it's special and only for occasions. Except, we've made all these different fabrics ourselves in our Minecraft world, haven't we? More accessible for everyone, which I guess changes the story of the "value" it carries – since anyone can get it, does it value less or more? That's a great question! It shows how concepts of value changing according to where we are – in Minecraft, everything can be recreated and it's a bit more equal. But for us, in real life, the rarity and difficulty in obtaining something can increase its perceived value. Can we have a real world treasure hunt to find some metals and fabrics? Maybe even invent some legends of our own about where we found them? We could!

Yo, mate, did you hear about that strict policy they've introduced online regarding paedophiles? Yeah, I saw it. It's about using algorithms to spot the fences and stuff, but I'm not sure how effective it will be. Honestly, anything is better than nothing. But it’s so bad that we have to make those kinds of rules. Totally. I'm glad they're actually doing something about it. Anyway, have you got any keepsakes from when we first started playing music together? You know, before we had proper vocals? Oh yeah, I’ve got my first ever guitar I used for our band Smokey Meadow. It’s like my baby. I remember that one session we tried to record at your house. You had an old cassette recorder and a boombox. Haha, that was hilarious. We were so proud of our two-track system. Right? And we thought we were so professional. I still keep that guitar as a reminder. Nowadays, I’m more into tech for music production, but it's good to have that starting point to look back on. Yeah, it's amazing how things change. I was at a gig the other day and the sound quality was unreal. Absolutely, and the production techniques too. Honestly though, I sometimes miss the raw energy of a DIY recording. Me too, we used to get all excited about even the smallest improvement in our sound. Or the biggest drama over the placement of the mic for bass. Haha, I still remember when one mic stand fell down the entire time. Yeah, weren’t we, like, 14? If only we had some solid advice back then. Well, and now you could give it! True. I was watching some online tutorials the other day, advanced vocal techniques and all. Cool, I might look those up. Yeah, they're pretty useful. Speaking of useful, have you still got the guitar you got for Christmas four years ago? No, I sold it when I decided to focus more on my studies. It still sits well though. I remember when you were just obsessed with that guitar. I was, I used to play that thing... I don't know, every hour of the day. Like when we’d have impromptu jam sessions and then someone would walk in on us playing "Stairway to Heaven" with just youthful passion and no clue.

Yo, you hear about that new dinosaur exhibition at the science museum's opening soon? Yeah, super cool! I was thinking of going after our exam week. It's the first time they've got a live exhibit here. A live exhibit, wow! That sounds really educational – do you have to book? Apparently it's ticketed and you need to pre-book online but my history teacher says they're offering some free slots for students, as long as we bring our ID. That's even better! You know what's not educational though? This food at school. They always serve the same thing. Like, ever heard of variety? Haha, you have a point there. I was just looking at online recipes to try to make something for myself. Want to join in a cooking session over the break? I can bring the ingredients and you bring the idea. That's a great idea, let's plan it before we head home. What do you both want to make? Something vegetarian. I'm thinking this black bean burger recipe I found online looks good. But I'll admit, sometimes it's hard to stick to this diet, especially when we're out. Me too. It's pretty hard to find good vegetarian options in Slough. But I actually got so into learning about it at school. We're doing an EPQ [extended project qualification] on sustainable farming and vegetarianism. It's really opened my eyes to food production and its impact. That sounds really interesting! Did you know about all the food waste in our society? It’s a real issue. Yeah, it doesn’t even start to cover it. The project is making me want to do more – maybe even consider a career in that field, or at least volunteer in some capacity. That’s really commendable, doing something real, you know, besides just exams and stuff. You ever think about volunteering or something? Yeah, next summer, I’m hoping to join a group that works on humanitarian projects. You know, help out in some of these poorer communities or even abroad. That’s amazing! I’ve also seen ads about charity work in Montenegro, something about working with children. I might look into that over the summer if uni doesn’t get too intense. Euu, could you imagine? Living and working in another country, just for the experience... I’m trying to figure out what I want to do after uni.

Ugh I can't believe how much I'm spending on groceries. I thought I would save money by cooking more at home, but clearly I was wrong. Yeah, unreal! I mean, I'm here at uni and I'm almost broke because of this. Just this week, I've spent £40 on food! You should see how much I spent last weekend on takeaways. Guys, we need to set a cap for how much we spend on food each week. This is ridiculous. That's a good idea, actually. Like, we could have a rough budget of £20 each and then split any extras. Might just work. But even then, what about when we want to buy something nice from Waitrose or when we have a pizza night? Pizza night is every other week, so it's already part of our plan. Waitrose sometimes, but let's not make that a weekly thing, okay guys? Agreed. Plus, it’s not just the shopping, it’s also the rent. £520 a month this is nuts. Totally nuts. I mean, I'm counting every penny now just to save for the summer break. Me too. I'm trying to also work part-time but finding time between lectures is tough. I know what you mean. I started tutoring but it’s a lot in itself, trying to balance studies and work life. I should help with the budgeting. I saw a great app doesn’t come with ads. That’s perfect. Thanks for looking into it. We should also prep meals together sometimes. You know, one of us cooks together, we all just bring £10 each and we have a meal that way? That’s solid. Saves money and it's also fun. I’m actually changing the subject. Did you guys see that Facebook post Rohan from first year posted? What’s up with Rohan now? Apparently, his family is planning a lavish trip to Paris this summer! Can you believe that? They’re not even that well off. That’s almost upsetting. I mean, all the uni job I’m trying to snag and I’ll be lucky if I can afford to go to Manchester for a night. I’ve told you guys before Rohan acts like he’s got a trust fund. We all know his dad works for some pretty big corporation. Maybe there’s a company trip involved?

So, I hear you've seen some of the family friends from Cardiff while you were back. How'd it go? Oh, they've been lovely, as always! We caught up well over tea and cake. There was quite a bit to talk about because they've recently gone through a bit of a change. Oh, what do you mean? You'd mentioned they were considering some big lifestyle shifts a while back. Yes, actually, they've moved out of Cardiff to the countryside and set up their own organic farm! It's quite a big venture. They've always been interested in sustainable living but I wasn't expecting them to take the plunge like this. That's really big news! I can't imagine just up and moving to start a farm. Must be rewarding, though, but also a lot of hard work. Definitely. They seem very happy with the decision so far. It's been a big adjustment for them, but they're very determined. And how's the travel been going for you? You were talking about visiting different places for work and training as well. Oh, it's quite varied. Just last month, I was training a group in Manchester, which was fun. The city is always bustling with energy. Speaking of Manchester, have you noticed there's been a bit of a revival in local culture there? I've been reading about all the new independent coffee shops and arts projects, it feels like the city is really in a positive phase. Oh, absolutely, and it shows. And with the working environment, I've been doing quite a bit of remote work, which has actually given me the opportunity to travel more for leisure. That’s really great. I've been wanting to plan more trips myself. More travel for work would be a bonus too, if I'm being honest. If you're considering it, there are definitely some TEFL opportunities abroad that could offer both travel and work. While you're dealing with the business side of things, I was also reminded of how different the Christmas season feels out of the country. Yes, I know what you mean. I've experienced Christmas in different cultures while abroad, and it's fascinating how traditions vary so much. It's one aspect of traveling I really enjoy – experiencing cultural holidays firsthand. But I've also been trying to capture those moments with some photography lately.

Oh, Dad, it's so good to see you again. I still can't believe it's been two years since we last met. I know, lad. It's been quite a while isn't it? Sorry I couldn't visit more regularly, but you know questions at work kind of piled up. Don't apologise, Dad. I understand. Anyway, how have you been? Everything alright? I'd say alright. Life goes on. The company's got a new boss now, and they're always tweaking things, so it's keeping busy, you know. That's good. I was going through some old photos last week and stumbled upon that old family photo from when we went to Tanzania. Do you remember that trip? Oh, yeah! Of course, that was fun. Good times. You were a kid, so it must have been more exciting for you, but it was also a good experience for me. We met some amazing people, saw some incredible sights... Yeah, I remember the village we visited and the orphans. They were so cute and curious about everything. You and Mum were so patient with them, even if they did give you a pretty hard time sometimes. They certainly tested our patience, but it was worth it. It also made me think a lot about what life could be like without so many of the comforts we take for granted here. Speaking of life here... have you noticed any changes in Bedford since you left? I moved here, and it feels like there's a lot more speed cameras now. Plus, doesn't your road still have that hellish roundabout? The roundabout? Oh, dear, that hasn't changed one bit. And yeah, speed cameras. Seems like the government's got a bit too much dependence on cameras for revenue rather than improving public transport or road safety. Agreed. But have you heard anything about new developments or housing projects around you? Yeah, they're building on that field down by the recreation ground. I think it's more housing. The area's changed a lot since you moved out and I moved back. More families, fewer pensioners, it seems. That's a shame. We're losing some of the character. Did you hear about Mr. Jackson's gone? The café just won't be the same without him. No, I hadn't heard. I liked Mr. Jackson.

So, how was your day? It's been alright. Got through most of the lecture slides and marked some papers. The students seem to be finding the Milton stuff quite challenging, but I've planned a few activities to make it more accessible. That sounds good. I had a productive day too. I finally got to meet with the new publishing team and got a better understanding of their marketing strategies. What did you think of them? They seem enthusiastic and knowledgeable. The marketing manager even mentioned how they could get our new book onto the local radio station. That's great. I've always thought your research could really benefit from more public exposure. Yes, that’s true. While we’re talking about work, did we decide on the places for grocery shopping this week? Ah yes, right. I made a list on the fridge, but I do need to check if we have all the ingredients for the recipe you mentioned the other day? Yes, I was thinking of making that roasted chicken with quinoa salad. We should probably check the supermarket down the street. I heard they have good sales this week. Alright, I’ll go this evening then. I also wanted to pick up some new music. Any recommendations? Do you listen to [Artist]? I’ve heard great things about his new album. But if you want something new, perhaps look into [Band]. They’ve received great reviews lately. Thanks, I’ll check those out. You know, I also saw that the local community center is showing that live music event this Friday. It’s [Local Musician]. Would you be interested in going? That sounds lovely. I haven’t caught much live music lately. Shall I just check the times and purchase tickets? Yeah, do that. It’ll be nice to do something different together. Definitely. While you’re dealing with the music and that, I’ll prepare the guest room for your visiting aunt. Good thinking. Let me know if you need any help with that. Alright, I think we’ve covered most of the plans for the evening and week ahead. Yep, and we still need to figure out the kids’ Halloween costumes and party. True. That’s still a few weeks away but I can start looking into some ideas now. Great, thanks for volunteering to help with that. Happy to. So, what’s for dinner?

I've decided I need a new shower curtain. Our old one is so faded and boring. Well, haven't talked about that before. What are you thinking? Are you still into plaid? No, this time, maybe a bold pattern or something nautical. It kind of matches the theme of the bathroom I've got going on. Ah, I see where you're going with that. Now, you’re getting creative. Yeah, well, when you start redecorating one room, you kind of want it to tie in with the next. I’m glad you're getting into interior design. It's actually really enjoyable when you mix it up - like making the bean bag that cushion. Remember that? Sure, I recall you knitting a bean bag. It didn’t look very user-friendly, but I guess it was functional? It wasn't so much user-friendly as it was a bit or a lot too snug. I'm thinking this time it should maybe have some give, or use a softer material. Or maybe the knitting is just fun but not practical for every project. It was quirky. I liked it, though. It kind of looked like it had been knitted by your grandmother, nice and chunky. Maybe I could try combining knitting for the pattern and another material for the comfort and ease of use. I like where this is going. So, is the plan now to refurbish the whole bathroom or just the shower curtain? A bit of both, perhaps? The whole togetherness thing. Plus, the bathroom could use a bit of brightening up since we've been living here for a couple of years now. Well, it's great you're feeling inspired. You know, it's funny how we never really tackled the bathroom decor. We just sort of... lived with what was there when we moved in. That’s so typical, isn’t it? You move in somewhere new, and there's always a project list for the house. And we usually just focus on the essentials. But I’m all for making our living space, you know, livable. Speaking of which, does that meat smell right to you? Smells great. Just the right amount of herb. Remember to check if the potatoes are done in about 10 minutes? Already have them timed. Speaking of timed, we should keep this conversation at a good pace so dinner’s ready by the time we sit down.

Ah, I was just going over some of these letters we got. We have some from today. Oh, which ones did you open up? Well, various organizations but I need to decide what's indispensable to handle first. You know how it is. Yeah, it’s always something or other demanding attention. That’s true, it’s socialism in action, isn’t it? Erm, now that you mention it. But even so, it’s mostly just bureaucracy. Bureaucracy, indeed. Like when we started getting these letters about paying for the NHS. Does anyone actually have any say in how our money is being used? Not really, it’s all set from above. But that’s another matter. What I’m trying to decide is which ones to tackle first. It might be easier if we made a list and then divided tasks. Good idea. You’re always practical. I’ll put what I’ve got down. Now, let me see this pile. Alright. I think most urgent would be the ones with the deadlines first. Indeed. Especially if we’re to make sure we can claim certain benefits or avoid penalties or extra costs. Like that letter from the pension service, it sounded rather serious about making sure we’re up to date for our national insurance contributions. Yes, and that’s always a can of worms. But it’s not just about the paperwork now, it’s about making the most of what we have. Absolutely. Though sometimes it feels the government's more interested in making a list than actually helping. On that note, did either of you see this couple on the news? They were featured for making do with what little they have but still finding joy in life. You mean they’re still struggling but finding ways to be content? Exactly. I found it rather inspiring, actually. It’s all about attitude isn’t it? The world can be quite bleak if you let it overwhelm you. There’s truth to that. We could all do with being a bit more grateful, I reckon. Definitely. And maybe our thinking about this paperwork will be different if we keep that in mind. Good point. It’s not just about the letter itself but what it can lead to or represent: a better situation, better security, or a bit of peace of mind. Let’s focus on that then.

So, I thought we could plan out our Christmas shopping first. We've got Grace's birthday coming up too, right before December. Right, and then there’s the family gatherings and of course, the traditional Boxing Day meal with your family isn't it? Yeah, and let’s not forget grandma’s traditional gingerbread isn’t possible without her special ingredient, the dark molasses from that specific shop in Rochester that only opens pre-Christmas. Absolutely, we can’t miss that. Oh, and have you heard how they’re doing with the crowds in town? I’m thinking of avoiding the high street, if possible. Yeah, I've been avoiding it as much as I can. But did you hear that the new online marketplace is having a dedicated health and wellness section? Maybe we can get some healthier options delivered. That’s a great idea! It’s less hassle and probably saves a bit too. Speaking of creative solutions, have you heard of those meal box subscriptions that pair food with recipes from around the world? Maybe we could try one of those as a fun Christmas or new year’s dinner. Oh, that sounds fun! I've wanted to try something like that. We could even use some of those ideas for our family gathering. That could be really interactive. We can even make it into a bit of a cultural exchange kind of evening. Everyone brings a dish or drink from a different culture and shares why it’s special. And for the family in Rochester, maybe we can pick up some of those special spices they always use. That would add a nice touch. Yeah, definitely. Okay, so the plan is Christmas shopping, meal box experiment for the family dinner, and including some of those special family recipes or ingredients in our gatherings. Sounds like a plan. Shall I just start by making a list of all the ingredients we need for our meal box and who wants to join in? Count me in! And I can ask mom to include some of her classic Kentish Xmas fare. That’s a great idea. We’ll make sure there’s something for everyone. And while we're planning, did anyone want to make a plan for a quick trip over spring? Somewhere warm would be nice. Or perhaps a quick weekend to visit some of the new art exhibitions coming up.

So, I hear you've seen some of the more…interesting things during your time here in Northern Cyprus? Oh yes. Well, let me tell you, it's a different kind of life here. Not always easy, but it has its surprises. Like, the other day, I was walking in the Kyrenia mountains and I saw this flock of sheep led by a group of goats. I've never seen anything like it before. Really? That's quite unique. I've been here for a few months now, but even I've been surprised by the local customs. Last week, for instance, I was invited to a family dinner and they seemed quite keen on engaging in some old verbal sparring matches I wasn't prepared for. Ah, yes. Those Cypriot debates can be quite... spirited. But the food's usually excellent, isn't it? Excellently generous, you mean. They keep piling plates on the table, and by the end, you feel like you've done a bit of a physical training session just by eating. And their hospitality! I once took a wrong turn in the old town of Famagusta on my bike, got completely lost, and ended up at this old man's house. He invited me for tea, while he sent his grandkids to find me directions. It was the kind of kindness that reminded me why I moved here after all. That's amazing. Do you know, I had a similar experience visiting the Bellapais Monastery. I was there early, really enjoying the solitude, when this young local, couldn't have been more than 16, approached me and started explaining the history of the place, it was like I had the best tour guide ever. You're lucky. Some days can be tough, especially when the bureaucracy or less-than-ideal infrastructure get frustrating. But there's beauty in the simplicity of life here. I've learned to appreciate the slower pace, despite my impatience at times. Absolutely. I've been trying to slow down myself, but changing habits is tough. Do you find that the isolation affects people here? Like, I've noticed there are fewer support networks for outsiders like us. Well, it can be isolating, yes. But over time, you find your community. There's a group of expats, and even locals, who gather for coffee and such once in a while. It's informal, but it's a start.

Ah, I'm so glad we decided to walk home instead today. The pollution is really bad around here. Yeah, talked about that with the department last week. It's been getting worse over the years. Specially around the factories and the construction sites. It's just so disheartening sometimes. I mean, we lecture about sustainability and environmental science but out here it feels like we're just talking to ourselves. I know. It's always that weird contradiction between theory and practice, isn't it? And, you know, there's this new project our university's planning with the local government. It's supposed to be about reducing carbon footprint through community engagement. But even then, among the students, there's still a lot of skepticism. What's that about? Don't they see the urgency? I think it's a mix of things. Some are just too disengaged, others feel like their individual actions won't make a difference. And then there's the financial constraints for many of them - relying on what or whenever their parents can afford. So, for this project, we have to start very small. I understand the sentiment. When I was doing my research, I talked to youths in certain urban areas in the UK, and the pollution and climate change were the last things on their mind. Issues of rent, food security, vocational training are much more pressing for them. Exactly. There's this hierarchy of needs, right? You have to start from where they’re at, and somehow connect those immediate concerns to the bigger environmental picture. But it's hard to find the right frame for that. I've been thinking about using local examples, things that would directly benefit them or their family. But the problem is less about convincing the young people and more about convincing the policy makers, isn't it? Exactly. Which is why we need this project to move beyond raising awareness. We have to show concrete benefits. From improved air quality to lower healthcare costs. It’s a step-by-step process, though. First, we need some influence with the local government for actual policy changes and then we can trumpet real, tangible benefits so the population at large can see the worth of sustainable practices. And then we’ll have to educate the educators themselves. Change has to happen at all levels. You know what else I realised?

Oh, did I just type that or's that you Grace? Oh, that's you. You got the voice command to write the recipe now? Yep! I just got so immersed in making the batter. Ah, what's this... voice-activated confectionery? I thought we were just going to set up for dinner. Well, I was just seeing if voice commands would help me assemble this crumble recipe. Seems like your smart fridge is just trying to upstage you. It's almost like we're on a cooking show. Voice command batteries activated! So, are we on? What do we have in the kitchen already? We've got those honeycrisp or as I like to say, Yorkshire beauties. And if anyone needs anything from the store, just tell me and I can stop on the way home. Good idea, we do need some golden syrup for the topping. And brown sugar, perhaps some mixed spice, and flaky pastry isn't in there, right? Got brown sugar, but no flaky pastry. How about we use puff pastry instead? That'd be tasty. And what time's lunch planning? We've got about an hour before we should start prepping for lunch. Oh right, before we dive deep into this, what do you all want for lunch? I was thinking maybe a cold platter of leftovers from last night. That works for me. Anything Grace? Maybe some wraps or a salad if there's any leftover chicken from the roast. Good job I put those into the fridge. I can just nuke some and add to the platter. How about company updates while we cook? I know that department meeting tomorrow is going to be... interesting... Don't get me started. How about we watch a show tonight while we eat dinner? Which one? You've been on a 'Heartstopper' streak lately. Yeah, but why not mix it up a bit? Thought maybe 'The Crown' season 5 came out this week? Really? I didn't catch that. It did. But between you, me, and the cabinet, I think 'The Crown' requires more concentration. Not great for multitasking like cooking. Good point. Let's finish up the crumble, then we can decide. I can just listen to 'The Crown' while you two talk about work. Fair deal? Well, as long as you promise to keep up. Whoops almost forgot! It looks perfect, Sarah. Thanks!

So, I hear there's a new bus route coming in from's supposed to connect our house to the train station. Yeah, I saw the announcement. Makes life easier for commuters, but I'm curious how they plan to time it so it doesn't clash with the existing routes too much. Exactly. You hear a lot about traffic congestion and delays, but I've noticed the city's done a decent job of optimizing things, right? Definitely. I mean, Cambridge's always been good at that, especially alongside all the tech startups and bus companies competing for routes. Right, and they're always passing along the colleges and through town, which is nice. Yeah, and you get to see all the hustle bustle of uni life every day - though maybe not so much during this time of year. Exactly! It's always buzzing, especially around terms. Speaking of which, have you been in the Cambridge University Press bookshop lately? They've got a few new titles in science or arts, whatever field. Oh, actually, yes! I've been meaning to pop in. I found a book on innovative pedagogy that I assumed would be on the must-read list. Did it have anything to say about online learning? I mean, given recent sentiments... It did. The author explores how to integrate technology effectively, especially during times of uncertainty or restrictions in class sizes, really interesting. I'm glad they're addressing it. Technology can't replace good human interaction, but it sure helps. True, but I think the author emphasizes finding the balance, using tech to enhance engagement and accessibility rather than replace face-to-face learning. Makes sense. Have you seen the students protesting recently? Yes, over another climate change issue, right? It’s always something. It's great they’re passionate, but sometimes I worry if their message is getting lost in all the activism. I understand that feeling. But for many of them, it’s not just about the issue - it’s about feeling heard, especially if they see universities as being part of the problem. True, the universities themselves often aren’t very transparent about their carbon footprint or sustainability efforts. Yeah, and I heard Cambridge has actually been working with the city to reduce its carbon emissions. But yeah, still needs improvement, especially with the pressure from all these large industries and big tech firms that are often tied to academia.

Oh, Mary, remember when you used to make that shepherd's pie? The children just loved it. Oh, yes! It was the real deal. Made with love. Indeed. She used to make the best shepherd’s pie – hearty and comforting. I miss cooking like that. It used to take the edge off a tough day at the school. Speaking of which, have you keeps coming across any job opportunities or courses that might interest you? Not really. It's all just transcription these days, you know. And the pay isn’t great, to be honest. And the places can be quite far from here. You need a car to commute properly. Yes, the transport here is not the best, especially if you didn’t drive. But maybe it’s just me not looking hard enough. Well, there might be something coming up soon. A friend of mine mentioned that a company is looking for online educators – they need people who can create math tutorials for kids. That actually sounds like fun. I loved teaching and explaining things to people. That's wonderful to hear, Susan. It'd be great to see you take it up. It'd be a shame to waste all that expertise. I'm not sure if I’d be any good at it, though. It’s been a while. Well, you have the degree and the experience. Plus, online platforms make it easier to start slowly. You could start by just offering some free beginner classes and see how it goes. She can always reach out to them for an informal interview or chat. Sometimes, getting a feel for it first really helps. You’re right. I could do that. Speaking of kids, Abigail is saying she’s tired of salads at school. How do you manage with such picky eaters? You know, most children go through phases. Just keep offering variety and almost always there’s something they’ll happily eat. Ah, yes, offering. It seems half the battle is getting them to try new things. But, food aside, have you all seen those new series for kids on Netflix? I heard Abbey’s really into that new... Oh yes! The latest Marvel series, isn’t it? Yes, that's the one! Maybe she can get her father to sit with her and watch it this weekend. Brilliant idea. Quality bonding time over good content. And quality educational content if we’re lucky!

I keep reading that if you've got any passport apart from your British one; it's like super valuable to have and clearly nobody cares when you're using it for anything particularly practical. Right! Exactly! I mean it just comes into play when you need to get out of questions at some kind of border control isn't it? I mean, what's the point of having "citizen of the world" written on your birth certificate if actually, as soon as I pick up that ticket to wherever it is. Right, let me pull out my multiple passports and try to escape to a hypothetical alternative world – that's about it, isn't it? I used it only once when I had to pick up something online from a US store and was stuck in the question of weighted versus volume when following recipes. Ah, the infamous cup measurements. I never seem to remember which is the other. It's just... how do you get through life when measuring cups are your only means of travel and baking success? I've just resigned myself to living in a world that accepts that a cup is a cup and it might be imperial or metric depending on who wrote the recipe. I just assumed the rest of the world would also just 'get along'. Speaking of the rest of the world - we can't even do that properly with or without technology. Look at all these fancy landmarks we're walking past. Woolwich old docks, and the Thames really is so calm today considering we’re about to get all thrown about by the 'informal' O2 Arena plans. But it proves the point - the world has so many systems, so many conflicting measures, and yet somehow, we're here strolling along the Thames, enjoying the day side by side, without needing to figure out just what the hell a "cup" is supposed to be in relation to volume or mass. It's quite philosophical, really. There's a lesson in here somewhere about accepting changing measures and embracing that not everything needs to be standardized or scaled or… measured. Exactly! I mean, people used to travel by horseback or on foot without needing to specify so much about distances or how long things would take because they just did it. And now we have these precise navigation systems almost anticipating our every move and guess what?

Mum, I can't believe how much it's raining today. We have to make sure the kids' outdoor swimming lessons aren't cancelled at school again. Oh, don't worry, Lucy. These grey skies can clear up really quickly around here. Especially now that the kids are all excited about sports day on Friday. The little one was arguing with her toys, saying they needed a "baking show" too.

So, I was thinking that we might want to recommit ourselves to personal development goals this year. Considering how busy we were last year, and how slumped we've been lately, wouldn't it make sense to set some new goals and work towards them together? That sounds like a great idea! But let's face it, we haven't been so bad about personal development. But, definitely need to refocus and make them a priority. What makes you think we've slumped, actually? Well, your point about feeling stagnant is valid—I have thought about exploring more leadership roles within education or even looking into creative writing therapy programs. How about you, any big ideas on where you want to focus in your entrepreneurial life? I've been considering joining a business incubator program in our area. We could meet with other entrepreneurs, get some mentorship, and maybe even find new ventures or partnerships. Plus, it'll force me to focus on growing beyond my comfort zone. Also, think we should set aside a specific amount of time each week for us, no matter what. Friday evenings, maybe? Just to review progress or just relax together. That sounds good.
