Okay, so we have goals and we have a time commitment to holding ourselves and each other to account. Any other ideas? As for career stuff, I just had this thought: what if I started leading more project-based learning initiatives in my school? It feels like it's time to think about moving into more of a leadership role while still being in the classroom and it could be really rewarding. Definitely aligns with my own leadership goals in business—working with others, leading teams. It’s a good skill set to keep honing. On a different note, what about our friendship group back in the UK?

Yo, anyone got a pint? Yeah's all right mate, spare a quid? I got it this time, enjoy your ale. Cheers, you're a lifesaver. Did anyone see this new episode of Pokémon? That questions are some kind of new skill isn't it? I mean, what's the point of a "Pokequestion" that makes you pause and think... right in the middle of a battle? It's so out of character, right? I mean, would Ash randomly start philosophising mid-battle? Exactly! Like, "Pikachu, is it right to attack something just because it appears on your screen?" I mean, is this preparation for the eventuality of Ash becoming president or something? And the accents, oh god. They have this one trainer with a posh accent, makes me cringe. I know what you mean, there's barely any regional voices. And when there are it's often caricatured, or whatever the English equivalent is. Like, why? I mean this is a global show, you'd think they'd celebrate their diversity of accents more. Yeah and then we have the 'diversity' they show us; it often feels like a checklist more than anything else. Well, technology-wise though, I'm actually quite impressed. The augmented reality stuff they're dipping their toes into is actually pretty cool. True, it's actually quite well done. But what's with Smoking? Like, why is that still a thing in this world? [Laughs] Just last weekend our friend, Sarah, went all out and smoked like it was the 90s. I mean, was she reviving an old habit or was she trying to look tough for the night? [Laughs] Oh God, Sarah’s always up for a confrontational moment and she really took to it! I mean, the smoke and everything. We all just watched her like, "What are you doing?" I'm sure she thought it added to her aura. Either way, it made for a pretty funny story later at the pub. Speaking of funny stories, did you hear about [Speaker_5]'s little adventure at Leeds this week? He tried to order coffee at Costa and ended up with complete and utter gibberish. [Laughs] Oh god, yeah. I wanted a mocha but I just ended up with something that tasted like burnt flowers. How did... I mean, any word recognition issue? No, it was just me being slow. I took like five minutes to get the words out.

Right, so I had a bit of an incident at the station's bakery today. What happened? Oh, talked to this rather charming fella down there. He was all into some ridiculous sports fad. I've now got the feeling, though, that I might have questions his status as a "rabid" fan or whatever he'd have you believe. Ah, sports fanatics of Norwich, never change. Sounds like it was an interesting conversation even if it wasn’t exactly on topic. What sport was he going on about? It was one of those new MMA hybrid things. Idk, dear, I just came out saying I did boxing when I was younger and he thought he could take me. Oh god, old man dusting off his gloves again. On the topic of Norwich, have you all seen this new café downtown? It's supposedly very trendy, serves ethically sourced food and such. I'd love to check it out sometime. I heard they have some amazing vegan options. Oh, on that note, I've been meaning to try out different vegan recipes with the kids. Where did you get that great vegan cheese alternative recipe? It was actually from a friend who recommended it online. They have this wonderful blog with all sorts of recipes for families like us who want to try less meat-heavy meals. Good on you for suggesting that, really. Makes you think twice about the choices, doesn’t it? And with the "Eat Local First" policy we're aiming for in Norwich, it's fitting. Speaking of policy, did you hear about the new policy discussions in town about improving public transport? More plans and discussions, but little implementation, sadly. I do think our local MP is working on it though, but grassroots support is always helpful. Maybe we should write and show some interest? Yeah, and not just about transport. It’s time we voice our concerns over all these new shopping centers and what they're doing to small businesses. Absolutely, and so much focus on student areas over regeneration elsewhere. Speaking of regeneration, what’s the latest on those new housing developments? Anyone gone and seen them? I did catch a glimpse when out with little ones. They're talking about “affordable” housing but I saw prices that still seem quite out of reach for most families. True, that’s often the issue. “Affordable” is a term that gets thrown around without much substance behind it.

So, I was thinking about what you said to me last night. You know, about dropping out. It really got me thinking. Yeah, I talked to you about the whole unrealistic expectation pressure, right? Exactly. I feel like, even though I came in here knowing I wanted to study this subject, the workload and the constant comparison and competition, it’s making me feel a bit defeated. I can imagine. I felt a bit like that in sixth form too. Like sometimes I thought that if I wasn’t doing as well as others, then I must be failing or something. Exactly! Like, did your parents or anyone ever tell you stories about dropping out back in the day? Oh, my grandma did. She actually dropped out of university because she got pregnant. And you know, that was in the 1970s when that meant a lot more societal pressure and less support, especially if you didn’t have a partner. Really? That’s quite a story. It wasn’t so common, was it, back then? No, it wasn’t. But it wasn’t seen as the end of the world for her either. She went back to studying later in life and passed, while raising kids and working part-time. It’s more common now, but even so, there’s still a lot of stigma. Yeah, I know what you mean. People always look at you like, “Oh, why didn’t you just study harder?” Exactly. But, I mean, if you’re not enjoying it and you’re not doing it for yourself… I think that’s my problem. I’m doing this course because I thought I should, you know? Maybe I need to consider whether this is truly the right path for me. You always were a bit of a free spirit, weren’t you? Different from most people here. Maybe you’re just not meant for academia in the way it’s presented here. You think so? I mean, we did grow up in very different environments though, didn’t we? Your upbringing in Liverpool, mine in Falmouth. True, but I think the spirit remains the same. Like, do you remember when we used to come back from playing outside and have the dirtiest shoes? Oh, yes! I swear my mum used to want to kill me because I came back with the mud on everything. Exactly, and now look at us.

Ah, I can't believe we're finally catching up! It's been ages since we've seen each other. Too right! I've been meaning to get in touch for ages but work has just been absurdly busy. How's uni been treating you? Same old, same old. I'm actually kind of dreading graduations and all that jazz. Feels like the end of an era! But why dread it? You graduated, you did well, and now you're doing this project coordination keeps changing right? Yes, it's really interesting but some days, I fucking hate it. Like when they expect me to just appear in meetings having done all the work from scratch. But then, when I actually have to coordinate something, it’s really rewarding. You can see from start to finish. I suppose organization is a big part of what you do now, isn’t it? Yeah, it requires a very specific set of skills but when it all comes together, it feels great. Anyway, how’s uni life for you these days? You’ve presumably finished your business degree? I have, actually. Just started working for Pearson a few months back. Marketing is quite different from what I expected but I'm still figuring things out. Quite interesting seeing the academic world from the company side though. Interesting, huh? I used to think working for an educational provider would be really straightforward but I imagine even Pearson must have its complexities, especially with current tech integration and all. Oh, absolutely. For instance, trying to automate some of our services and working with AI to improve analysis... it doesn’t come without its hiccups. Still, the possibilities are incredible. Tech, huh? I don’t envy you having to deal with the future of education. I just try to worry about my projects a few months at a time. Same here. Though, we had this meet-up planned for ages, I’ve been meaning to ask, what are your plans for the future? You sure you’re going to stay in project co-ordination? Honestly, not completely sure. I do like it but sometimes I wonder what else is out there. And given the stress levels, if I’m being completely honest, It sounds good. Yeah, well, maybe not the best job for longevity or sanity. But for now, it pays the bills and it feels challenging in a good sense.

Right okay let's look on Amazon. I need some new stationery. What for? Well I've been marking exams this week and the pens are down to stubs. I can help you choose the right ones. You can get good deals but sometimes you never know what you’re getting. True, but if you know what you’re looking for, you can find some bargains. If you know to look for. Yeah, but let’s quickly search eBay too. Fine. Okay, pilot G2 pen 20 for £15.50. That's cheaper! But are they new? I suppose sometimes on eBay they are, but sometimes people sell used or refilled. Either way, it looks alright. And if you're going to use them for marking, the condition doesn't matter unless they're completely unusable. True. 20 A4 lined exercise books for £4. That’s a steal! Well, we need a couple of folders too. On eBay, 5 A4 folders with pockets for £2.50. That’s even better! So, overall, which one do you think? I reckon we should go with eBay. All these items are cheaper than on Amazon, and we need to buy quite a few. Okay, let me add them to the cart now. I’m just glad that after all these years of teaching, I still get some of my back-to-school shopping done through online shopping!

So, how was your week? It's been alright, but today's been a bit of a slog. The production numbers slumped again after the weekend, so I've been scrambling to get everything back on track. That sounds exhausting, the weekend’s always a kind of production nightmare, isn’t it? Yeah, something about people having more time to get into trouble or forgetting to restock. Anyway, I'm just glad the report meeting with management went smoothly. They're still set for their numbers so that's keeps everything steady. Good. You'll need it to stay steady, especially with the way things are – production stocks low, supply chain stuff, and all that. Totally, just trying to keep everything moving as best as possible. It's actually really good for me career-wise though - dealing with these challenges, it's showing them I can handle pressure and think on my feet. That's great for your career, but also how are you doing? These pressures? Uhm well it's tough, between the shift roster ever changing and whatnot, but it's manageable, I cope. Coping isn’t always the same as thriving, mind. You’re doing well though, I can tell. Thanks. It’s interesting, we were discussing the other day, us and the others in the sector, about how vocational training might equate to higher management roles perhaps? I’m thinking, why not? It seems a bit one-way sometimes, really - if you don’t come from the 'right' contexts, it feels like. That’s a socio-economic issue isn’t it? The way things are structured now, kind of holding some people behind, while others seem to skip yards based on who they know or the school they went to. More training for those in your role could level the playing field a bit. I noticed a lot of the production line folk skills are unrecognized or underappreciated. Exactly! They should see it as changing the business model not just hiring on pedigree. Change does come slow but it's also about cultivating new perspectives. I know a few from when I was working - so much talent overlooked because they didn't tick certain boxes. Right! And yet, vocational education right now, you can go all the way postgrad level just in vocational studies. There are all these pathways opening up. I was reading about that new program in London that aims to upskill adults wanting to change careers.

So, I was browsing on Flightradar24 last night and it looks like there are still some flights scheduled for Christmas day. Really? I wouldn't be surprised if they're all sold out already though. Yeah, considering this is a pretty big holiday for most people. Yeah, but some people might have to travel unexpectedly, so I guess there are still some options available. Do you remember that time when Sam got stranded in New York on Christmas Day? Oh yes, that was fun... or not fun, seeing his face on video call when he found out about the flight delay. Haha, poor guy. Speaking of travel, what about the food we're going to have for Christmas dinner? I've been thinking about trying out some new recipes. Maybe this year we should do a roast goose instead of turkey? Ooh, that sounds interesting. What inspired you to try that? Well, I saw a few exotic recipes online and thought it could be a fun change. Plus, this is a smaller gathering this year so it might work perfectly. I'm all for fun changes. Though, I hope we don't need to deal with roadkill deer at our doorstep to make it interesting. Oh, you're always giving horror stories about roadkill. It's not entirely silly considering where we live near the wildlife reserve. One time, we actually found a piece of deer on our lawn and. But it wasn't from Christmas dinner, hopefully! Don't worry, I think all our roadkill is mainly fox around here. Though less frequent, of course, they do make an appearance. Speaking of wildlife, do you remember when we tried to integrate environmentally friendly practices in our café? That was an adventure! We tried changing the straws and packaging, but making those changes stuck was a challenge. Yeah but it was worth it for the customer feedback and knowing we're trying to do our part. Though, I have to admit, we have a way to go still. This reminds me, are we planning on making any New Year's resolutions this year? Definitely. I'm thinking we should all try and reduce our single-use plastic even more. Good idea! I've been reading up on barista tricks to reduce waste behind the bar. Maybe I can inspire this year. I've been thinking about maybe picking up a healthier habit, like finally starting a regular exercise routine.

Yo, mate, did you hear about that new car that's almost entirely voice-controlled? Yeah, I saw a thing about it on social media. It's the future man! Is voice control really practical or just a gimmick, though? I think it's definitely starting to make a difference. But, and this might sound weird, part of me misses the feel of buttons and a physical interface. There's something satisfying about manually switching gears or pressing a button. You know what's odd? Back when I was a kid, everyone was talking about voice recognition being the next big thing – and here we are, with stuff like Siri, Google Assistant, and whatever your car is doing. Yeah, but the car thing, in particular, is interesting because driving can be distracting. Voice commands reduce that distraction. True, it makes sense in that context. But looking at it from a creative perspective, thinking about the kinds of games we make, voice recognition is still quite limited in terms of nuances. Sometimes it's hard to convey the exact tone or emotion you want. For me, that's a challenge. Totally see where you're coming from. For driving specifically though, it’s useful for hands-free phone calls and whatnot. But the tech has its flaws, hasn’t it? Absolutely, technology is rarely without its quirks. The car I had last year, for example, had this voice-activated system that sometimes misheard really basic commands. It was meant to help, but it often felt more hindrance than help. Yeah, that's a universal experience with voice tech, isn’t it? The issue of misinterpretation. I mean, in design or editing work, voice input could be great for initial ideas or drafts, but for final tweaks, I always find myself going back to a keyboard. Right, so it's complementary but not quite ready to fully replace traditional interfaces yet. Exactly. As editor, my job is often about refining language to convey specific emotions – and that’s hard for AI to replicate, for now. And as a game dev, I’m always on the lookout for new technologies to enhance player experience, but voice tech, like you said, is still pretty niche and almost feels like a novelty feature in most titles. I guess what we're really talking about is how voice tech still has a way to go. But, you know, I’ve been reading up on some company that’s using AI for voice tech that can almost perfectly mimic any accent.

Yo, you hear that new album from James Blunt?? It's sick. Dude, I haven't checked it out yet, but talked to someone who said it was pretty good. Is it better than his previous ones though? I think so man, his voice kind of got better with years and stays pretty consistent. I heard some tracks that have some real interesting minimalist beats actually, quite fractal I'd say. You're putting a physics spin on it already, Liam! True, true. Idk, I feel like with this one he's getting more experimental. Might just like it because of his voice. You can't beat that voice though, can you? Definitely. But what about you guys want to watch The Matrix one day soon? That would be awesome. Haven't seen it in ages. Seconded. It's like, for all the older folks, it was or still is like one of the best sci-fi movies. Totally. Though, I was reading this article the other day. It was kind of explaining the physics behind 'glitching' like in the movie. It was interesting, they were discussing the plausible factors contributing to such phenomena, even in today's technology. Like, what? I thought that was all just 'movie magic.' Yeah, but they were considering parallel universes, and all that. And stuff like "quantum entanglement leading to anomalies." Well, it's the same kind of principle as the 'simulation hypothesis,' but applied on a more localized or structured scale. But the article was less into that and More into "What would it take to create, say, a stable digital wormhole?" A stable digital wormhole? That’s wild. That’s what I’m talking about - the movie takes that concept and just blows it out of proportion. Exactly. But some of the theoretical discussions these days, like what's currently in quantum computing theory, isn't so far-fetched anymore. Like the concepts of erasure coding and entanglement for data storage could perhaps lead to more secure data transfer over vast distances... You're getting into advanced stuff. I was reading about that stuff in a physics book for fun. Dude, your head must just be bursting with all this stuff. I'm here for the music and movies. Though that's...kind of cool anyways. It's just, you know, if we're gonna enjoy the Matrix or Star Wars and all that, it's kinda fun to see where real science ends and movie magic begins.

So, how was your class today? I heard you've started Balanceability. Oh, it was really fun! We got to ride these balance bikes and practice balancing. I had some trouble but I'm getting better! Yeah, and Mrs. Lee said we'll be assessed on this soon. I don't really like tests but maybe it'll be okay this time. Well, balance is important right? In many areas of life, not just riding bicycles. Yeah, I guess it is. And in homeschooling too, we have to balance studies with fun activities. Exactly, and I heard that Max's new house is being renovated near the pool. Does he have a pool? Well, from what I heard, the backyard has a pool and even a waterfall. It sounds wonderful. But you guys should never, ever dive into unfamiliar water without looking. Why not? What's wrong with that? It's very dangerous. You can't see what's underneath or even how deep the water is. You can really hurt yourself. Oh, that makes sense. So, shallow is just fun, but deep can be scary? Exactly. And speaking of water, I also learned today that in Japan, they have a special day to celebrate cats – like a national cat day. Fascinating, right? That's so cool! I love cats. But what about food? What are some good combos you love? I like pizza with ham and pineapple! Really?! Pineapple? Absolutely! It’s sweet and savory at the same time. I see what you mean. The right mix of flavors can be quite delightful indeed. Different strokes for different folks, as they say. Speaker_2 and [laugh together] We could try some unique combos at home sometime, though maybe not on the same pizza for everyone. Like what? Well, have you ever heard of a honey mustard grilled chicken with a side of blueberries and walnuts? It's surprisingly good. Wow, that sounds interesting! We should try that sometime if you're up for it. Definitely! Let's add it to our list of things to do. Also, speaking of lists... we should start making our Christmas lists soon. Okay, I want a new drawing book and maybe a cat toy. And I’d like a new puzzle and some more colored pencils. Great choices! I've already thought about getting everyone a fun book for Christmas, something that interests each of you, like a science book for you, Speaker_3, a classic novel for Speaker_2, and probably something educational about baking or history for you, Speaker_1.

So, I've been going to the gym like four times a week now. I'm really trying to get more active and eat healthier. Ah, that's great, really well done! Are you feeling any difference already? Actually, yeah! I've lost a few pounds and I'm sleeping better. It's amazing how a bit of exercise and a balanced diet can make a difference. Definitely! I'm right there with you. It's supposed to be really helpful in reducing stress. Yeah, I've tried that a bit. It can be a bit tricky to get into the habit, but once you do, it's wonderful. It's amazing how much difference it makes being more aware of your thoughts and feelings. Absolutely. It's crazy how similar our approaches are. Yeah, I've cut back on processed food and try to cook as much as I can. It's actually kind of enjoyable. Well, most of the time at least! Aha, right, it's good to have a hobby in cooking, isn’t it? I never thought I'd say that but all those nights of cooking and working out have taken up a lot of free time. True, but the upside is you kind of see food and exercise as like part of your hobby now, or just your lifestyle? Exactly! I try to make it a part of my daily routine rather than a chore. On that note, have you dealt with anything interesting at work recently? Oh, well, we're actually planning a big conference in a month. It's going to be our biggest event yet. It does take a lot of work but it's worth it in the end. I've had to deal with everything from booking the venue to arranging catering and now the last details.

Alright so I heard you've been doing these Domino drives with your mates every week. How's that going and which pizza do you like the most? Oh yeah! It's been great fun. We all chip in, pick a pizza – usually something like a meat feast or a chicken bad boy and then we make a group order. But the one I like the most is probably the Hearty Meaty, it's got loads of different meats and vegetables. keeps you fuller for longer. Yeah, but Domino's is easier for us to order together on the app. And now we can't do takeaways as much because of the virus and stuff. Sure, I can imagine. So, on that note, have you thought about this year's Easter and maybe doing something together as a family instead of different plans? Like what? We usually just have the chocolate eggs and a family meal, that's it. Well, what about making it bigger this year? Maybe a big barbecue or take everyone to the park, see if we can have a family-friendly event that all of you enjoy. That’s a good idea. I don’t think anyone would say no to that. And since you're the one that usually does the grilling and the picnic, we could do all that if the weather permits. Seems like a good plan! We need to agree on one thing first… do we all like the idea of having some family time together in a new way? Yeah! That sounds fun. And maybe later we can all go for a haircut together? You know how funny it was when we all agreed to the same hairstyle once? Oh yeah, the time I and uncle Simon, and your dad came back with the same mullet. Well, Simon liked it more.

Oh, did I mention my first trip's passport was covered in veggie stains? I talked to someone recently and she was like "I love your blog, you've really understood our tastes." She just assumed the writer was a woman, though! So questions were like "What’s it like being a housewife and cooking all the time?" I'm pretty sure those actually came from my... never mind, let's just say it was my mother! Speaking of mothers, did you hear about that celebrity chefs' new vegan cookbook? No! I wasn’t even aware they had shifted to veganism. It’s a little surprising, but apparently the whole making vegan meals that are fun and easy has been a challenge for them, so it’ll be interesting to see their take. I barely have time to check food blogs. You ever try this black beer vegetable stew? No, sounds new? I’m more of a stick to the basics person, pasta and all. The basics sometimes can surprise the most, though. You know in the Midlands, at least where I'm from, the local pubs serve like the best basic fish and chips, but it's like a whole different level from what you'd expect. Yeah, really good point. The key is the batter, and they have this local secret ingredient that keeps it crisp even when served later. I can almost taste it. Reminds me of our trips to the pub on Fridays when I was in Cambridge. More like your trips to the pub! I was usually the designated driver since you'd never pass up a good couple of pints. Well, you know, you provided moral support. You can’t really go on a solo pub crawl as a postgrad, though maybe you could have? Either way, it always led to so much laughter later. I mean, we explored Cambridge so thoroughly except for that one infamous night. Oh, the folklore of the midnight walk back... We could write a whole saga from that night if we really wanted. Totally worth it though. The food, the late night company, the general university life – it was all so much more than just the work. Absolutely. Now, shall I make a tea? Yes, please. How about trying that new batch of tea leaves I got last week? Alright, let’s see how these new leaves hold up.

Right okay so I think it's time we figured out the rules of this articulate game. Am I right? Yes, let's clarify. It seems simple but the rules are quite specific. As usual, isn't it? People think board games are chill but then they read the questions and realise they need to have an answer and it's not as chill as they thought. And the rules can always come with a few... local twists. Are there any local twists for articulate? I don't think so, but we should probably clarify the basic rules for Player 5 here. Might just need the "baby" version for me. Alrighty then. So the basic rules. You draw a card and it'll have certain letters on it which you'll need to use to describe the word without actually saying the word or any part of the word. The others have to guess what the word is. Perfect. That's sounds a bit like a more complicated version of Hangman! Exactly. Sort of "reverse hangman" because you're trying to help the guessers. So no proper nouns, no parts of the word itself? Correct. If you say a part of the word or a synonym that clearly indicates, you're out. Can you repeat that for us, please? Sure. So you can't say "s doesn't come in that word" if the word is "snake" because you're pointing out the "s" in snake, which violates the rule. But you could say "it's the opposite of tall" for "short." Wow, sounds fun but tricky. Yes, it's a great game for building vocabulary and communication skills. Alright, ready to start? Before we do that, how are we going to handle the timer? I know some games have strict timed rounds. Normally, one minute is the standard for figuring out the word. However, as we're family and not competing, maybe let's just... As if I need an extra minute to figure out "sandal." I'll probably need it just to get "tea" right! Alright, no time limit. We're all here to enjoy ourselves. But first, um, if anyone here is better educated than the rest of us at using specific letters, maybe we should draw straws to see who goes first. No seriously, we should just take turns. But that would mean the first round is better prepared folks.

Right okay let's start this over. I will choose first, I've got these options today. Oh alright. Hopefully we don't get talked into another game of Bullshit. You know how long that one took yesterday? That was quite the event wasn’t it? I think we had about three different debates on whether a narrative was believable or not? I'm just glad the children didn't come in and hear us calling each other liars. That could've gone down as a family tradition. Okay, I'll pick. I've got Shedding Light here. What's the rules again? I seem to have forgotten. It's quite simple. You need to get rid of all your cards - "light" cards are worth 1 point, and "dark" cards are worth 10 points. You play a card, the next person needs to play a card that's either the same color, same number, or the same type . If they can't, they gain light/dark card depending on the card played. Got it. So I can play a 5 of lights on a 5 of anything? Or if someone plays a dark card, the next person has to play a dark card or gain the dark points? That's right. But if you have no option , you can "shed light" or "shed dark", which means you gain the points but doesn't give you the card. Actually, that mechanism reminds me of the "pass or play" rule in the game we played last week. More strategy than luck, really. Strategy is fun. Okay, I'll start. I'll play a 5 of light. Wait, if I play my dark 7 here, it's forcing you to play a dark or gain 7 dark points. But if I play a red 6 light, I might be helping you lighten your load. Either way, the aim is to not finish with any dark cards at the end of the round. We can all do math in our heads I hope? Alright then, your turn. You're on 6 now. And don't forget, if we get rid of all our cards, we lighten our points by what we gain here too. Remember, sometimes it pays to keep your light cards close, but if someone’s sitting on a bunch of darks… Right, so we can try to force each other into positions where we might have to shed or play something that lets us get rid of multiple cards at once.

So, I hear everyone is planning for university. Yeah, I've applied for five places. Two in London, and three up North. Oh wow, five? I'm only applying to three. I've already got into Engineering, but I'm thinking of doing questions for some kind of apprenticeship instead. Really? Like companies take on apprentices now? Yeah, there are some actually very good programs. I'd be earning while I learn. Which is tempting when you think how much university can cost. Totally. I hear some people are actually struggling a bit with the idea of student debt. I know, right? But then again, some of the online courses sound pretty cool. I'm looking into some part-time ones while I study. Yeah, I'm also going to have to work part-time most likely, so it’ll balance out. But you also get so much support in university. Like, academic help, mental health support. It's not all about money. True, and I hope I don't get too homesick. We're all from Frimley, so it's gonna be interesting if different parts of the country. I think it'll be good. Seeing new places, making new friends. Although, it sucks not being able to see the others as much. Ah, but we're gonna make sure to keep in touch, right? We'll have a group chat and all that. For sure. Although I'm also excited because my cousin is over in Sussex now. Maybe we can visit. True, and the train journey isn’t too bad. If you’re in London, you can easily visit or vice versa. Seems like the Morecambe & Wise Christmas Special just came on. Okay, fun fact. Did you know they actually did couple of specials before they were regulars? No way! That's interesting. Well, I'm not sure I'll be watching that. Although I suppose it's nice for a bit of light relaxation. Oh, definitely for light relaxation. But hey, has anyone else been cleared for Christmas shopping and all that? I've already got most of my shopping done. But I swear, those prices for presents are insane. Well, someone's got to help stimulate the economy, right? True that. Although, I heard Aunt Susan is making some homemade stuff this year. So maybe we can help out with presents that way if anyone needs it.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time I drove my Mini into the park? Oh, no, you must tell us all about it! A Mini into the park? That sounds like quite an event. Oh yes! I must have been about 25, going about a quarter mile per hour, but I hit a bump and... right into the bush it went. The neighbors had quite a laugh. Right into the bush. You okay? Oh, absolutely. It was a very slow crash. Idle, really. I just sat there for a bit thinking what just happened. So what happened next? You just got out and started again or...? Well, I gave it some gas and it just pulled out, bruised but unbroken. It was a fun car, that one. Let's just say it had its own little...personality. Yeah, I can imagine! I’m more of a walker or cyclist myself. Oh, good for you. I prefer driving myself. I love the freedom it gives. Though, in this part of town, it’s so much easier to walk or cycle. There’s always something to look at, you know? Like what? Oh, the architecture here is fantastic! And Cambridge’s really good with cycle paths. I used to cycle to work all the time when I worked over at... Oh, yes! I’ve been thinking of switching to cycling for work. Except, I worry about all the time it takes compared to driving. It definitely does take longer, but you save money, get exercise, and it’s so much fun! You get to see parts of the town you’ve never seen before. As long as you avoid the park like my mother did! Well, that’s not every day! But you’re right, I did make a bit of a mess of it that day. So, what do you think? Should I take the plunge and try cycling to work? Absolutely! Start with small journeys. If you like it, you can work your way up. We have fantastic cycling groups around here. And company. Someone to talk to on the way. Exactly! And it’s better any day to be outside than stuck in traffic. Though, I have to confess, I miss driving sometimes. How about trying a hybrid approach? Walk sometimes, cycle sometimes. That’s a good idea. Depending on your day, energy levels, or suit! Yeah, and as someone who’s retired I’d say, taking a different route every day, seeing new things, it’s a lovely pastime.

Good afternoon, I'm Cassie from Aylesbury. Nice to meet you. Hi, I'm Rachel from Lincoln. Nice to meet you too. Ah, delighted to make your acquaintance. I’m Edmund from Oswestry, by the way. Yes, and I teach here now, but I'd definitely say Aylesbury and Lincoln aren't places I encounter often in academic circles. I've never had a classmate from Aylesbury before. It's nice to meet someone from another part of the country. Oh, certainly, regional diversity is rich. I’ve always had a soft spot for the lesser-known areas of England. There’s a certain charm to them. Indeed, Buckinghamshire has its own unique dialect but it’s often glossed over. And you? Well, my background is in language, so I’ve always been fascinated by dialects and regional differences. Did you know that the beginnings of English law were heavily influenced by Welshmen in medieval times? That’s really interesting, Edmund! So, do you often incorporate that kind of information into your lectures? Yeah, it’s always fascinating to find the threads that connect us across time and place. I once lectured on the linguistic influences in Spanish Law, and the Basque Country has some fascinating legal intricacies rooted in language. Absolutely, I did my studies focusing on language as a tool for legal communication across borders. It’s fascinating how in China, for example, the dialects vary so much even within the same city. Yes! And I've always been curious about the London dialects, it seems like there's the working-class rhyming slang and then the kind of posh, more refined one. Right. London is the melting pot for those things, a microcosm of England. The East End rhyming slang is indeed working class, while the more traditional Received Pronunciation has its roots in the upper and upper-middle class areas like Kensington and Hampstead. It’s really interesting to see how English is used in legal contexts in these different cities. I spent a semester studying abroad in Spain, and it was invaluable. But back to sport, I couldn’t help but notice last weekend’s Rugby 7s tournament was quite something. Rugby, yes... I played at university, in fact. I've had the privilege to see how sport crosses boundaries, much like language. Rugby in particular has a universal sense of camaraderie. I've just started watching it more closely since moving to the east coast.

I saw your mum's latest Facebook post. She's still doing that Ice Bucket Challenge isn't she? Oh, yes! She's always on about various charities. It's actually quite admirable, isn't it? Caring about so many causes and people – always willing to help. But she definitely puts the pressure on us all to follow suit! I wish I could get away with just donating instead of having to get doused with water and set up my own fundraising page! I know! She's always saying, 'if not for anything else, for your health!' But seriously, it's great that she encourages us in our own capacities to give back. Speaking of health, did you hear that Aunt Margaret's adopting another child? Oh my god, no! I want to hear more about that. We've been talking about having children, and how it might affect our careers, lives, you know? Yeah. Aunt Margaret's always been so open about her experiences as a mother. Now that she's looking to extend her family, it might be interesting to ask her about her approach this time around. And while on the subject of family, what about arranging a time for all cousins to get together? It's been ages since we all met. Ah, a nice idea! Possibly, we could plan an event or a trip together? Something really fun. I'm all for it. I always enjoy our get-togethers doesn't matter what we do as long as we're together. Yeah, like we used to, exploring Bedford or just having a big lunch at mum's. I miss those days. Who knows, maybe we could even plan a family reunion or something? It could be really fun. As long as changing the date and place isn't on my end. I can plan anything as long as it's on paper and not for me to physically do any of it. I see what you mean! It's always funny when it comes to family. One could think you're more organized than a business just because you have all the qualifications right there on the certificate! Very true. And don't even get me started on filling out forms. I just wish all that could be automated for family stuff. I know! And don't you always say the most about your diet when it's not actually working?

Oh, did I mention my first move's cost? I'd nearly forgotten. It's been ages. The council will want £100 just to move my chicken coop, and that's not including storage fees—or the ridiculous quote from that removals company just for the beds, let alone the rest of the house. I knew those chicken coop relocations weren't part of my technical planning training. What did you end up paying for the removals? I had a similar deal with my own stuff last year when I left Walsall. Oh, we had that, but with a twist. I have to check the website for the transcription job today. It's only been a week since I got the new online gig, but already I'm loving the flexibility. No more early starts for me, though I do miss making coffee for everyone morning and evening. It's funny, isn't it? Used to be, everyone had a morning coffee, then after school, and now it's just people grab it when they can. You, for example, with those early morning transcription or whenever jobs. Mornings or no, it’s different working from home. I used to commute for 45 minutes each way. Now, my commute is the short walk from the bedroom to the study. But the early starts do leave me with some extra time later for community stuff, if I want to engage. Speaking of time engagement, isn't it bizarre how time really is money now? They charge by the hour for all sorts, storage, and removals included. I saw online storage doesn’t come cheap either. The labour leadership and this country, we've been all about time and money in politics lately, haven't we? I just wish there was a bit more idealism in the mix. The Labour party’s so divided now since Corbyn's leadership ended. It feels like nobody can agree on anything anymore. Idealism and changing the world. It sure seems harder to change things now than when we were younger. Or does it just feel that way with each generation? I think we've given up on public service for personal gain a bit too much. Look at the Brexit fiasco. Or even the council’s household waste collection changes. It's just all about cost-saving, seemingly with no thought to services or, you know, the planet.

Mum, I was thinking about Christmas. I don't think we've ever had a theme. You know, like when people decorate their houses in matching colors or themes. It might be fun. What do you think? Oh really? That sounds interesting. We've always just gone with a traditional red and green, or some kind of winter wonderland thing. A theme could be a nice change. What kind of theme did you have in mind? I was thinking maybe a Scandinavian winter theme. Like white and light gray with some natural elements like wood and fir. Or maybe something a bit more fun, like Wonderland or a winter forest. What theme would you like? Honestly, I'm open to anything that's not too messy or complicated, but a bit festive. Right, but fun and festive can go together. We could do little deer and mushrooms and stuff. It would be quite magical, don't you think? Mm, creative. I like that. But also, let's not forget about the people we're going to be spending time with. Do we have any big family gatherings or plans for friends? Not really. Last year we had a small dinner at home with just the three of us. But maybe we could invite some of our closest friends this year. What about the in-laws? We haven't seen them since lockdown, right? Yes, it's been ages hasn't it? Maybe we should invite them as well? We could do a hybrid thing if they're still in Wales or...? Yeah, we could do a Zoom if necessary. But face-to-face would be better. Maybe we could plan something ahead, a week-end get-together in Totnes? That could work. Totnes is lovely for Christmas. And it's close enough for them to come over, probably together with your brother and his family. Okay, that sounds like a plan. And we could couple it with a low-key trip somewhere next day, if everyone's up for it. Not too much of a holiday, but just a day out to change things up. A day out somewhere? Like where would you guys like to go? I don't know, somewhere local maybe. Paignton Zoo if it's open, or maybe Dartmoor for a walk. It depends on the weather. Dartmoor sounds lovely. We could all do with some fresh air and a walk around Christmas time.

Remember when we all went to that Richmond's place during Grace's birthday? The sausages were incredible. Oh, they were. Had the proper chip van on site, right? Still have nightmares about the handkerchiefs though. That questions game was kind of intense. But those sausages, they're a part of my history now. Any chance of a return visit? I'd be in. All in. But speaking of intense... how keeps coming up with these questions at a moment's notice? Yeah, and the handkerchief bit – I'm still waiting for my dues. She's running out of socks. She likes to keep things suspenseful, even in places of leisure. Like the whole "who's the best snorer" thing that she imposed on us. The best snorer? That was... enlightening. I thought it was just my mate for sure until… Yeah! Until that moment when Vik scoffed on his back and started a symphony all his own. I mean, I thought I knew loud, but that was something else. It was peak camaraderie though, wasn’t it? Like we were all in this together. Even if it was about who could make the most noise in their sleep. It’s funny how silly things can bring us closer as a group. And then you add the fact that she somehow dragged us into that 'waterfields bakeries' debate – doesn’t matter if it's Warrington or London, the real question is which one does the best sausage rolls? Definitely Warrington for the win. But getting side-tracked, any updates on your audit work? I feel like the world of numbers doesn’t sound quite as exciting as our pub adventures. Oh, it has its perks but honestly, I spend my days wishing I could just be discussing sausages instead. Or hunting down the best handkerchief. Our next challenge? Actually, what about revisiting the chip van concept at the pub? Like a sausage roll and chip combo that can show Bridgewater what’s up. Now you're talking. There's just something about sausage rolls that screams 'northwest'. Maybe even start a local contest. “Best sausage roll in Warrington.” Could be our next project. But we'd need a proper judging panel. Not just us, this time. Maybe drag Vik’s parents into it – they love their food standards. I’d love that. Vik, here's your next role: taster extraordinaire. Count me in, I'd be the vice jury for handkerchief aesthetics if that's going on.

So, Dad, did you manage to sort out anything on the farm this weekend? Yeah, had a bit of a tussle with the new tractor. It's not as user-friendly as I thought. Had to read the manual twice to figure out how to get the plow down! Oh, that sounds like a right faff! I knew those new models were going to cause some headaches! But I got there eventually. I had to call Sam up and he walked me through it over the phone. Good lad, Sam. Always willing to lend a hand. That's Sam for you. Always the hero. What else did you get up to? Did you get any of your gardening done? Well, I was planning to, but the weather didn't quite play along - another rainy day on Saturday morning. So I just tidied up the greenhouse instead. Still, at least you got something done. What about you? How was your weekend? Pretty good, thank you for asking. Had a lovely day out with Sarah and the kids. We took them to the new theme park that's just opened on the outskirts of town. That sounds busy but fun. Did Thomas and Emily enjoy it? They loved it! Thomas was over the moon with the ride that spins round really fast, and Emily was more into the pony rides. It's amazing how different their interests can be at that age. It sure is. I've been trying to get more involved with Thomas' coding lessons, but it's not easy keeping up with that stuff. How's that been going for him? He's doing okay. He seems to really enjoy it, but like any new skill, there are ups and downs. Sometimes the frustration shows. But he's getting there. I was thinking of setting up a coding meetup with some kids from his school. Just to make it more fun and maybe find some other projects we can work on together. That's a great idea. Coding's such a useful skill, and who knows, it might even lead to something worthwhile for him in the future. Yeah. Plus, it could be a way for him to meet other kids who share similar interests. You know how it is, most of his friends right now don't really 'get it' yet. I do. Boys his age are all into football, Minecraft, and whatnot.

So, how are you finding teaching at Ravenswood? Oh, it's been a whirlwind. The kids are lovely, but it's been a learning curve for me, you know? I used to teach languages at the university, so moving to secondary school has been quite a shift. I can imagine. Going from uni to school is quite different, and the curriculum can be a challenge sometimes, right? Absolutely right. I mean, with languages, we're trying to create secondary materials for kids who have never really been given much opportunity to learn a language in primary school. It's tough, but rewarding. That’s great to hear, dear. I used to teach languages too in London before moving here to Birmingham. How is your husband coping with the new baby? Ah, well, that’s a whole different story. He's doing his best, but we're all up late, I must say. We’re looking for a bit of advice on how to create a routine for the little one that works for both of us. Oh, that’s right. I’ve got a bit of experience with that myself. I have a nephew and niece who are about your baby's age. How old is the little one now? He's nine months. He's so inquisitive already. I remember when my niece was that age. She was always so interested in everything around her. The most important thing is probably trying to set a routine but also being flexible. You can't predict really how each day is going to go. That's exactly what my husband and I are finding. But it's hard to find the balance between the baby's needs and our own, and our need to rest. And you know, it's okay to ask for help too. No one expects you to be supermum right away. Do you have support around you? Oh, yes, we do. My mum's really been a lifeline but we also have a nanny a day or two a week which is a big help. That does make a huge difference. I remember when my sister had her first and she just couldn't imagine how she could manage without her mum's help for a while. Exactly. And what about you? How have you found moving to Birmingham and this new job? You know, it's taken some getting used to, but I enjoy it.

You know, it's remarkable how complex these nests are. The birds are truly engineers themselves. Yes, and they're always so neat and tidy. You never see any mess outside the nest, do you? That's because birds are tidy creatures. It's just one of the many things that I find fascinating about them. I've also made a new cake today. Do you fancy a slice? Oh, always up for cake. Are you still using the same recipe you taught me? Yes, the classic Victoria Sponge – always a winner. Is that the one with the added bit of ginger, as well? Correct. It gives it a nice zing. I should probably cut back on the ginger though – diabetes you see. Ah, yes, the diabetes. How are you managing with that? As well as can be expected. I've been watching my diet much more closely and taking my meds regularly. It's a bit of a challenge but I'm managing. You’re doing well though, I think. You’re still active and in good spirits, at least. Well, it’s better than the alternative. Speaking of which, have you seen all these birds? I’ve got at least three different species visiting the feeders. Yes, they love the feeders. I’ve noticed the sparrows are very… bold. Indeed. Very proud and chattering, aren’t they? Reminds me, we weren’t too clear on the bird feeder situation. Do we need to refill them before you leave for your trip? Good point. I’ll make sure to fill them up before I go. You taking your trip soon, then? No, not for a while. Just busy with errands and family visits at the moment. Speaking of which, has anyone been over to see Aunt Betsy lately? She can get lonely sometimes. Yes, I was thinking I might take her some of this cake if I can get her to take it. She used to make the best puppet shows with our kids. Those were the days. I remember when this whole garden would be clogged with children and the puppet theatre would pop up out of nowhere. Yes, and now it’s just the birds and a few stray cats. It’s a bit harder to keep up with everyone as we get older. Absolutely. I used to ride my bike everywhere, now I’m finding that a brisk walk in the garden is about all I can manage.

I've decided I need a first course. I have to order today's special, sounds lovely. Splendid choice. You know, reminds me of my grandmother who always insisted on choosing the day's special herself. She'd say "Nancey, today’s special – do tell!" Yeah, I'd totally order the day’s special at my grandparents' place too. Waiter approaches, interrupts: "Could you kindly pick out your special today?" Ah, keeps coming backwards and forwards with the coffee. Thank you, sir, yes. The special today. I’ll have that as well then. Is that a local dish? Waiter: "Yes, madam. It’s a sample from village recipes. Traditional - "Şaraplı Sığır", beef in wine." That sounds appealing. How about your second dish, have you already picked? Ah, perhaps I’ll have a bit of the grilled meze. I don’t normally eat much meat but it sounds good today. I think I’ll have the vegetarian option, while I'm being adventurous. It’s a first time for everything, right? Waiter: Anything else? Perhaps a bottle of the local white wine as well? I’m told, it pairs well with today’s special. Waiter: "Excellent choice, gentlemen. Our Anorthosis Reisling is local and goes well with the dishes." Actually, on a different note. Did you hear about the family who adopted the stray dog that hangs around the restaurant? Oh, the one that sat right by our table last year? Yeah, ended up chasing my niece’s ball. Waiter: "Yes, they’ve named it Belkis after the mythical queen of the place. It sure knows how to steal hearts!" That's so sweet. They really spoil it. I know because just yesterday when I took my cat here, he freaked out at the prospect of a real dog in such an enclosed space. Waiter: Ah, pets and almost upsetting the café's order. I was telling you about my hearing aids the other day. It’s amazing. Totally changed my world. For the first time in ages, I could actually hear what people were saying across the room. That’s fantastic for any of my older family members that are going through similar issues. I know it’s been really tough for my aunt recently. Waiter: Yes, it’s a common issue, very debilitating when it’s not addressed. Indeed. So, I’ve been thinking about what we might do when living out here in Northern Cyprus for the summer.

Mum, Dad, it's so great to be here! I've missed you both so much. How have you been since I last saw you six months ago? Oh, we've been busy working, as always, but doing really well. I've just finished the GCSE marking season and things are settling down. You know how it is. Besides my work, I've been out at the farmers' markets a bit more lately, trying to get some new suppliers. The past year has been quite challenging with the weather affecting crops. That's a lot to deal with. You two always manage to stay so positive. Speaking of challenges, I have to ask about the old house. Any progress on deciding what to do with it? Yes, actually, we've been looking into some options. We were thinking of a partial refurbishment. The kitchen and bathrooms could definitely use an update. But we want to keep the character of the house as much as possible, you know? Exactly. And maybe we should visit some of these heritage home shows. Some of the restorations they do can give us really good ideas. For sure! We could also look for some local contractors who specialize in preserving heritage properties. I’ve heard they often have some clever ideas for updating historic features. That’s a good idea. We’ll look into that. It’s just finding the time. You know how it is when you’re working full time and still managing the farm. I understand. It’s a lot to juggle, really. But you should enjoy yourselves while you’re making plans. And what about Christmas? Will you two be doing anything special? Well, we were thinking of inviting your friends over this year. It'd be nice to have all the family here. Maybe even have the dinner at our place instead of yours this time. Yes, that could be fun. We can decide on a menu and allocate who does what. It’d be great to have you help out with the cooking and planning. I’d love to! You know I love making big meals. Plus, it’s always great to see everyone together. And what about presents? You’re getting quite grown-up now so we might need to up our game if we want to surprise you properly. Well, you know me... I'm easy to please.

So, I was browsing on YouTube yesterday and came across an episode of Jeremy Kyle. Jeez, I can't believe people still watch that show. Are you kidding? It's like reality TV gone wrong. People get insulted, yelled at, and for what? A bunch of catfish conversations? Exactly! Like this one woman who was convinced she was talking to someone from a dating app right? And turns out... I can't believe it still goes on. Are you serious? Right in front of the live audience? That's some hardcore shaming. It's such a cheap way to get ratings. They just set people up with easily debunkable dating profiles. But the worst part is how the audience reacts - oh we're all so shocked and appalled until we see the next person getting berated. It's tragic that it's entertainment. What's next, a rebooted Jerry Springer? Well, at least with catfish stories, people might watch to learn or even enjoy the mystery aspect. But Jeremy Kyle...it's just about tearing people down for ratings. Honestly, most of those stories could probably be solved with a bit of common sense. Like if you're on a dating app, do a bit of research on the person. It's not rocket science. Totally. Like, if someone's too good to be true or is avoiding video calls, there should be some red flags flying high. We all know someone who’s been catfished or at least been approached with suspicious online profiles. Oh yeah, my friend Alex went through it last year. This guy would send her super generic yet romantic messages and the profile picture was clearly a stock photo. Oh, the blurred profile pictures are always a sign. If they're too vague about their life, like they can never talk about what they do or where they live... Or if they seem to be making an excuse after excuse for not video calling or meeting – it’s probably some kind of scam or catfishing attempt. And it’s so much easier for them to be shady online because people drop their guard. This reminds me of the adage about not believing almost anything online. There's just no way to truly verify someone’s identity or complete honesty. Yeah. It's amazing how often we don’t question or investigate. I saw one YouTube series where they investigate profiles like that, it’s really eye-opening... and kind of scary.

Mum, I was thinking about studying abroad next year. Maybe move to Paris. What do you think? Oh, my dear! Well, that sounds exciting. But don't forget you'd need to learn French. You've always been lazy with languages. Hmm, true. But I'm considering it. Going to France could be a great opportunity to learn and experience the culture. Yes, indeed. It's a wonderful country, full of history and beauty. You'll love it. But don't forget about the language barrier. It's a bit different when you speak it fluently. I've been lazy because English is everywhere, but I think I can manage. You're very quick to pick things up, even if you're not the keenest at the start. Just remember, it's the best way to truly experience another culture. And you'll have wonderful foods to talk about! That's true! And maybe learn some basic Italian? You visit Venice pretty often. Ah, Italian. Well, that's next on my list! I'm not too bad with German and this is a perfect moment to start. But learning a new language is different as we get older, isn’t it? Quite. You're in good health though. 60 is the new 40, right? Ah, my dear, I'd take that motto as an exaggeration! But it's a good spirit. Old age really is a mindset, you know? That's true. Anyway, you're quite comfortable with German doesn't come in handy when you're in Italy? Sometimes, but it's different, especially in Venice, which has its own dialect. But the basics help. And who knows, maybe we together learn Italian someday! I'd like that. Speaking of getting old, I wanted to tell you about my grandma's bees. She's been having trouble with them. Oh, dear. That's a shame. Bees can be quite delicate, especially these days with all the environmental changes. Yeah, just like when I was little and so fascinated with your art, I want to see if there's a way to combine my love for tech and bees. That's an interesting idea! There's a real need for sustainable beekeeping these days. I might even know someone who could help with that. Really? That would be perfect. You connect me? Sure thing. I'll reach out tomorrow. Thanks, any word on the computer problem I left?

Oh did I ever tell you about that time I drove past a police station and failed to turn around when they were clearly illuminated? You didn't mention that. Is this some kind of indispensable driver's skill now? Oh no, it just seemed so bad because they were clearly equipped and ready. Like they'd been waiting. Perhaps they actually didn't notice you at all, considering how often they probably see people speeding past. True. That's probably too much knowledge for most drivers, isn't it? True. But seriously, have you guys heard about Dorset's roads? They're so narrow, just like the ones in Kent. I bet they cause more accidents than the places we've talked about earlier - oh, and did I mention how much I dislike Hammersmith? Hammersmith is a whole different story. And these people barely scrape by in their old buildings, between the rain, their poorly-made homes or flats, it's a wonder there aren't more collapses. Yeah but it's funny, I met someone who just moved to a new town that I thought was 'bad' based on reputation. But they loved it. Said it wasn't as bad as everyone made it out to be. Ah, the power of expectation, perhaps? I know someone, a friend's mother, she lives in Harlow, really enjoys it despite what others say about the area. Harlow's got a lot of character. And they've really made an effort in the last decade or so. Yeah, it's all about finding the right place for you. And sometimes the secret gems are in the places people least expect. The secret gems. Speaking of which, did you see those MOT signs on the last roundabout we passed? Oh yes! Because who actually remembers six months to the day when our MOT is due? Exactly! It's like they put them up everywhere just in case we forget, isn't it? And of course, then there's the shock when it comes to the cost. "Our solicitor fees this month, just for paperwork..." Oh, I know. It's like a mystery whether they're skilled or just good at charging us more. And don't even get me started on health. I was trying to make a doctor's appointment... Oh, that's the age old hunt for a GP appointment. Phone systems these days, they make you feel like you're watching paint dry.

Ah, keeps coming backwards and forwards with nothing else to do. You know what it's like, keeps me on my feet.      Oh dear, I know exactly. Can't sit still for long anyhow, but this is something else.      Well, when you've spent your whole life working and then all that suddenly stops… it's like a part of you is missing.      Exactly. But we've each other, family, and the comfort of our own home. And these good cups of tea. It's not so bad, really.      No, that's so true. And it's funny, when I was working, all I wanted was a break from the daily grind. Now, I sometimes find myself missing it in ways. The structure, the routine, the daily interactions even if sometimes they drove you crazy.      Well, at least you're not missing the commute. I used to dread that every day.      True, true. Alright, I'm making you another cup, deal?      Lovely, thank you. So, is the lounge room sorted? The insurance people were supposed to call back.      Oh, I forgot all about that! Yes, it’s sorted. They came, saw the damage, and are going to send someone over to sort it out. Just waiting on them now.      Thank goodness. That room’s been a headache.      Indeed. It’s one of those things that, though minor on paper, can really spoil your day when it happens.      That’s so true. Reminds me of when we were younger… the little things would set us off, wouldn’t they.      Like being late for school or having to do math homework.      Math homework was the worst! “In 1992, during the company's...” You’d think it was fiction, not education.      Story of my life. Though, funny enough, it’s come in useful here and there though never in a situation I anticipated.      Same. Who thought we’d be needing fractions to bake, right?      Exactly! But baking has been a good pastime. Here, would you like some of that cake I baked yesterday?      Oh, would I! You’re getting better at it.      Thanks. It’s all practice and trial. Plus, you, my friend, are my number one taste tester.      I’m just glad to help! As long as there’s cake involved.      Alright, alright. Here you are then. --- This conversation touches upon a mix of present-day topics , and typical topics for people in this age group and relationship, which could range widely and would usually be tailored more closely with specific details about their personalities or current interests.

So, I was browsing through some old photos today while you were at the workshop. Found this one; it's of us at that music festival in the late 2010s. Ah, right. I remember that one. Wasn't it just the best? The atmosphere was electric – and the questions we asked ourselves back then... Haha, yeah. "Should we stay in the city for our music careers or pursue PhDs right now?" Exactly. All very pressing life decisions. But even though we chose different paths, it’s been amazing to watch each other grow in our respective fields, don't you think? Absolutely. And, honestly, I’m glad you've been able to stick with something that brings you such joy. PhD life must have its moments, but from what little I understand, you're making valuable contributions to your field. It's been quite a journey, and being able to talk about it sometimes makes it feel less isolating. Plus, there are the little things that make it all worthwhile - like when I finally got my research question right or when I heard back from editors that my submission was accepted. I'm so proud of you for sticking through all of that. Not to mention, it has to be kind of neat, while I'm managing research projects and overseeing entire teams, to be able to say you're also contributing to the academic side of things. Ah, but without your guidance and mentorship earlier on, I might still be questioning my academic choices in hindsight. You were one of my biggest influences in deciding to pursue further education. I'd say we’ve definitely helped each other navigate the toughest parts of our careers. And it’s funny how our paths continue to align. Even now, when I'm working on the next big project or thinking of how to approach a problem, I still draw on some of the strategies we discussed back in our uni days. Speaking of which, have you noticed how the weather has been lately? It's like the entire season changing in a matter of days. Our garden must be loving all the unpredictability, though. I know! Our roses have bloomed like crazy because of it. But, it’s so hard to keep up, right? One day we're preparing for frost and the next it’s shorts weather again. And it’s not just the garden; the whole job market seems equally unpredictable these days.

I keep telling you to invest in Spotify's stock. Look at today's news, it's skyrocketing! I talked to my cousin the financial advisor and he said tech stocks are unpredictable right now. Plus, I'm not sure I agree with their subscription model... It's just so convenient isn't it? I mean, I used to have about a hundred gigs of music that I couldn't play because they took down the websites... and I had to buy the CDs again. Which is fine, but I keeps changing phones and losing all my music every time. Yeah, I had that issue too – always had to transfer everything. But, honestly, I’m not sure if I’d pay for a subscription like that if I wasn’t among the chosen few who can afford it without thinking twice. University fees are through the roof, and then you’re supposed to spend even more just to listen to music? It feels unfair. Oh, university fees... how’s that PhD going? Struggling with the funding or are things looking up? It's... varied. Some weeks it's brilliant, other weeks it just feels like a never-ending slog. The fees are a killer, if I’m honest. I’m counting every penny now. I know what you mean. I was telling my mum the other day about how the university fees are so high now, and she said back in her day – which wasn’t that long ago – it was free or significantly cheaper. Yeah, it really is a different world now. I’m worried I’m going to be paying these loans off until I’m 40, and who knows if there will even be jobs available for a PhD in my field by then. Except, I guess I’m lucky if I do get a job, at least I have that hope, unlike some people. Exactly! The unemployment situation isn’t fun for anyone. I mean, I know couple of people who have been out of work for over a year and it really takes a toll on their self-esteem. You feel like you’re losing your purpose. Absolutely. It’s that constant search for meaning, isn’t it? For validation and purpose in our lives. And it’s so much harder when you can’t find work that uses your skills or education to its fullest potential.

Mum, I was thinking about writing a kids' book. Oh really? That's quite ambitious, love. What would it be about? Well, it's kind of about different families. You know, like mixed families, step families and all the different ways we can be – you know, because some of my friends don’t live with their dads and stuff. Ah, that's a brilliant idea, actually. I wish I had something like that when I was your age. It would've helped me understand things better, even though my situation with your dad wasn’t too bad. Ah, dear, I can attest to that. When I was your age, I struggled to make sense of what happened when our family was in a bit of a mix due to the war making life complicated. Books might’ve helped me feel less alone. Oh, Gran, you were a kid during the war? Did your family structure change often? Yes, ever so often we or our friends were adjusting to new arrangements. We didn’t have all the resources back then, but we found ways to cope together. You know, seeing kids deal with separation nowadays is different, but the feelings are similar, right, Mum? It’s about making sense of their new normal. Yeah, exactly! A book could show kids it’s okay to feel different feelings in different families, because all families have their own way of being, and all are valid. I like where this is going. When I was teaching, I found using storytelling helped children process big changes in their lives or just understand people around them a bit more. Maybe the book could include pictures, different characters just like the families we're talking about. And maybe include some stories of patience, understanding, and acceptance. From your own life, or even changing the endings to positive ones. Yeah, that sounds perfect – make it real but hopeful. Remember those days when I used to tell you those bedtime stories? It was my way of making sense of the world too, and connecting. Clearly, storytelling runs in the family. Do you think it could show that blended or any kind of family can be a funny, happy, and supportive one just like yours and mine? Definitely, I can use those moments as...kind of the heart of the story maybe. But how do you handle if the stories are really sad?

So, I've been meaning to talk to you about it, babe. I've been meaning to shave my legs. I've never really been one to worry about body hair but recently I noticed all of my uni friends shave and. Aye now, the peer pressure is a real force in uni life isn't it? But don't do anything that makes you uncomfortable, you know? If you feel like it's just a bit of maintenance and you enjoy it why not? Exactly, and it's not like I'm weirded out by it or anything. It's just...when I started noticing all of them shaving. Like at first I thought it was just girls but now I've seen guys too. Is that a trend cos down here in Cambridge, among my mates, we just let it be. I mean, I've got a bit of stubble and no one bats an eye. Exactly! It's all about personal choice. But sometimes it feels like you have to. Right? And it's funny because in this house growing up, it's all about not really caring what anyone else thinks. Like, my mum would say this is about what makes you happy. Aye, I know. But funnily enough, while I was growing up in Doncaster, there was this whole stigma about body hair. It was really weird, like, the more hair you had the more 'manly' you were or something. Wow, no way. That's really different in Cambridge. If anything, more often than not, we praise each other for embracing what we naturally have. That's a nice way of putting it! I like that. I think that's kind of what's influenced me to consider it, you know? Being here and seeing people not caring really gives you confidence to just be you. And, if anything, it's good to consider shaving just for ease when you're in hot weather or things like that. Yeah, but also it's a pain changing the blade every couple of weeks on my Dad’s razor. I know what you mean! My brother is always using Dad’s and he just gives me his, but I don’t like using those, they’re not that great for the skin. Exactly! Plus, the whole process. I’d almost rather just let it be if it's just for what others think.

I've decided I need a first name's passport. I want my first initial to be D and my last initial will clearly be Jones. That'll give me D J Jones, just like David Jones but without all the plaid. You might need to get used to questions at the border: "Excuse me, sir, where'd you say you got that tattooed accent of yours?" Might be worth it. Just picture walking through customs and everyone suddenly speaking with a Geordie twang. "Alreet love, welcome to... I need me spectacles to see where I fucking am!" Hilarious. But sticking with first initials, you've got your pick. Might just highlight the whole drinking and alcohol thing though - you planning on testing the limit of 'D' through the alphabet by having each drink start with a different letter? Oh, that's a hilarious thought... D beginnings in the English alphabet are pretty thin though. Dandelion and Burdock? Dry Pastis? Yeah, maybe that's why you're a research manager and not a bartender. But seriously, different letters can significantly impact the perspective. For instance, if we focus on 'R' for reasons unknown to most: Russian roulette with random cocktails, or 'X' for the more... exotic or extra-ordinary concoctions? Aha, now we're onto something. I could write a study: "The Impact of Alphabetical Choice of Ingredients and Perceived Quality of Cocktails." Just need to get past the ethics committee. True, "X" has so much potential: Xanté, Xá xá, and if one’s feeling adventurous, some less conventional mix of liquids starting with "X". The possibilities are endless. Speaking of endless, getting back to reality - did you hear about those controversial boxing matches they're planning in Reading and how some people are linking it to potential for increased drug use in the area? Yeah, I saw something about it on BBC News. Specifically, they were discussing how events like these might inadvertently promote drug culture among spectators, particularly if there are large numbers of young people attending. Right. And then, of course, the aspect of racism in football... it seems like every other day there's a new incident reported in the news. Absolutely. It's a concerning trend. I've been following some of the research on the psychology of sports fans and how it connects to racist behaviors. It often ties back to a sense of identity linked to the team, which can unfortunately be tied to harmful stereotypes if not monitored carefully.

Right, so I've been looking at this incredible old barn from the 18th century that I want to convert into an event space and a small eco-lodge. It's got so much character and history. You've been doing this work for years, so I'd love to get your advice, Linda. Oh, absolutely. I'm always keen to help where I can and share my experiences. It's a fantastic project idea, but I must admit, you've taken on quite the challenge there. Historic barns can be tricky for so many reasons - structural keepsakes, conservation guidelines, and working within local heritage laws. Yes, I've started to delve into all that. But I want to make sure I do it in a way that respects the building’s original integrity while making it functional for our current needs. Was there a particular project that really tested your limits? Oh, there have been a few over the years. But I recall one at a 16th-century manor house in Kent. The barn there was barely standing and we had to carefully restore it while also meeting modern fire safety and building codes. One of the biggest challenges was sourcing materials that were both modern enough for today's standards but looked appropriate for the era. That is the perfect dilemma. I've already started scanning local suppliers for 'like' materials. But in terms of the acquisition process itself, do you think the local council will be open to funding part of it? Some of these buildings are under the local heritage conservation board. Funding is always the tricky bit. The local councils, Heritage England, and sometimes even the National Lottery Heritage Fund are fantastic sources. However, they can also be very competitive. You'll need a robust, well-thought-out bid for any funding. Start by making detailed appraisals of the barn’s current state and what’s required to bring it up to standard. Outline the measured steps you'll take to preserve as much of the original fabric as possible. Every little bit counts when it comes to showing historic responsibility. So, creating a detailed bid framework and conservation plan upfront is key, even before the application. You also mentioned local suppliers for materials matching the historical period. Exactly. For the Kent project, we found a local supplier who specializes in reclaimed materials. And for those we couldn't source historically accurate for, we ordered bespoke pieces that matched the original.

Oh, did I ever tell you about that online linguistic course I took over the summer? You're always doing something, aren't you? Are we still on about the one from Coursera? That’s the one! So, there was this one particular module about the evolution of dialects in urban environments and how they're becoming more accent-neutral, less tied to region where you're from, especially among younger people. I found it absolutely fascinating! That makes sense, given the mix of people moving around for work and study. It's like seeing the old regional dialects being hybridized in new ways. Exactly! It's similar to what's happened with your research, I think, even though you're more focused on historical linguistics. But the big themes—how language reflects society and how it changes—are really tied together. Absolutely.
