And for the rest, how about a sit-down dinner, but then let them mingle afterwards, maybe outside if weather permits? Brings out the social aspect."   ANON:   "Excellent, that sounds like a plan then. Speaker 2 can you tackle a few calls to confirm attendees?

So, girls, what do you think we should do for Mother's Day? We're going to make it special for me. Ideas? Oh, can we go on an adventure again? Like to the Forest School? Yeah, Forest School! We can pretend we're little fairies and trolls and collect sticks for Mommy! That sounds like a lovely plan, but I'd also like something a bit more comfortable for this special day. How about we get out all the art supplies and make cards and decorations for Mommy? Something she can treasure. But, but Mommy, don't forget about your cup of tea with those homemade biscuits. That's a great idea! And maybe even bake cookies this time instead of just drawing them. What do you want to call this day of celebration? How about "Adventure and Art Day"? Yeah, and "Mommy's Cozy Day" too! I love it. Now, let's break that down. We'll spend the morning at the Forest School if the weather's nice, then come back for lunch and art time. And can we have a picnic at the Forest School? Like, bring blankets and all? That sounds perfect. And then we'll return home, whip up some cookies, and decorate the cards and all those fantastic artworks you're going to create. And maybe Mommy can wear that crown we're making! Of course, Mommy would wear a crown. Now, let's get started on the sandwiches and treats for the picnic. Who likes to help with that? Excellent! We've got our Mother's Day planned! But first, let's make sure we use proper English and some fun idioms in our cards. Like what? Alright, let me see... How about "You're one in a million!". And maybe "You help me shine brighter than the brightest star!" Like in this drawing of Mommy being the sun! Exactly. And another one could be "Thanks for being my rock", thinking of how steady and strong rocks are. I like that. And can we draw... a big heart with arrows pointing to Mommy because she always points us in the right direction? That's a beautiful idea. Let's make sure we include a little joke too to make Mommy laugh, like "Why did the coffee file a police report? It got mugged!" I don't get it. Why? Because a mug is a container for coffee, so if it gets taken, it's like the coffee got mugged!

So, I hear that your sister was recently diagnosed with breast cancer. How have things been for her and your family? It's been a tough time, to say the least. We've all rallied around though, you know? Family time has been drastically different, but in a way, kind of brought us closer together. Yeah, I'd imagine. A diagnosis like that can change a lot. Have they started treatment yet? Yeah, she had surgery to remove the tumour about a month ago and is currently undergoing radiotherapy. It's a whole new world for us, discussing things like scars, hair loss, and the emotional ups and downs. I can only imagine. When my father had cancer, the hardest part was seeing him struggle with the treatment’s side effects. But also, seeing how strong he was - oh, he was so strong. He always made sure to keep our spirits high, which made the whole ordeal easier for everyone, especially my mother. That’s exactly the same with my sister. She’s always been one to hide her vulnerability, but since the diagnosis, she's opened up a lot. It's actually been really good for our relationship. It's reminded us all to value each moment and not take anything for granted. I think that’s one of the most important lessons anyone can learn. Speaking of which, I’ve been feeling quite overwhelmed by the amount of work I’ve been handling lately. I know, it's not as dire as what you're going through, but it’s making me consider my own health really - both physical and mental. That’s something we all deal with at some point. I mean, since things with my sister started, I’ve also been checking in on my own health more regularly. Stress, burnout, it all affects you one way or another. More people need to talk about mental health openly, don’t you think? I noticed a lot since my father's passing, my children seem more aware and open about their emotions. Maybe it's because of the family discussions we now have, but changing the conversation about health sure seems important to me. Absolutely. My kids have been really supportive with their aunt during this. They often talk about feelings, about what they do when they're feeling overwhelmed. I reckon if we model openness about our own struggles, it sets a good example for them.

So, how was your lecture with Dr. Smith? Oh, it was pretty good. He was covering the theory behind semiotics again, which I talked about at length the other day. Made me realize again how complex language is. Yeah, the way language signifies meaning is fascinating. It questions how much of what we communicate isn’t even verbal, isn’t it? Exactly! And that makes teaching English as a language of its own quite the challenge. Not just teaching grammar but also how to “get it,” how to pick up on the cultural implications behind words. Definitely, and then on top of that there's the colloquialisms and slang. It's a very dynamic system. And I think that is why linguistics excites me so much. The language of study itself is English - which we both speak well - but to properly analyse and teach it, you need to understand so many other language features and cultural references. Absolutely. It's like learning a new language just to learn the first one properly. But it’s also so rewarding when a student finally understands a concept or a nuance that was previously lost on them. Totally, and that balance between theoretical linguistics and the practical use is difficult but so important. Speaking of which, have you seen the timetable for this term at all? Yeah, I checked it out yesterday. It seems like they keep trying to make us prioritize certain modules but my research project seems to take centre stage this semester. Oh really? What’s your project about? Comparative linguistics and food culture through a case analysis of Korean and English cooking habits. That sounds cool! I kind of went vegetarian recently because of animal treatment concerns and now I’m curious about cultural aspects around food in general. Yeah, that’s a great angle, especially for the food culture. I’m looking at how different ingredients are used or avoided, and even things like table manners or food combinations reflect cultural values and language. That reminds me, do you want to grab lunch together? I can cook if you want. I was thinking of trying some new recipes - maybe some Korean? Actually that’d be great. I want to learn more about Korean food, and having real conversations about food preparation and culture is so useful for my research. Sounds like a plan. I just have to figure out what I’m in the mood for.

Does anyone know if we’re doing any sort of quiz night or something this week? Yeah, I think we are. Didn't we all agree on doing Articulate or something similar? Oh right, I almost forgot. We can play Articulate tonight then? It's been ages! Yeah and maybe we could even have a bit of a theme, like a history quiz or something. I'm pretty sure there's a box of quiz materials somewhere around here. That sounds like a plan. Are there still Hungry Hippos in the common room? I swear I saw those on the shelf in the common room when I moved in. Hungry Hippos?! You're not seriously considering playing those as part of our quiz, are you? LOL, why not? They're just as valid as any other game option. Sure, if you want to make it fun for all ages, Hungry Hippos could work. But maybe we should also consider something a bit more... intellectual. Like, University Challenge or something. No, I'm not really that competitive about it this time. Hungry Hippos sound fun. I prefer the competitive aspect. You know, something that we can actually argue about. Like, what the most likely answer is or... Arguing about Hungry Hippos? That's a first. Yeah, but, you know, it breaks the ice and all that. Whatever, I'm in. But only if we also have a round where we have to describe stuff like it's from Twilight. Oh, or we could do a round where you have to explain something like it's in the Chaos Walking trilogy. That could be hilarious! Or a round where we describe our dream sports kit top. That could lead to some interesting designs. That's actually a great idea! Because who doesn't love designing dream sports kit tops? Or how about we describe some of our favourite in-jokes. I mean, we must have a few, right? Absolutely, we have a few. The one about the airport scanner that thinks you're smuggling puppies. That’s always a winner. Yeah, or when you crack your knuckles and someone screams "Rocky Horror Picture Show!" Oh, or talking about how we all seem to bruise at the slightest touch and pretending it was like we survived a dramatic sports injury... True that. We're also all pretty dramatic when it comes to minor injuries.

Speaker_1 and Speaker_2, let’s assume they are on their way to a family event and stuck in a traffic jam. "You'll never believe who I saw at the office today, actually, I've been meaning to tell you about this for a while." "Who? You're not gonna start telling me about your co-worker seeing ghosts, are you? I thought you were past those stories." "No, no, it was just a colleague I've been trying to catch up with - turns out she actually used to be in a band! Played lead singer in this little indie pop group that even got a bit of attention back in the day." "Oh wow, didn't know you were into indie music. Did she mention anything about reunions or if they're still active?" "She didn't say much, but it was really refreshing talking to her about something outside work and it reminded me how cool it is to meet different people in the city. Plus, fun fact: she still goes on 'office jams' with the team; they do this thing where they all come together during lunch hour and play covers together. She said it's a great stress relief and morale booster for everyone." "That sounds amazing. I actually used to play drums as a hobby. One time, we even did an impromptu gig in a pub that ended with a bunch of people singing along. But that was years ago. It's great the office has that kind of environment; it breaks the ice and makes everyone feel more connected." "Exactly! I hope our office does something like that someday. Now, speaking of breaking the ice, it looks like our traffic is getting even worse. We'll be lucky if we make it in time for tea..." "You're right. Let's just hope we can make it to the party before everyone finishes without us. I was really looking forward to some of that classic Sunday roast. Funny how a bit of traffic can ruin my appetite so much, isn't it?" "Hah, trust me, it's not just the food. It's about sharing the experience and memories. But you know, the real job will be trying to convince our uncle John to not talk about Brexit. It always ends up leading to debates. Do you think our family plans to actually discuss the Scottish referendum seriously at the party or is that just a casual dinner conversation?"

Ah, the weather today is awful, isn't it? Yes, it's been raining all morning and the wind is quite strong. It's just the kind of weather that makes one worry about catching a cold. Indeed, the change in weather can often bring with it the flu season. That it can. And with the rain keeps coming, it's just about impossible to get out for a walk without getting soaked, isn't it? Even with my boots on. Well, at least your boots are good ones, aren't they? Remember when we used to have to buy new ones every year because the rain just destroyed old ones? Speaking of practical matters, have you two had your flu jabs? Ah, now that you mention it. I think I did. But Richard here might need to book his next week or so, don't you, Richard? Probably, yes. I might have let it slip. You’re right, though, the flu can be particularly nasty for older folks like us. And technology can certainly help us stay on top of things like that. I noticed Health Service had a reminder system for flu jabs and other essential check-ups. That's a good point. I wonder how effective those things are in practice. I've always been a bit suspicious of how much influence such technology has on public health decisions. Mm, I reckon it helps a bit. But nothing beats a human reminding another human. Speaking of which, have you checked on Jane recently? Her hip is still giving her trouble, isn’t it? Yeah, it’s been a bit of a struggle for her, isn’t it? No real solution for it, unfortunately. That truly is a challenge. Hopefully, one day we'll see real advancements in hip replacements or other treatments for conditions like hers. There's actually been some real progress in prosthetic development, I’ve read. Not just for hips, but for other joints too. It’s remarkable what can be done. Really? I had no idea. I suppose it’s one of those things... keeps getting better and better, don’t it? Indeed. Seems like it's always something new with electronics and medical science, innit? Though sometimes, it feels like it's moving slower than we'd like, given our individual circumstances. That's the nature of progress, it's often slow until you look back.

So, I hear that Cassie's wedding is coming up soon, have you all started planning or talking about attending? Yeah, it's all been super talked about at work. We all kind of chatted about it during lunch the other day. I'm definitely going, and I think most of us are too. Oh, definitely! It's going to be a great time. I've already picked out a dress that I think I'm going to ruin at the reception, you never know! LOL, always the dress keeps coming up. But seriously, it's going to be an amazing wedding, I've heard. Cassie chose such a beautiful venue. I've heard it's very fancy. Apparently, they've got a band and it's even going to be fairly formal. Ah, Cassie - she’s always been quite the organization. Hence why she’s a sales manager, I suppose. True! But as much as she loves order, she’s got a knack for big surprises too. Remember when we planned that surprise birthday party for her? Oh, or that time we convinced her that a jump scare attack would actually prevent her fear of spiders. HAHA, I'm sure she would have approved of that plan. Anyway, back to the wedding - do we have a plan on who's bringing a plus one? Well, I'm still wondering if I should invite my current significant other, but we’re not really at that stage yet… Oh, that’s a dilemma. And what about those of us who don’t have a plus one… should we just RSVP with just "yes" or say something about it? I think Cassie will understand one way or another. She's very thoughtful and would just want us all together, regardless. Plus, the less of a fuss we make about it, probably the better. Good point. It’s about celebrating Cassie and James after all. True, but changing the subject, has anyone seen the new restaurant they’re building downtown by the river? I was there the other day for work and it looked amazing. Oh, yes! I heard they're having an exclusive pre-opening dinner for some of the staff and business owners’ friends. Maybe Cassie could even use it for her wedding dinner? That would be amazing! She mentioned something about wanting an outdoor, stylish spot. That could be perfect. Totally worth bringing up to her.

Ah, I hear that grandson over at James' has started using one of them new whizbang gizmos for school work. Whole council will be using it from now on they say. Young folks these days, they don't half need a degree just to work a computer or a mobile, eh? Oh yes! I had one of those newfangled tablets for my childminding business. It was a right pain to figure out at first, but once I got the hang of it I couldn't believe how much simpler it made my paperwork! True. My school district has been pushing for better tech integration, and I have to say, there's been a noticeable improvement in engagement since we got kids to start using devices in class. Though, let’s be honest, it’s also been a learning curve for us teachers. None of us were born with the internet in our pockets, after all. I remember when my oldest was at school and they started looking for a football team. He was only little, but he barely knew the rules! But these days, it seems like the kids are so savvy with all their gadgets and games, much like my grandkids who can navigate a tablet before they can tie their own shoes! Ah, they certainly are. Reminds me of when I was young and all we had was the good old BBC at 6 and 9 to spin stories for us. Though I must say, it was better for my imagination, spending more time outside and less staring at screens. Evolution of the times! But sometimes, I wonder if they're missing out on the benefits of good old-fashioned play. I always try to get my students doing some hands-on things in class, it proves to be great for developing fine motor skills and problem-solving. I completely agree! When I worked as a childminder, we used to have days where it would raining and the children would want to do nothing but sit in front of the TV, but I'd try to get them engaged in some play that didn't involve a screen and it always ended up being so much more rewarding for them. Like when we used to go to the park on days like that for a game of hide-and-seek. You'd find hidden worlds in the overgrown bushes, run tirelessly until you dropped, and then just sit and watch the world through a dandelion.

So, how was your weekend? Oh, it was fine. Nothing much. I was thinking about maybe going to the Milton Keynes chicken show this Saturday. Have you ever been? A chicken show? Yeah, it's quite a big deal. Lots of different breeds and handlers. Never been, but it sounds quaint. It is. And there's always a very traditional rural English atmosphere. That sounds fun. Do they have any good stuff to eat there, or is it just chicken? Oh, there's food stalls, pubs around. Worth a try then. And the language of it all is quite interesting. You get all sorts of terminology and regional dialect from the locals. It's great for a language teacher to hear all the variations. You talk about language a lot for a language teacher. Well, it's what I do! What's your favorite? I mean, which dialect or accent? Well, being from Hitchin, I'm most familiar with the Hertfordshire accent but I have a particular liking for the Received Pronunciation. Especially after several years of teaching it, I find it quite elegant. Ah, the Queen's English as my granddad used to call it. Exactly! Although RP is more based off certain areas of the south and not just what the Queen speaks. How about your family? What do they enjoy doing? My husband and I both love to travel. We try to take one or two trips abroad each year. He’s into the history, architecture, that kind of thing. I love the food and languages. Ah, I used to love traveling. Before Alzheimer’s, I went all over with the kids. We had great holidays in France, Spain. That’s really cool to hear. I imagine those were unforgettable for your family. Absolutely. We always made sure the kids learned a few words in the local language too. That’s so great. Language education from a young age can really stick and opens doors for them later in life. Did. I wish I could have continued encouraging them to travel and learn more languages. It’s never too late to start learning something new. Maybe there are some simple language courses you could take online? Or listen to podcasts? I might look into that. Maybe if I pick up a bit of French again, I can have some chats with my grandkids sometime. That would be lovely.

So, how was your Valentine's Day? Did you receive any chocolates or flowers or anything like that? It was actually okay, I talked to my boyfriend over the phone because he's not in town this week. But no chocolates or flowers though, which was a bit disappointing. He promised to send some flowers later this week though. That’s nice. I didn’t really do anything fancy. I went out for a meal with my family, as per usual. But we did have a very nice Italian for dinner. That sounds lovely. Italian is always a good choice. I’m actually looking forward to trying a new place in town with friends later today for my birthday. Since I wasn’t really celebrated Valentine's Day with my boyfriend, I figured why not have a girls’ night instead. That’s a great idea. And what did you choose for your birthday dinner spot? It’s a new Indian place that’s been getting a lot of good reviews. They have a special menu for big groups and it’s supposed to be great. It’s also supposed to be less expensive compared to other places. For me, it’s usually about the food, not the price when it comes to choosing a restaurant. If the food is good, I’d pay a bit more. Yeah, same here. But sometimes, you do think about value for money, especially when you’re with a big group. I agree. A mixed bag of cheap and expensive dishes is usually a good plan. You get a bit of both world. Definitely. And have you watched any good movies recently? Actually, no. I’ve been so busy catching up on studies and work this month, but I do want to watch one or two during the weekend. I’ve heard that the new Pixar movie “Soul” is good, and of course, we are supposed to watch “Valentine’s Day is Cancelled” online with a few friends. “Valentine’s Day is Cancelled”? What’s that about? It’s a romantic comedy – I think it’s supposed to be funny. We saw the trailer and it seems like something we’d all enjoy. And with it being on one of the free streaming platforms, it seems like a good idea. That sounds like fun. We almost didn’t make it to the cinema the other week because all the good movies we want to see were sold out or got moved to online screenings due to COVID.

So, I was browsing this weekend. I came across an article about this new policy in Sweden. They're basically instituting an education program aimed at tackling young children's unconscious biases. Oh yeah? That's interesting. What sparked that? You know, after a couple of high-profile incidents, there was kind of this nationwide reckoning and they decided something had to be done. I wish we had more of that here actually. We've been talking about racism and police brutality non-stop for years and... well, it feels like not a lot changes. Exactly! And, you know, it's not just about the police or individual racist acts. It's systemic. The system is racist. This is a good step though, even if it's just the beginning. Absolutely. But let's not kid ourselves, it's going to take more than a few educational programs to dismantle centuries of institutional racism. True, but... how else do you intend to start? You have to begin somewhere. And it's this kind of grassroots approach that can lead to real change in the long term. Definitely. It's just frustrating how slowly these changes come. And funnily enough, while the system is so slow to change in politics, the tech and financial sectors seem to think the market can fix everything. Capitalism's promise of solving all our problems is perhaps its most insidious trait. Meanwhile, housing prices are skyrocketing because somehow buying property is key to financial stability, and all the while, social and working conditions just get worse. But it's not just about the working conditions. For many, even finding stable, affordable housing is a nightmare. We've just had a proposal for a new property development go through near my parents in Kensal Rise and... the inequality of it is just staggering. Just another couple of thousand rich investors getting richer while the existing community gets priced out. Exactly. It's not even just about the pricing. Where do you put these people if they do get priced out? The council housing list for London is like trying to win the lottery. It's absurd. And the politicians? They just seem to be overwhelmed by it all, and even when they have good intentions, they almost always seem to be just tinkering around the edges. I know, and it feels like no one's really looking at the larger picture anymore.

So, how was the first weekend at nursery for Emily?? We've been thinking so much about how she's been doing. Oh, it went really well! She had a few tears on the first day, but the nursery staff were great and by the end of the week, she was chatting and playing with the other children. I'm so proud of her, she's been adjusting so quickly! That's wonderful to hear! And how are you coping with everything, going back to work soon and all that? It's a bit overwhelming, to be honest. I'm trying to get everything ready before I go back – enrolling for daycare for Amy, reorganizing my schedule... it feels like I have so much to do. But I'll get there, I guess. At least when I'm at home, Emily's already adjusted well to nursery. I know you will! You're already juggling so much with looking after Emily and also handling your studies. Make sure you take care of yourself too. Yeah, I've been trying to make time for exercise and stuff like that, but it's not always easy. We were talking about planning a holiday this summer though when you’re back from your gardening break. Where should we go? Oh, I’d love to go somewhere relaxing. We could maybe look at a few places in the countryside? Maybe the Lake District again or spend some time by the coast? Yeah, I love those ideas. Also, have you considered weaning off breastfeeding? I know it’s a personal choice but with you working and me here more often, it doesn’t feel ideal that she’s still reliant on me for feeds when I’m babysitting. But it’s also a natural stage. We can start gradually and see how it goes. You aren’t alone in this by any means. We can make it work for both of you. That’s reassuring, thanks. And tell me about last night! You sent a funny show clip from something and I’ve been laughing about it. Got any more of those? Oh yeah, I love those Saturday Night Live sketches.

So, how was everyone's day? Mine was alright. Got a bit of a stressful situation at work today. We're trying to raise funds for the local youth center and there are a lot of administrative hurdles to jump. That must be tough, but it's for a good cause. Yes, and it's something close to my heart. Still, it can be draining at times. I actually got a call from EE today about my phone bill. They've miscalculated something and keeps coming up with a different amount each time. Oh, that's frustrating. EE can be quite tough to deal with at times. Yes, they've promised to look into it, but it's been happening for weeks. Yeah, I've had similar issues with my company's phone plan. It’s always something or the other. Have you all thought about looking for alternatives? Maybe a different provider? I was thinking about that. But switching over seems like a lot of hassle right now. Yeah, maybe we should look into this together. One of you might find a better deal than I would. I’ve been with EE for years and never really thought of looking elsewhere. Yeah, that’s a good idea. We could compare the costs and plans. It’s always good to explore options. Definitely. I'd be glad to look into it. And in other news, I need to go give a statement to the police next week about that local vandalism they're investigating. Just a routine thing, but I'm a bit anxious about it. That doesn’t sound like fun, but it’s important to contribute if you can. And you’ve probably dealt with similar situations in your role as a fund raiser. Yeah, I'd be nervous too but it's for a good reason. Do you know what they'll be asking for? They just wanted a firsthand view of the area that was affected. You know, if I noticed anything unusual around the time of the incident. Well, I hope it’s straightforward. Sometimes these things can be quite invasive. It shouldn’t be too much trouble. Just a straightforward account of what I’ve observed. Do you think it’s going to be at the station or can we give a statement here? They said they’ll arrange for someone to come here. That’s a relief.

Yo, man, welcome back to Bedford. How was the wedding? It was chill, you know. Whole celebration was a blast. But, deep down, I was thinking, man, who knows how long ANON is gonna make it with his new wife now? Oh, come on now. You’re not one for the whole, “early deaths of historical figures” angle, right? Nah, man, you’re getting me all wrong. I was thinking more about how even Spartacus, who was a total boss, only made it to 32 before getting brutally fucked up. Well, at least ANON wasn’t leading a rebellion and fighting to the death. But, you’re right, in Roman times, your 30s were considered old age, so... Exactly! So, you never know when you might be looking for a nice souvenir, and next thing you know, you’re out. Right? But, on a lighter note, did you catch that new TV show that’s like a mix between a historical drama and a Forged in Fire episode? Oh, you mean that show that tried to recreate the life and times of... Exactly! The one with all the weird weapons and mortars and pestles, right? It’s like, imagine using a mortar and pestle for a duel. Now, that would be one way to grind your spices... violently. But you know what would actually be cool? If there was a cooking show that used ancient Roman cooking techniques. Man, the herbs and spices they would use! Actually, that kind of makes me want to experiment with some Roman recipes. Maybe a chickpea and herb stew? Now, that’s a thought. I once tried making pesto with a mortar and pestle, but it was backbreaking work. Exactly! But, food aside, I heard ANON’s wife is into her teas? Yeah, she’s all about these fancy herbal teas. I had no idea about all these different types. I mean, I always thought tea was just... well, tea. Same. I thought tea was either English breakfast or green. But nah, there’s like a whole world out there, including some that might even protect you from malaria or sea lice. Sea lice protection tea. Someone should invent that. You know, we could even start a tea company. “Bedford’s Historic Herbs: Romans Used It, So Should You.” “As used by Spartacus and his crew.” Exactly! We’d at least get some fun with the marketing, even if the tea doesn’t actually do anything.

So, I hear that Cassie's practicing her cello pretty hard for the upcoming orchestra recital. You know how competitive she is. Oh, yeah. She's really worried because she missed out on a key part in the violins for once because she was away the weekend before. Yeah, I've seen her playing and she's seriously improving, but the pressure of getting into the wind-band must be intense. Also, have you started the art project? We need to get that finished before it's due for the end of the term. Honestly? I haven't even opened my sketchbook yet. Perfect, and then I can take pictures to show in the class. How about you pull out the materials, and I’ll get my ideas down? Deal. And while we're at it, have you started studying for the English test tomorrow? Not really, but we could use this afternoon to go over the most important parts. We often struggle with those verbs, but quizzing each other could make it easier to remember. Yeah, it's a bit more fun than just reading them over. Absolutely. Plus, it takes so much less time. And speaking of fun, did you hear about what happened during the hallway between classes today? No, what happened? Well, you know that new girl, Emily? She apparently tripped over her own feet during passing and then, when she was getting up, she accidentally knocked over a whole book rack. Oh... I saw that. So embarrassing... for her. Yeah, but she just picked up the books and kept walking, so I guess she’s okay.

Ah, marvellous to see you both again! How's things? All good thanks! Just about to start Sixth Form, can't believe it's the last year of compulsory education. Yes, the time just flies, doesn’t it? You'll be on to A-Levels before you know it. Which subjects did you choose, eh? I'm doing Maths, English, and History, actually looking forward to it. Oh, I always liked History, it's so full of stories. Reminds me of my school days, although, sadly, educational standards have seemed to have dropped a bit in recent years. Well, from what I've seen, they're still pushing for good results among the kids. It's the funding and resources that need a boost - oh, and the well-being of the staff, of course! Exactly! It's all about the money as much as anything. You can have all the best teachers, but if you can't pay them properly and provide them with the right tools for the job… Yeah, and the emphasis on technology this side of things is quite different than what I remember from when you were teaching. Indeed, it's a challenge for sure. I remember when the biggest tech problem was a faulty overhead projector! Now it's laptops, tablets, and whatever. But it's important to keep up, isn't it? Absolutely, it's good for engagement and can bring new approaches into teaching. But it also means we’re always worried about the budget for updating equipment and training staff. Speaking of things that are important but often underfunded, how are you finding the new food technology scheme at school? I know some schools have been trying to do things the healthy way. We do have decent options, like fruit and salad, but it’s not as fun as the occasional pasta or chips. It's about making healthy choices accessible and appetizing for kids, you see. But also teaching them about where their food comes from and cooking basics. Definitely. I try to make sure we do some cooking together at home, just because it's a good skill and we can make better choices for ourselves if we know what we're doing. Again, health and wellness have become a bigger deal in school too. There's more focus on mental health and getting kids involved in sports. I started playing football again this year.

So, I was browsing on the news yesterday and came across an article about how more and more people are driving more recklessly due to mobile phone usage. I don't know, but it seems the number of car accidents due to distraction caused by mobile phones really seems to be on the rise, and it’s quite alarming – do you have any thoughts on this? Absolutely, and it’s not just mobile phones. You see, I was out on a job and right in the middle of a busy street, there was this young woman texting away without even looking up from her phone. She didn’t even notice when she nearly ran over someone crossing the road. It was such a close call. Oh, I’m sure you’re right. But then again, I think there is also an element of increased car ownership and the roads getting busier. People also seem to be driving larger vehicles that might give them a false sense of security. I think you’re onto something there. But speaking of cars and how we use them, I recently read something that links increased car usage to issues like obesity. Since owning a car allows people to avoid walking or cycling or even just taking the bus, it leads to this sedentary lifestyle. It’s quite astonishing how lifestyle choices like these can have broad societal implications. That’s very true. You see, when I was in London, the main commute was public transport - the bus or the tube. Now, people have become accustomed to using their cars for every little task, which is perhaps one of the reasons why we’re facing an obesity epidemic. Exactly! For instance, when I was a child, we’d always walk or cycle to school. Now, it seems most kids get a lift from their parents the moment they can’t even see the school from their window. Maybe it’s the combination of less outdoor play and More screen time together that’s a contributing factor, isn’t it? Yes, definitely. But coming back to driving, personally, I find it interesting that cultural and religious beliefs also influence transport choices. I read somewhere that in certain communities where owning a car is seen as a symbol of status, people overlook more sustainable options for these social reasons alone. That’s quite insightful, isn’t it? And it doesn’t end there.

So, I've been trying to figure out how to use Moodle better. I want to learn how to create interactive quizzes and embedding videos. Oh, Moodle! I've used it for years. It's indispensable for online teaching. Really? It feels so clunky to me. Do you have any tips on how to make it more convenient or user-friendly? Well, it was clunky when I first started too. But it really depends on what you want to do. For quizzes, you can use the standard quiz activity, but if you want something more interactive, you can check out H5P. H5P? Yes, it's a plugin that you can add in Moodle. It lets you create interactive content like quizzes that are fun for students and give immediate feedback. That sounds perfect. How do I get it? First, you need to make sure that your Moodle site has it installed. It's usually done by the IT team at the university or the system administrator. If it's not installed, you can usually just request it from them. That might take a bit. Alternatively, if it's a private site or if you have a lot of control over it, you can install it yourself. There's an official Moodle plugin repository where you can find and install H5P. Oh, good to know. And in terms of embedding videos? For videos, there are a few ways to do it. First, you can upload a video directly to Moodle. It supports various formats, but I always recommend converting videos to MP4 to make them more compatible. Right, less stress on the server. Exactly, less stress, fewer compatibility issues. The other way is to host the video somewhere else, like YouTube or Vimeo, and just embed it in Moodle using the embed code provided by those sites. That’s a good idea. Plus, with YouTube, for example, you have a lot of control over privacy settings and so on. That makes sense. And for interactive elements, don’t forget about the Labels and HTML modules within Moodle. They are very flexible and you can embed pretty much anything you need. Very helpful. This is really useful. I'm glad you found it useful. It took me a while to get used to Moodle too, but over time, I've learned a lot of tricks that make it much more enjoyable. I really appreciate your help.

So, I thought we could go see that performance at the theater's upcoming production. They're doing a local performance of "Romeo and Juliet". I think it would be a nice little outing for both of us. Oh really? That sounds great. I must admit, after all the traveling for work, I'm kind of looking for something to do and relax. But do you think the baby won't be too much to handle? I mean, she's still young. Ah, absolutely. We can set it for a time that works keeps her nap schedule in mind. That way, she'll probably just sleep through some of it. Plus, there's always the possibility of finding someone to watch her if we both are really keen. Might just do that then. How about Sunday evening? I read that the matinee is at 2:30 PM and the evening performance is at 7:00 PM? Yes, Sunday's looking good. Since she naps around 2-4 PM, maybe we should go for the evening show if it's quieter afterward. Also, I can check their website to see if they have any accommodations for parents with toddlers. That would be helpful. And if not, we could always just stay vigilant and know that we might need to excuse ourselves if it gets too rowdy. Right, we can't expect too much. She's still at that stage where one minute she's the most well-behaved child in the world and the next... [laughs] The terrible twos are round the corner. No doubt. But hey, it's a window into the hell that parents face the world over. [both chuckle] Speaking of windows... I've been trying to handle this recurring jetlag of mine, and it's making me just want to sleep all the time. I noticed last year that whenever I travel for work, I come back and it takes me about 4-5 days to adjust. Yep, jetlag sure can be a pain. I've tried a few things to help – maintaining a consistent sleep schedule pre-travel, adjusting bedtime by an hour or two each day when I get back, trying to stay active during the day but not too close to bedtime... Did you use any specific apps or tools? Actually, yes. I used an app called Timeshifter, it's quite personalized. It gives you a plan based on your travel and sleep habits.

So, I hear you’re planning on moving to Libya soon, Kamal. How’s that coming along? It’s been a bureaucratic nightmare, but I think it’s finally progressing. The visa application process is quite challenging, isn't it? Absolutely, especially for someone like you with connections outside of Libya isn’t it? I remember my colleague tried to move there a few years back and it took him months just to get the right paperwork sorted. Exactly! It feels like they’re always looking for an excuse to get out of issuing a visa. But, I’ve got to say, the politics of oil there have always fascinated me. It's such a dynamic sector and I believe it has a lot of potential for development, despite the chaos. Interesting. You're in petroleum engineering, right? It’s a field we need more people to consider here in the UK. But I can see how it’s different there with such rich resources. Yes, very different. Working there would allow me to build on my skills while contributing to something significant. Plus, it’s a bit unsettling relying on what the government here has to say about oil. We know how it all works, don’t we? True. Where politics and oil meet can get messy anywhere. But don't the Wahabi’s make life interesting up there? They do. It’s a part of the landscape for sure. But, to be honest, my focus is more on the work and the possibilities for making a positive change, than really getting caught up in the religious or political factions. We all know how that can go over there. Wise move. Going into it with a bit of the 'I'm here to work and contribute' attitude, rather than diving into the complex politics. I can only imagine how the young people there view all this - do they feel a connection to the rest of the world or are they more isolated now? It’s a mix, really. The younger generation, especially those with access to education and internet, are a bit more connected. But, sure, there is an isolation sense due to all the restrictions. However, there’s also a lot of eager young people wanting to learn, work, and see the world, same as anywhere. That’s good to hear. Isolation can breed all sorts of negative attitudes, and it’s heartening to know there are still those wanting to reach out and engage.

So, I thought we could keep the conversation to more social or mundane topics for tonight. You know, just to avoid any serious talk about work or health issues? Absolutely, sounds good to me. We can discuss the usual everyday stuff. How was the lamb, by the way? Really good, wasn’t it? Oh, it was lovely, and the mint sauce was a nice touch. Mint sauce, actually, that reminds me I bought some Scottish tablet for everyone. It’s a bit like fudge, right? Yes, it is! I’ve had that before. It was great. Mmm, and I’ve been wanting to go on a cruise. Might just book one next year. Really? You haven’t started planning or anything? Not yet. Just started fantasizing about it. It's been so long since I had a proper holiday. That sounds very relaxing. Speaking of relaxing, have either of you started these workout challenges on TV? I started one last month. It’s been alright. Kinda makes me feel productive this time of year, you know? Oh, I’ve been dilly-dallying on that. I might try joining in. Good excuse to get moving more often. I’ve also started bringing Elsa to local parks more. It’s been really nice to get some fresh air. Ah, dogs are the best! They keep us really active. Speaking of which, we should also discuss the plans for her vaccinations. Yes, absolutely. I’ll look into it. How are things with your landlord, by the way? Any issues? We’re actually planning to look for a new property. Can’t stand the current one. Our landlord won’t fix anything. We’re considering selling Mum’s flat. It’s been a bit of a headache sorting out issues with the ins and outs, but we should probably make a decision soon. That’s a big decision. Yeah but I think we’ve put it off long enough. Either way, it means sorting out so much paperwork. It does. And of course, all the memories that come along with it. It’s just a lot to handle, I know. Yeah, and it feels like just another thing on the list of adults. For sure. But I suppose that’s part of what being an adult is often like—dealing with all these... Responsibilities? Exactly. Anyway, I really enjoy these relaxed times though. They keep me sane.

Yo, mate, did you manage to sort out that beans on toast thing? Aye, what's wrong with my beans on toast? Oh, it was just a joke, sorry. You know, we're all hungry after that long day. Hehe, questions are always asked when bellies are involved. Right, well, I did make beans on toast. Not fancy, but it's food. Yeah, food is food. But I was actually thinking more about dinner plans. Think we should cook something proper tonight? Something proper would be great. I've been craving proper chips with everything. Chips with everything? You know we can't have proper chips around here. Everyone would want to move in. True. And the flat's too small to properly have guests over for a proper meal, anyway. True, but man, sometimes I miss home proper food. Back in Whitehaven, my mum used to make the tastiest fish and chips. I never even tried fish and chips until I was about 16. You and #homegrown Whitehaven boys always making me feel left out with your seafood talk. You need to try some proper chips with Stamp at the harbour, then you'll understand. Stamp's got the best chips in town, no arguing. But I'd take home comforts over visiting restaurants any day now. Yeah, but sometimes you just want to be taken care of a bit, you know? To sit down and have someone else cook doesn't sound bad. We can plan that. After we're done with our degrees, we can do all the fancy dinners in style. Right, right, worry about that after final year. For now, let's focus on not having to eat beans on toast for another week. Yes, that's a great long-term plan. Meanwhile, we should probably make dinner happen. What do we have? Let's see... bread, cheese – I know it’s not chips, but... Cheese toasties! Proper Whitehaven stuffing. And maybe we can heat up that Chinese takeaway from last night. It was good the first night. Good idea. I'll get the cheese out. And I'll grab the bread. And I'll heat up the leftovers. You know what would be nice? If we could have this with some... proper conversation. You know, not about work or uni or all that stuff. I’d love that. Just hang and talk about whatever. Yeah, like, our favorite childhood stories or something.

Right okay so I need your help. I'm supposed to bake something for my class but today's the due date. Well don't panic, we can do this. What kind of baking do you need to do? Did the teacher say anything about what kind of cake or cookies or ?? She said it could be anything but she really loves themed lessons. So I thought of a Harry Potter themed cake or cookies. Mm, that sounds just like the Chocolate Frog from the book. Wait, can we also add golden snitches? They’re so easy to make and look so magical. Yes, we could, but how do we shape them? Do we have the right ingredients? Don’t worry about it. We can make these with rice paper and gold or yellow sugar. Oh, that sounds fun! I can help make these. That would be great! I can set up different stations, each related to a different book from the series, and they have to solve puzzles to progress through the room. That sounds like it would be so much fun! Yeah, you could include things like decoding messages or figuring out potions. Exactly, and it’s all a bit like the challenges Harry and his friends faced.
