While you’re dealing with the guitar and Oisin, I was thinking we could plan a day out to try out some Ramen. Ramen! Ramen! That’s a great idea. Maybe we can fit that in after the show this weekend. It’s good family bonding. And who knows, maybe we can sneak in some ice cream afterward. I was thinking about that too. We could even make it a picnic if the weather’s good. Picnic! Ice cream! And while we’re planning fun days out, maybe it’s time for Oisin to get some new clothes. His trousers are getting really short on him. Good point. Skinny jeans are in, but mostly youth sizes, I think, right? Yes, and trust me, it’ll make him so much more comfortable. No skinny! No skinny, unless they’re soft and comfortable, like slippers.

Remember that gardening set? Oh gods yes. The poor old thing was always getting lost and causing messes around the house, wouldn’t it? Right! And remember Bako? Oh yes! Oh my days. Bako and his little block buddy and the construction theme. We spent hours creating roads, buildings and sometimes even our own little towns. All very meticulous with our tiny plastic trucks and everything right? Yeah, meticulous. I was always the one who would spend hours creating the little roads, and I used to get so fed up when my sister would just like smash them up with her big feet. Ah yes! I remember. She was never very careful with our things. But we had the best time playing with them. It's weird how when we were kids, we didn't spend a thought on the possible financial value or whatever these things might have now though. For sure! We were just kids. It was all about imagination. These days the kids just play on those tablets and all, while we argue about how to tidy the cupboard. It’s interesting how time changes us, right? Absolutely. But hey, nice weather today, isn’t it? It is isn’t it? Makes all this tidying out feel a bit more bearable. We might actually get some fresh air and do some gardening like we used to… in our dreams! Perhaps we could use some of that enthusiasm we had when playing with the gardening set. Though less getting side-tracked, maybe! True. I used to wander around pretending to plant flowers when I should have been helping. Oh, but we should! We could benefit from some fresh air. We could sit on the back step and… maybe lay out a bit more of those old blocks and teach the grandkids about them. That would be so much fun. I’m sure they’d find it quaint! It would be nice to have something physical and tangible to play with. Not just screens and games. As if they’d want to play with blocks! But it’s the thought that counts. It’s not so much about what they do with it as it is about the joy they find in exploring this ‘ancient’ form of play. Exactly. Maybe if we tidy this cupboard, we could even find the gardening set or some Bako blocks from the attic and surprise them.

I keep reading that if you've got any plant that releases citronella; it's supposed to be a deterrent for mosquitoes. Yeah well I don't think anything can deter the mosquitoes here. Oh, that's the best part.

All that light and all that fluff You could get a knife and cut it in two D'ya like clouds, d'ya like cool nights and electric signs All that light and all that fluff Perfect, perfect execution! Film! --- Please note that this conversation is meant to be representative of what a family might discuss while around a dinner table with a toddler acting out their own 'performance' of a popular song.

Oh, did I ever tell you about's ANON story? No, what happened? You know, one lazy Sunday. ANON just decided to sleep in his pants. He must have had his reasons, but I don’t think they were terribly wise. Oh, dear lord, I can just imagine the look on his face when he woke up! This is going to be good! What happened next? Was he embarrassed or did he just get lazy about changing? Keep going, let’s hear it! Please? So, ANON wakes up and realizes he’s in his pants, under the covers. And guess what? He thought it was a brilliant idea to simply roll out of bed and head downstairs still in his... pants. Unbelievable. The rest of us had to play it cool. ‘Good morning, ANON. Sleep well?’ He must have thought we were all blind or something, 'cause he replied back, all nonchalantly, ‘Yeah, just a bit chilly last night, didn’t even bother getting dressed.’ He didn’t change?! Until his mom, bless her, just had to point it out. ‘ANON, dear, you do know you weren’t meant to...’ And then he just casually chuckled and said, ‘Oh, really? Must’ve slipped my mind!’ You’ve got to admire his… confidence? Yeah, for sure. I mean, we all have our lazy moments, but this one’s a story for the ages! This needs to be one of those family jokes we never forget. Absolutely! And you know, it made us all think. What if we extend the house out back? Maybe a little reading nook with a window just so ANON could sleep there for hours on end? We could even call it... The Lazy Pants Library? That’s brilliant! A library? Like, with books? Yeah, if he’s going to sleep in his pants, he might as well have a library to do it properly. Maybe some audiobooks, so he doesn’t have to even wake up to choose what to listen to. You’re thinking ahead, I see. A lazy person’s dream, really. Honestly, if we do extend the house, it could be really useful for us too. More space for everyone, maybe a cozy corner for reading or just hanging out. Yeah, and maybe a little sleepover area for when friends come over, so they can join in on the lazy pants reading sessions? Well, let’s not jump into too many more details just yet.

Ah, Professor Evans, I've heard of that latest grant from the Royal Society. Quite impressive. How's that research project coming along? Thanks, Professor Milton. It's going quite well. The preliminary results are promising. We're looking to submit the full proposal soon. Impressive indeed. I've been working on clearing out the old house for my wife and the struggle with getting a simple bid for some decent windows makes me appreciate your challenges with funding. Ah, home decorating and academic funding—the pursuits that never keeps money backwards. I'm actually working on a bit of decor myself. Trying to find those perfect Italian tiles for our bathroom. Italian tiles, you say? Did you hear about the new coffee beans from Italy that the university is considering for the canteen? They're supposed to be from a specific region that grows the cherries on well-drained volcanic slopes. It sounds almost as meticulous as your research, if you ask me. Indeed, I did. But have you heard about the ridiculous bill from our water company? They claim it was because of an old leak in the piping, which I suspect took place under the previous owner. A leak, you say? I bet it's been leaking as much water as the Hadron collider leaks funding. I once tried to explain the merits of the Hadron collider over a pint to a friend, but it was like trying to teach quantum physics to a wall. I'd take that over trying to understand why our water bills skyrocket in price any time it rains. Speaking of things we’re trying to understand—the science behind humanity’s fascination with overcomplicating simple problems is a socio-linguistic study waiting to happen. Indeed. Just last weekend, I helped my son with his homework and one question was "Why the Hadron Collider was built." The answer was as simple as "To understand the basic structure of particles." But explaining that in a way he could remember was as complex as trying to explain why we can't get reliable internet in our homes. Perhaps changing the world byte by byte calls for simpler answers. Like, "To find new coffee beans."  laughs  Well, I suppose if we're talking about simplifying our lives, perhaps we should discuss over a cup of coffee rather than a grant proposal. Speaking of which, would either of you be interested in joining me for an alternative source of coffee beans in the form of a socially responsible roaster I’ve discovered?

Right okay so I think it's time we sorted out the Lego. It's been getting so messy every time you and Alex play. But I like messy! Why can't we just play? Hi Emma, isn't it time now? Ah yes, it is now. You see, if we sort out and organize the Lego, next time you and Alex want to play, you'll know right where to find everything and it'll be easier. And we could make more things! Oh, we could, yes. Daddy was saying we might have to check for any broken pieces, too. Exactly. We want to make sure it's all good to use. Do you want to help us sort them out by colours or maybe by what each Lego set is? I want to sort by colours, I love red and yellow! Me too, blue and green are my favourite though. Alright, we'll sort by colours then. And remember, if any pieces are broken, we put them on the side so we can fix or replace them if we can. Where should we put the finished sets? In their own boxes like in the picture? Yep, like the picture. That way, they keep nice and tidy and we know which set is which. "Turtle power to the Lego sorting!" That's right, turtle power doesn't come in disorganized Lego piles. What about finding the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtle set? I want to make the Turtles. We'll make sure that set is easy to find. Maybe we can even make a Lego Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtle city or something. Yeah! And we can use a green base plate for the sewers. And we can use blue for water – I know because they swim in the sewers sometimes. Perfect, let's start with collecting all the green pieces for the Turtles first then. We could even make Leo, Donnie, Raph, and Mikey! Definitely we can do that. Do you two remember how to follow the instructions to make specific sets too or do you mostly like to build from your imagination? Sometimes I follow instructions, especially for new sets. But with old sets, I build any way I like. Me too! I like to build my own stuff most of the time. That's a great way to do it. Remember though, if you're building something new and get stuck, the instructions can help a lot.

So, how was your holiday? It's been great, but today's been a bit of a slog after all the relaxing. I've been deep into this new chicken recipe, and well, let's just say I've managed to squeeze in almost no other activities, including replying to those emails – do you have any idea how long it takes me to get back into the rhythm of work? Haha, that makes two of us – I've actually been marinating a steak for tonight. Our very own home-away-from-home get-together right here in this kitchen. Oh, that sounds lovely. Tell me, anything exciting come up at work since I’ve been away? Yeah, actually. We just had a Sports Day happening – among adults, you read that right. It was oddly invigorating. And the summer fair that organization gave a hand in was wonderful. It's amazing how much you can learn about people when you see them in a different light... or in this case, in a different field. That's quite the shift. I've been dealing with a lot of... well, let's say this new team on my ward has been a learning curve. It’s different working in the mental health sector during this time of year, the season can really affect patients. Speaking of which, I met up with Emily last week at that new café on the high street. You know, the one that opened up where that old bookstore used to be? It was actually quite nice, much better atmosphere than expected. Yeah, I saw they were getting it decorated over the weekend. I might have to check it out soon. Oh, definitely. Their cakes are supposed to be amazing, and I could use a break from cooking myself for a bit. Speaking of which, I made this fruit salad for the family dinner. Do you think I overdid it on the oranges? Not really, it’s nice but we should probably keep some for the week. You sure know how to use up our fruit stash. Thanks for saving me. You're welcome! Anyway, did you manage to run at all while you were away? Yeah, cleared my head, and it felt good. How about you? Did you keep up with the gym? Uh, I tried. I started reading about that new workout trend but then just... Honestly, I’ve been too busy just enjoying company and food to worry about that.

Right okay now I know this weekend might've been a bit brash with all these grandparents visiting so let's just talk about how we'll manage things from now on? Yeah, I mean I don't want to be rude but it's been a bit much now, the mess, the noise... Aye, and don't forget the house cleaning! Oh now dear, we've not ruin things have we? I'd be upset if we had. You haven't, it's just when you both have your parents here we usually try to keep to a routine. Like with the baths and the food, and I've been worried you've been under too much pressure. Well, we've done our best. But when your mother and I are here we bring a bit of...different pace you might say. Aye, and your mum's always looking for a laugh, can't very well refuse. Right, no problem there. But this weekend it's been a lot of noise at night and I or Dad have had to miss our favorite TV show this morning because we were helping prepare breakfast for both of you. I'm sure we can figure something out. Like maybe we can alternate weekends so it's not both at the same time? Or we make sure we have a bit more time for your normal routine without so much interruption? Yeah, maybe that could work. Like sometimes in school we have really busy weeks and then quiet ones so we can catch up. Maybe something like that. That sounds like a good idea. But it's good to see the lads, they're growin' so quick, and I do enjoy the time with them. More than they do, probably. Speaking of which, is it okay if I ask for a bit more space next time they visit? Like maybe Dad and I could sit with you in the kitchen for a bit after dinner? Of course, that's a great idea. We can build that into the schedule for sure. Ah! A proper evening so we can swap tales and all that. That would be grand. You could even show us more about these games you play, the new ones you've got. I hear they're full of little creatures running about. Yeah, sometimes. But they're fun. And sometimes it's fun to watch something on TV together, like old movies or shows that you... don't watch anymore.

So, I was thinking about what we could watch tonight and I thought about Peter Pan. You kids like him, right? Yeah! Peter Pan and Tinkerbell! I love them! They fly and fight pirates! Yeah! Especially Captain Hook! He’s so mean, but funny. Exactly! Peter Pan is so brave and Tinkerbell is super kind, but a little mischievous sometimes. And Tinkerbell never gets older, right? That’s cool. Right, exactly. That’s a magical part of the stories. They never grow up, which means they always have fun adventures. Do they ever live with Wendy and the boys in London? Yes, that’s what happened in the original story. They live in Neverland but also go to London to visit Wendy and her brothers. Can you explain why they're always fighting Captain Hook? Well, Peter Pan is like a protector of Neverland and Captain Hook is his main enemy. He tries to stop Peter and take over the island. And he cuts off Peter’s hand and it gets replaced with a hook, right? That’s right. And the most exciting part is when they have the great sea battle. They use ships and swords; it’s quite dramatic. And Tinkerbell is always making things magical, right? Like she makes Peter fly or helps them hide. Yes! Tinkerbell is very important. She’s really good with magic and helps Peter and the Lost Boys all the time. I like how in Pan they show that Peter was actually a real boy who was taken to Neverland, but then they made it into a film with action and flying. Right! And he fights with swords and has lots of adventure! Pan is a fun way to look at the story. It’s more action-packed but still has the core characters and themes. But in the classic story, Peter Pan is more carefree, right? Not so much action, but more about adventure and fun. Right. In Peter and Wendy, it’s more about the idea of never growing up and the fun of being a kid forever. Can we watch the movie where they fly over London and go to Neverland? Maybe we can watch that version next time we want to, but for tonight, how about the 2003 Peter Pan with Jeremy Sumpter? That sounds great! We haven’t seen that one yet. Yay! Let’s do that then!

Alright so I remember when first move's here we had our house in Ilfracombe. You boys were about six and eight then, right? That old Victorian house, you remember? You two used to love playing out in the back garden. Oh, yeah! That was back when we'd have to drive past the clock tower every day and you'd have to get out and wind it up before we headed to school. Oh, yes! That was a ritual. But even with how lovely that house was, nothing beats this town. Devon has really stolen our hearts, hasn't it? Even with commutes to Taunton for work. It sure has. Devon’s just a nicer pace to live, but sometimes the journey to Taunton can be a real grind. Grind indeed! 1.5 hours each way, most days, I'd say. But with family here and a community, it's worth it. Though, when we first moved here, we thought we'd spend more time in Taunton and less in Devon, didn't we? How has that turned out? We certainly envisioned more work-related balance initially. But as time's gone on, we've kind of assumed Devon as the 'base' home. Work in Taunton still, but the heart is here, really. Well, technology has certainly helped make that balance possible. Like, my Zoom meetings are significantly easier than dealing with the old commute in bad weather. Oh, the joys of 'informal Zoom meetings’ when the internet doesn’t cooperate in bad Devon weather. True story. Except, we've been lucky with weather here lately. And let's not forget about those lovely sleep patterns, right? No more 5AM alarms. That's one thing we've all loved. Just hearing the silence or the birds instead of traffic. And we should talk about Christmas plans. You've checked if we're making time for a house warming party after Christmas? We promised a bunch of old friends from Ilfracombe and Taunton. Absolutely. I've tentatively set up one for the 28th of December. We can show off the new place. That'll be lovely. With the boys going off soon, we should have some time. I was thinking about inviting my old work colleagues as well. That’s a great idea. We'll make sure it's fun for everyone. And maybe this time, we can really enjoy some time with our family without any big projects or chores looming over us.

Oh, did I find you first or did you have eyes on me? Well, I think we both saw each other, and well, you were right there, so I figured I'd ask you. Ah, excellent. I'm glad you didn't hesitate. We could use a break and a chat. Say, are you working on the track today as part of a working party of some sort? Yes, that's right. It's always good to keeps things in shape alongside a bit of hands-on work for my community. I can see that. Looks like hard work. I was going through some old files back at my place today. Might have been related to a massage service. Ah, a massage service? That sounds interesting. Yeah, it was a Swedish massage centre. My wife did a stint working there a few years back. It was quite... enlightening, in many respects. The focus on relaxation and well-being, it struck me. Especially when juxtaposed against the stress of modern life and the lack of proper healthcare. Oh, absolutely. We see that a lot in our line of work as well, with the nursing and healthcare professionals often needing support themselves. Yes. In fact, at the hospice we were involved with, we noticed a lot of practitioners were carrying quite a physical toll for their work. A nice massage can make all the difference, right? Indeed. It's a shame really, with all the technological advancements we have and all, but humanity's wellness often falls through the cracks. But it's not just about the physical burden. As an artist, and before that, in my antique dealing, I've seen how people find the therapeutic or creative outlets to be truly healing. Now, speaking of healing and wellness, it brings me to a different line of thought. My granddaughter is quite involved with nursery education these days, really pushing for more integrated health and emotional intelligence programs for kids. That’s fantastic. It's such a crucial time – setting the foundation for these kids. Makes you think of the whole concept of raising balanced individuals. Exactly! And it’s not just the kids; female equality in the workplace still has a way to go. I often used to almost unintentionally use 'he' and 'him' when referring to people in general when discussing work or groups, until it was pointed out to me.

Mum, I was thinking about what we could do for the upcoming holiday. Do you want me to start looking into some options? Well, haven't talked about that yet. What are you thinking? Are you still keen on the usual lazy time at the beach or do you want to try something new? I'd like to try something new actually. But considering our budget, I thought maybe we could go to Cornwall again. I've heard there are some nice places where we could hike and enjoy the local produce. Cornwall is lovely. Think about Padstow. You'll love it if you're into seafood and there's nice coastal paths for your hiking. Or perhaps we could go to Dartmoor? It's not that far from here. Dartmoor is a good idea but from what I remember, the campsites can fill up quickly. True, but we could also look at B&Bs or self-catering places. Let's have a look at those options too. What about food? I know it's often a problem when on holiday isn't it? Sometimes you end up eating out too much which can get expensive. True, that's why I thought about Cornwall again as we could buy fresh seafood and maybe do some self-catering. That sounds like a plan to me. Another thing we can consider is the time of year we go. Right, less tourist months could be cheaper, yes. Considering our tight budget, we should book as early as possible. Agreed. What do you think about maybe the second half of September? It might be less crowded, and the weather should still be okay. September could work, but I do want to check one more thing. Are the schools or any clubs or community groups you're involved in having a schedule or event around that time? Good point. I'll check my schedule but I don't have anything major planned for that time. Because I want to make sure we don't miss on my end if there's a peak teaching week or a family event that I need to attend. Got it, I'll send over my schedule as soon as I can. Can we also think about the transportation? I was thinking about perhaps hiring a car if we decide on a self-catering place or somewhere a bit off the beaten path.

Yo, I got my bank statement yesterday. Thought you might be interested. I've been getting into some investments lately. Nice one! I talked to my cousin the other day and he said he's doing well with his stocks. Exactly! That's why I decided to try some of it myself. You remember that one football match last week? Yeah, that was wild! Both teams played right at the edge, and I had a few bets going on it. Me too! Think about it, if both teams get really invested, players, and fans. Like Ronaldo, I heard he's planning to retire soon. Really? That's sad. He's still got it, even at his age. Yeah, but even the best have to hang up their boots someday. Speaking of which, did you watch any of the Women's Euro 2022? Yeah, got to watch a couple of matches. The skills on display were insane. It's crazy how far women's sports have come in recent years, especially football. Absolutely. Despite all the progress, there's still that pay gap in the sport. I read an article about that, the figures are staggering. True. I think it's also about perception and exposure. As more people watch and support, the more attention and sponsors they'll get. Definitely. It's a snowball effect. Speaking of perception, have you seen any of the new videos of Chris Bosh? Nah, doesn’t come up in my feed. Last I heard, he's focusing more on business after the NBA. Yeah, I saw him do an interview about his transition into side hustles, pretty interesting. He mentioned something about mentoring younger players and investing. Ah, okay. That's smart move, getting into mentorship and investing. Gives back to the sport while diversifying earnings. You hit the nail on the head. It's a model more athletes should consider for long-term success after their playing days. That kind of foresight is key, especially for sports like cricket where the career span can be quite short. Agreed. Cricket's almost brutal in that regard. Look at the care job I put into my 8. I scored a ducat there. Nice. Always aiming high. I know. You know how my uncle Silas is doing? No, I lost touch after the family gathering last year. Remember? We were all planning a trip together but that got postponed.

I seen them educazhun things on telly ‘bout the globes an’ whatnot. Mind, I never did get to travel much meself, not like some of ‘em do. Yeah, it's all the world’s a stage kind o' attitude, innit? It certainly broadens one’s horizons, doesn’t it? I’ve always loved me own right here, never felt a need to see what’s abroad. Always found plenty to do even if keeps changing backwards and forwards with the seasons. Oh, yes. The gardens! They’re a right bonus when they’re looking their best. I used to love workin' in mine. Might just cos it’s bit easier now. You’re right about that. There’s somethin’ nice about seein’ all your own efforts growin’ before your very eyes, yeh? Absolutely. I remember how our school used to have a little vegetable garden project where we’d spend a few hours a week growing our own food. And those early teen trips or even just sleepovers at the Yorkshire youth hostels. I mean, nothing beats that for learning about teamwork and independence. Oh, those youth hostels! I’ve been to a few of them with the kids at the time. Used to think, why are we sleeping in bunk beds when we’re neither soldiers nor scouts? But it was always an adventure, especially if we got silly and tried to navigate the underground system for sport. That sounds like it’d be fun. I don’t think I’ve ever been on the London Underground. Just too complicated for me. Well, it’s all relative, isn’t it? But the point is about getting out of your comfort zone and seeing new things. Now, speaking of which, we should really consider a trip whenever your leg’s better. Just couple more months and you’ll be up and about, I’m sure. I’m hoping so. It’s been a long sit this time. Can’t wait to get outdoors again – and somewhere hot, if I’m completely selfish for a moment. That’s the spirit! I’ve always said, if you’re going to do something, make it count. And if it’s going to be somewhere hot, perhaps Spain or Portugal? Now, that sounds like a plan. Though, funny thinking back, when I was just startin’ out as a childminder, I often found myself planing more trips and hikes with the kids than my own family would dream of going on.

So, I've been going over the flight options again, and I still have no idea. These prices are just crazy. Tell me about it. It's like every time I book a flight, they somehow manage to find a way to charge more. Exactly! I mean, I've been looking for over an hour and still can't find a decent price. Have you tried searching without set dates yet? Sometimes that can help. Oh, I've tried that. You know what's odd? The price changes based on my location too. If I'm using a VPN in the UK, it's more expensive than if I'm set to a US server. That just doesn't make any sense. Have you tried looking at different airlines' websites directly? Sometimes the prices are cheaper there. Yeah, and then when you actually book, they slip in extra fees for baggage or seat choice. It's like airlines barely make any money on the ticket price anymore. I know, right? I found this one flight that was really cheap, but then I noticed it was with an airline I've never heard of. That's a risk. The airline might not have the best track record. Exactly! I'd rather pay a bit more with a more reliable airline. Maybe you should wait a bit longer. Prices can drop, especially if it's a new route or during the off-season. I'm running out of ideas and patience. You know what might work? If you set up price alerts. There are sites that can notify you when the price drops. That sounds like a great idea. I just tried to set one up for you. Okay, so I'm searching your departure and return dates, and then I'll see if I can get you alerts if and when the price drops below a certain level. You're a lifesaver. Thanks, Anon. No problem. Just for you. While we're at it, should we plan for dinner? It'll give me a break from all this. Good idea. How about we try that new Italian place? I heard the reviews are great. Perfect. Do you want to book a table for us? Let me just get this alert set up first. But yes, we can book a table for later tonight. Sounds good. We can also catch the latest episode of that show we've been watching.

Right okay so I've been keeping an eye on my finances and I've noticed that our main supermarkets are jacking up prices again. This can't be right, can it? Mm, I've noticed that too. I had a look at our weekly shop this morning and the price of fruit and veg has skyrocketed. You remember when one could make a meal for the whole family out of a £5 bag of assorted vegetables? Now you can barely get a decent bag of carrots for that price. Yeah, keeps changing right? I get how it's due to... I don't know, climate, supply chains, but still, it’s rough on us old folks, sticking by our pint of milk and loaf of bread. And have you noticed how even phone service providers are ripping us off? Was it faster before or am I just old making me complain more? No, it's not just you. We've decided as a family to shop around more. Make a note of when prices drop and stock up then. And on phones, yes, it's ridiculous isn’t it? I’ve had calls from my old provider trying to get me to stay, but honestly, they’re giving no incentive at all. The youngsters prefer the flexibility and extra services that the newer providers offer while the rest of us just want something straightforward and reliable. Do we also not just pay more for the convenience of having it all at our fingertips? Ah, the world's gone mad with technology I tell ya, especially with these banking apps making it seem simpler but actually really confusing if you don’t keep up. I know exactly what you mean. Just the other day I tried to transfer money and the app kept saying there’s an issue with the service and offered me to call them. So, I call and it’s an automated service, less helpful than the app was! And the voice quality is terrible. I swear, sometimes I think it's deliberate to prevent real human contact. Deliberate or not, it's changing the world. Speaking of calls, my grandkids can do all sorts of advanced things on their mobiles but if I want to call for a simple customer service query, it's like they take me back to the dark ages. But the customer service aspect...

So, speaking of animals, what did you all think was the weirdest animal you've ever seen? Oh, I was on holidays once in South Africa and saw a meerkat up close. They're so strange looking! And they're almost as tall and curious as guinea pigs but with kind of a face like a turtle? Wow, I've never seen a meerkat live, but my aunt has a farm in Ireland and she once took me to a petting zoo. The cutest thing I saw was a baby owl that was tiny and could fit in the palm of my hand. It kept trying to wrap its talons around my finger and seemed like it was practicing to catch prey. That's so cute! I've seen a seal once down in Penarth. They're so playful and just flop around on the beach like big dogs. And the sounds they make are hilarious. I remember going to the Hartlepool Maritime Conservation Centre and they have these enormous sea turtles. They're so calm and it's like they're floating in syrup it's so slow. Almost contradictory to the way they're supposed to look or act. Speaking of this, it reminds me, what’s everyone's favorite food to eat when we're on holiday? Seafood for me, no matter the place. Whether it's fresh fish in Greece or seafood paella in Spain. Yeah, I love trying local seafood too. But if I'm being honest, I'd take a good curry over anything else. There's a place in Manchester near the university that makes this incredible beef curry. It’s all about the spices and the slow-cooked meat. I'm with you on the curry. There's nothing better than a hot, spicy dish to make you feel all toasty when you come in from the rain or cold. Though, I also grew up eating lots of Irish stew, which isn't exactly exotic, but it's warm and comforting. Oh, and before we dive deep into food, I recently discovered this really good vegan bakery on Broad Street. They have these incredible carrot cakes that are so moist and packed with flavor without being too sweet. Plus, I'm trying to incorporate more vegan and ethical choices in my diet, so it was a win. For me, it's definitely anything with a good Yorkshire pudding and gravy.

Oh, did you finish that first year's art project yet? Yeah, it was such a hassle, I talked about old age and youth and well, that's about it haha! Did the lecturer like it? To be honest, I don’t really know yet. But she gave me some good tips on how to structure the essay that I’ve been using this term, actually. Oh, that's good. Which essay was that? The one about medieval Europe and art, I think it was about the role of religion in art. I’ve always loved computer games with medieval themes, and I used that interest to get into thinking about art through that lens. That's quite unique. So, do you think that project will lead to how you choose your degree properly? I'm not sure, I really do love painting and looking at art history, but... But? What do you mean? Well, it’s all fun, but sometimes I think I’m just not cut out for a career in this. I mean, it's so competitive. I understand the worry, but art isn't just about painting or the 'starving artist' stereotype. It’s a lot about concept, understanding human emotion and perception, and those are skills applicable to many careers. Yeah, I guess I always see art, especially traditional art forms as... a bit old-fashioned, really. But you never know, maybe I'll get a job in art education or curation? Exactly! Or digital art! There's so much the field has evolved into. Just last weekend, I saw this new exhibition in Lancaster using augmented reality to bring art to life. Really? That sounds fascinating. I feel like the tech-art blend is more interesting to me. It can be a really cool way to engage people with art. I remember we went to a digital art festival in Falmouth last summer, and some of the installations were incredible. Falmouth’s always been supportive of local artists, hasn’t it? Oh, yes, definitely. And now with all the students and influences from the university, it’s even more vibrant. Yeah, speaking of influences... I've been playing this game that has really influenced my art style lately. The way it combines 2D and 3D is amazing. Oh, what game? Might be fun to check it out. It's... ...wait um, I think it’s called "Semblance".

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time I had to make pancakes for fifty people at that conference? Fifty people? That sounds chaos. What was the story behind that? Well, the morning team decided pancakes for breakfast on the last day of the conference. Just thought it'd be something fun and different. But of course, they weren’t thinking that I would be the one to ruin their lovely plan by burning half of them. Oh, how did they react? You okay? They were really good. They just said, "Don't worry, dear, we've all been there." And I ended up having to make more. Everyone ended up getting their pancakes, just a bit earlier than planned maybe. That’s quite the pressure. I can imagine! How did you feel afterwards? Honestly, a little shaken but it was funny. And it made for a good story, I suppose. And you know what, the clients really appreciated the effort. So I guess it wasn’t all bad. Well, that’s great to hear they reacted well. Where did you get the idea for this job, actually? I mean, project co-ordination can be so varied. It kind of stems from my days at uni, actually. I used to coordinate events for my student society, and then I did some internships where I could see how projects really work. One of my lecturers suggested I apply for some project management jobs and here I am. It’s been quite a journey. It sounds like the skills are transferable. What about work-life balance, do you find it’s hard or do you manage? It’s definitely a challenge. Especially during peak seasons or when deadlines are really tight. But I’ve learned to prioritize tasks really well now, and communicating with my team is key. And, you know, it really helps to have a supportive team and a place where you can go and sit for a minute when everything's chaos. That’s important. I completely agree for my job too. Anyone from your social circles you’ve caught up with lately? Actually, yeah. I met up with Emily over the weekend for coffee.

Right, let's consider the consent form again for our first seminar's online participation. We need to ensure it is clear and concise. Absolutely, consent forms can often seem daunting to participants. We want to minimize any confusion. Agreed. It's also important to comply with the university's policy regarding research and participant welfare. Let’s break it down into essential parts that they need to know – what they're agreeing to, how we'll use their data, and how they can withdraw consent if they wish to. Good point. We'll need to make sure that any data collected is anonymized and secure. And I believe we also need to mention our ethical guidelines, just like we have in our research. Right, but we need to avoid jargon. These students are from different disciplines. Hence, we have to balance clarity with academic precision. True. Let me check our university's standard template for guidance. We can start with that and make necessary adjustments for our purposes. That's a good idea. Perhaps we can even have it reviewed by our university's ethics committee beforehand. Yes, that would be wise. I can arrange that. In terms of the seminar structure, what are we thinking for the first session? Well, we've been discussing an introductory lecture, then a case study followed by group discussions. We'd need to prepare some resources, maybe some videos or reading materials. Good plan. The key is to make it interactive. We should also give time for Q&A. How about leading the session with real-life examples, where the barriers and solutions for communication are clear? That could work well. We might also consider having a guest speaker for one or more sessions who has had real-world experience in international business communication. An international perspective would be valuable. We can allocate another session for that. We should also encourage questions and encourage students to think critically about communication barriers. Right. We can do a mix of theoretical overviews and practical examples. I like that. It will help them relate the theory to reality. Regarding activity planning, have we thought about group size and how we'll facilitate the discussions? I was thinking smaller groups, 5 or 6 people, plus a facilitator who can guide each group. That will work. And we should allocate enough time for each activity. How about we start with 20 minutes for each case study activity?

I've been feeling overwhelmed with work lately. We have these assessments due soon; it's been super stressful. Yeah, I talked to [Name] today and he's feeling the same. The reality is successful lecturing and the hustle of living in London is different from those glossy expectations I used to have.

So, I was browsing this weekend. I found this app that's supposed to help you reduce food waste. Oh, really? Tell me more. Anything to cut back the cost and be more environmentally aware. Yeah, it's called 'Fridge Pal' or something like that. You put in what you have in the fridge and it gives you recipe suggestions. Say you've got three carrots, a bit of sour cream, and some chicken leftovers, it'll show you recipes using those ingredients. Seems clever. That’s actually a genius idea. You know how many times I've thrown something away because I hadn't thought about using it in time. Exactly! I was just looking at their blog too. They had an article about our grandparents’ generation and how little food waste they had because they cooked so many meals that used every part of the ingredient. Like making broth from bones or using every scrap of veg for a soup. True. My granddad used to make these amazing vegetable soups. You couldn’t believe the amount of veg he would use. He’d say, “Waste not, want not.” And maybe it's partly because when our grandmas were young, they had to manage resources during rationing and all that while raising families. Their generation was so practical with food. It really stands out when you think about how we’re raised now. We're so used to disposable everything. Speaking of our grandparents, did you see that TV series that came out last year based on life around the time of the war? What was it called. Oh, was it… um… "Home Fires"? "Home Front"? No, it was about women in rural areas... I might be thinking of different shows. But yes, definitely, "Home Fires"! Ah yes! "Home Fires" dealt with women in rural communities working together during the war. It showed great community spirit and how resourceful they were. Right, exactly. And that brings me back to food and waste. I was also thinking about those old ways while watching it. Imagine having to manage so much just to feed a family. It’s indeed a different era. But some of those lessons are still very relevant today, like minimal waste. Yeah, plus the culture around here... We could all do with being less wasteful, not just with food. Like the recent news about the plastic bag charge.

So, how was your week? It's been alright. Got through the usual administration tasks. Well, at least you have that established. While you’re on changing the subject, how are the kids doing? Oh, they're great. The little one is in this new 'learning' phase where everything is about animals, which is so cute. She's always asking for information about animals. That's so great! It sounds like she's really interested in the natural world. Yeah, and the older one... Yeah? Well, he's still into his coding and robotics. I just hope all that coding doesn't creep into his language too often. Hah! We can only hope the practical application exceeds the purely theoretical.

I used to take my first wife's children to the sea. Costessey is right by the coast, and it was always a treat. It's sad really, because I've not been back there in years. Oh dear, I can imagine how that feels. I spent so many years involved with children, taking them out and about. When I stopped working, it felt like I lost a part of myself, especially since I've always done everything for everyone else. That sounds a bit like depression, doesn't it? I've noticed that with a lot of my students after they graduate or retire; they often feel lost without that structure. But did you ever consider looking into volunteering? It can give you a sense of purpose and allow you to connect with others who might be going through the same things. And being around nature like the sea can also be very therapeutic. You know, volunteering seems like a good idea. Maybe something that includes the outdoors. And it's funny you mention it, because I saw something about baby blue tits nesting near the coast. For me, looking after something, bringing life into this world, it might just give me back a reason for getting up in the morning. Ooh, that sounds interesting! I've never seen baby blue tits. I used to have a pet bird when I was younger, but this would be different. A bit spiritual, perhaps, to help mother nature do her thing. Exactly! And there are so many places where you can volunteer to help with wildlife conservation projects, especially in coastal areas. Plus, it could be a way to meet new people, make new friends, and maybe even learn something new. Yeah, I like the sound of that. The problem is it can be tough when you've dealt with money problems for so long. It feels like every spare moment should be spent looking for work or sorting out finances. You aren't alone in struggling with that, though it does make things tougher for sure. But you know, sometimes taking care of your mental health can actually lead to better financial stability indirectly. When you feel better about yourself, you might find that you're more focused and able to tackle those tasks more effectively. And volunteering could actually be a stepping stone to something more job-like eventually. I've heard that doing good for others can really lift your mood.

So, I got this new mask. I don't think I've told you about it. It's like an overnight cream that you apply and leave on overnight. Oh really, what kind of mask? I've been using this hydrating hair mask from a brand I don't usually buy from but I saw a discount, and it's been a game-changer. It does seem like a good investment if it works as well as it sounds. Totally. It's just... the real job of getting into weekly or biweekly routines is always the challenge. I know, right? Between work and everything else, it just feels like one more thing to fit in. Totally. But you know what's helped me stick to a routine? Having a friend to be accountable with.

Yo, mate, been meaning to catch up for ages, can't believe how busy we've been. Same here! I've been deep into this new volunteer role, and you've landed a new job, right? I've been living on a tight budget since leaving uni. It's a bit stressful. But I can't trade this opportunity. Sure, it is. It’s a sacrifice that will pay off in the end. And don’t forget, we're also talking about future plans here. Yeah, and then there’s moving house next year.

So, how are things going with Tom? I haven't seen any updates on social media. You know how he is, he likes to keep things private. Oh, things are really well. He's been doing fantastic. As usual, he's so particular about how the kids are doing and making sure they're not missing out on anything because of me not working. That's really kind of him. But most of the time, it's great seeing them all together. It creates this little village-like atmosphere. Ah, they love reading. Tom has this whole library set up in their room, and we read together every evening. It's actually become this lovely bonding time for all of us. And Mila is getting into baking with me. She calls it 'cooking magic'. So sweet. That's adorable! I bet Tom is thrilled. He always wanted to have a family. He is. And seeing them so genuinely happy with the setup has been so healing for us, really. It's like the perfect balance. Well, most of the time, anyway. A perfect balance in family life is something we all strive for, isn't it? I remember when I first started teaching, I couldn't have imagined balancing that and starting a family. How do you feel about your role in the household and the kids' relationship with you now? It's been a big journey, to be honest. At first, the step-parent thing felt daunting, you know? But over time, I've learned that it's not about being a replacement for their mum, but about being this unique figure in their lives who loves them just for who they are and contributes in my own way. That's really wise. You've really done a good job of finding your place. I know sometimes it can feel like you're not sure where boundaries lie or if you're doing enough. Exactly! That was a huge struggle for me, figuring out my authority without overstepping. But Tom has been great, really supporting and guiding me.

So, I was browsing on Pinterest yesterday and came across an idea for a customized photo gift. Imagine a wooden picture frame with the recipient's names and a heart, and then little magnets that can clip on pictures. You could be constantly updating it with new memories. Well, it could add up if you want a fancy wooden frame or use a lot of photos. However, if you keep it simple, the main cost would be the magnet printing and the photo collection. You could also use free images and design the frame yourself if you or a friend has the skills. I'm thinking it might be a cool gift for friends who have a lot of shared memories. I might consider doing something like that for my birthday next month as well. Hey, speaking of birthdays, have any of your friends from university heard from Jack recently? It's really good. You'd really enjoy it, especially since it's a bit more experimental compared to the usual stuff. Which one? I've been stuck watching the usual suspects. I might take a look if you recommend it.

Oh, did you find anything else besides houses online? Actually, I did. I was browsing through eBay and they have these really quirky light fittings. Want to see? Oh, show me! I kind of do love unusual lighting. This one's quite interesting – it's actually quite affordable, and I could see it working perfectly in our dining room. Yeah, actually, let me pull up my notes here to see if any of the prices match our budget – we're planning to replace some of the lamp shades, anyway. You're actually really good at budgeting. Well, it's partly out of necessity! But yeah, I do enjoy organizing and looking for the best deal. Let's see, if we get the lights and renew the lamp shades within our budget, it'd be a major win. For me, it's not just about the appearance – I've found that good lighting can totally change the mood of a room. Where did you get the idea for this? Honestly, I found it because the one we have now in the living room – it's plastic, you know? And the light it gives off... it's just so drab. There's one on Rightmove, actually, really similar to this one, shown in the interior design of a living room that I liked. Just a small detail like that doesn't seem much but, it makes a big difference. Yeah, that kind of makes sense now that you mention it. And let me ask, have you looked into getting estimates for those light fittings? Sometimes they look nice online but are a nightmare to install or require special fitting skills. Not yet, but that's a good point. We should probably factor in potential changing costs. Definitely. And also check reviews. You'd be surprised what some people will or won't say. True, true. Though, if anyone does review them as 'unnecessarily difficult to set up,' it might be a bit of a deal-breaker for me. I love how we're already planning contingencies. Well, thinking ahead is part of adulthood, I suppose. Speaking of planning ahead, what’s the latest with our house search? Nothing new yet, but I did find two potential viewings for next week if we can make them work. That’s great! At least there’s movement. Have you also looked at the schools? I remember we were interested in specific criteria around that.

So, I hear Sarah's dog did something incredible again last week. Oh really? That's not surprising at all. I've seen what they're capable of. Yeah, I've really enjoyed training him. It's taught me so much about patience and understanding animal behavior. I bet it's been a challenge sometimes, but rewarding too, right? Absolutely, especially when you see progress. But, talking about work, how's it been for everyone? I've heard loads of changes at your place. Yeah, there have been a few. They're trying to improve staff training, which I think is good, but it's added a bit of pressure to just trying to fit everything into the day. Yeah, same at my hospital. There's an emphasis on new training for infection control procedures and everything is taking longer than it did before. It's the same at our care home. More paperwork, more checks. But, I suppose it's all about patient safety, isn't it? Definitely. For me, it's more about working with the residents than filling out forms all day. Exactly. Sometimes I feel the paperwork is getting in the way of the actual care. It's hard when you're trying to do your best for the patient or resident, and then have to worry about all these other things. Speaking of which, how is the new colleague settling in? Alright, I think. She's been helpful so far. But I've noticed she doesn't come across as confident as she probably is. I've tried to make her feel welcome and offered to help her out. That sounds really considerate of you. More staff should do that, I think. It's always tough starting in a new place. Yeah, and we had a similar problem last term. We really had to rally around and support each other. Yes, and we did. I think that's what makes a good team. Right. On a different note, I’ve been looking into redecorating my living room. It feels like it's last had a proper update 10 years ago. That sounds fun! Where do you think you'll start? I’ve been dying to get my hands on some new decor for my own place. Especially something more modern and minimalistic. Maybe there's something on that big furniture sale coming this weekend. Oh, don’t you dare go without me, if you spot anything good!

So, I was browsing on weekend. I came across an article about getting a good night's sleep. It says that people who sleep better at night tend to have better routes into cities. Makes sense, really. Most cities aren't laid out randomly, and if you understand the layout and can navigate well, you'd likely have a clearer head when you wake up. I see what you mean. But getting a good night's sleep is a bit easier said than done, right? Life gets in the way, and then there's the light and noise pollution. Exactly, and it seems like many people get lost in the city, especially new cities, and then there's the bonus of struggling to find a good route into a city. Talk about a double whammy. So what does the article suggest? Well, it tells you a few things, but mainly to try and stick to a routine - you know, same bedtime, avoid caffeine and screens before bed. It also talks about how some people have managed to improve their routes by sleeping better. It's like those old stories of village folk relying on their instincts and their sleep to guide them? Maybe there's something there. Well, if you think about the early explorers. Navigators relying on the stars? They had to have impeccable directions, but also a good night's rest, right? It's like the human brain functions better when well rested. Makes you wonder about those people who claim they can still navigate after one or two in the pub, really. But you never know, maybe the combination of a good memory and a bit of luck? But it's not just about the directions. There was this story about a pilot who, after switching to earlier sleep schedules and improving his sleep quality, noticed his reaction time was much better, and his landing patterns weren't just more precise but eerily so. Ah, okay now that's interesting. Of course, reaction times are crucial in flying and it makes sense that sleep would impact that directly. It did. And the article quoted him saying that after a while, he felt like navigating in his sleep. Funny and a bit eerie at the same time. And have you ever tried camping? Oh yes, one summer. Didn't sleep very well actually. There's something about the fresh air and all that

So, I got my hamster yesterday. His name is Rudy. Aww, what's he like? That’s so cool, I had a hamster as a kid. Her name was Sparkles. She was so lively! I’ve got my bus pass already ready for the month, if anyone needs a lift. Perfect, someone always driving would make it easier. And it'll be a great afternoon out.

I keep reading "Iost" instead of "I own" today. Imagine how that would turn out in a game of Risk. You'd own everyone but be pronounced as you've lost everything. Ha! Now, questions for the game: have you guys checked if there are any update versions available for this year? Sometimes new editions come with adjustments to the rules or maps. Good call, Sarah. Actually, there is an updated version. Let me just check its compatibility with our game setup here. After our last few rounds with questionable luck and questionable pronunciations – you've been mispronouncing "Genghis Khan", you know. Anyone find it awkward saying "Enfield" when the game doesn't make it clear you need to pronounce 'field' like 'feeld'? Yeah, and the classic "Jee-uns"; how often do you think the world would change if 'Gin' was pronounced like 'Gee-n' in Gin and Tonic? I'm just relieved humanity hasn't yet solved the eternal mystery of how to rationalize chocolate consumption during Risk games. It's like the universe says, "You're conquering nations, but also eating chocolate, and both are just as stressful!" Speaking of stress, I just tried to relax drinking a cup of herbal tea. Grabbed the wrong cup by mistake. Man, mint tea can really destroy the taste of chocolate, huh? While you're on changing the taste, has anyone tried recording our game? Like, voice notes of our strategies and whatnot? It’s for educational purposes, obviously. Oh, because having evidence of how we historically screw up strategy after strategy would be a good educational tool, right? Exactly! It’s like real-time leadership and decision-making 101, minus any actual leadership or decision-making skills. Now, now, let’s not undermine our strategic geniuses here. I mean, did anyone else smell this when we started?... I thought I left the kitchen... maybe it's a mind game tactic, "The Scent of Confusion"? Yeah, that's how we keep our opponents off guard. The youth of today have no idea the importance of psychological warfare through smells.

Oh, Lena, remember that first year's flatmate who discovered today that she's pregnant? Of course! Young Chloe, unreal! I really don't understand how it just...happens. I mean, do people not think about it before? Honestly, Jess, sometimes I wish I could roll back to those days when life felt a bit more manageable. All we had to worry about was which module to drop and if we'd actually pass our first year. True. But at least now, we can say with confidence that we've passed our first year of just trying to survive uni. Yeah, now we can graduate from making coffee in the morning to being properly career-ready and everything. Seriously though, what are you thinking you'll do after uni? I'm still torn between doing arts or switching entirely to engineering. I know, right? I've been oscillating between wanting to get into content creation on YouTube and pursuing a career in marketing. I think most of us are just assumed we'll figure it out. But it's terrifying, you know? It is. Especially with all the pressure to have a 'stellar' career right off the bat. Sometimes I wonder if it's all just a giant waste of time, really. What, becoming 'successful' isn't worth the effort? No, it's not that. It's just...sometimes I look at celebrities or people in my parents' generation and they all seem to have this whole togetherness thing figured out. And then I'm sitting here, wondering if I'll ever be able to balance my own life without dropping everything. Well, at least now you can bond with Chloe over something other than lost lecture notes or missed laundry days. True. Although, Chloe's biggest current worry seems to be whether her future in-laws will want her to be on birth control if she decides to pursue a career. Again, timing right out of the textbook. It's like uni wasn't already confusing enough with all the coursework and social pressures. Now add in these 'real-life' decisions. You know, during freshers' week, there was that workshop about university life, and this one speaker said something...kind of stuck with me. She said that no one has it all figured out, even if it seems like they do. Like, imagine Drake's life—we only see the concerts and the Grammys, but do we worry about when he's worrying about the future?

Yo, man, did you finish that history project? Nah, mate. I started it but it's too much. This thing about Renaissance art and philosophy. It's not my cup of tea. I know what you mean. Especially now, the system’s so geared towards exams. Why can’t they just teach us practical skills and life skills instead of all this stuff that won’t affect most of us after school. True. Life would be a whole different ball game if they taught how to balance a budget or how to respond to racism and poverty. That stuff affects us all. For sure. It feels like they're preparing us for some fantasy world where we all have perfect jobs and no problems. Exactly, like the whole consumerist society aspect we discussed in our ethics class - "buy, buy, buy" without a thought of the consequences. It's mad when you think about it. Mhm, and yet we’re taught to study for these exams and that determines our future. It's so stressful. Almost like it’s all about measuring us and not what or who we are. I mean, it's not all bad but it could be different. Like the school doesn’t push us to debate wider world issues. We need to learn about politics in a way that isn’t just revision for tests. And the scientific research - it’s all about who can make the next big breakthrough without really thinking about moral implications. Look at all this tech we're getting in, people say it's progress but is it really when it benefits a select few and abandons the rest? Like my mate’s family - doesn’t have a laptop, it's tough for him to even catch up with homework. And then on the other hand, seeing stuff like Musk and Bezos making all this money, but meanwhile in Slough, people are struggling. Exactly! It's like the disparity is widening. Our borough could do with some of that investment for once. True, but changing the world takes time. We could start by doing little things like helping out with local community projects, that sort of stuff. Definitely. Actually, I saw this comic about poverty and inequality. Might be a good meme for the project. Comic? You could use that. Anything to break it down in a way people can digest. We could also do a skit.

So, how have you been keeping yourself busy? Oh you know. The usual. Well, I've talked to our neighbour the other day. He's been hooked on this new podcast about the recording process. Really? He always has questions for me when I see him isn't he? What's he been saying? And he also mentioned something about ensuring you have the right microphones for your specific voice types - which we both know well isn't going to help you much though. Yeah, my voice is quite... distinctive. But, you know, it's just good to hear people passionate about something. It's nice to share in that. Absolutely. It's refreshing, actually. He's also on about this new physiotherapy he's been trying out for his bad knee. Yeah, I know joints can be such a pain. Stiff at the end of the day, especially when you're not moving much. Exactly! He's been saying it's made a huge difference, though. Considering surgery before but now he's much more hopeful for a non-invasive solution. That's good to hear. He needed a plan B because the NHS waiting list would have made it hell. Oh, definitely. It's crazy how long you can wait if you're not privately insured. Yeah. Anyway, I've also been thinking of trying some new clothes. Nothing fun since whenever. That's a good idea! We should look into some charity shops around here. Sometimes you find great things. It might be a good change of pace. I was shopping online but it's so much pressure when you're comparing yourself and all. I so get that. It can be overwhelming. It's also about finding clothes that are comfortable and make you feel like yourself right? Yeah, plus it's better for the environment. Always. Do you ever think about trying a new diet or working out? I've been wanting to start but it's hard to get motivated without... well, I suppose it's a vicious cycle.

Oh, did I just burn it or's it supposed to look like that? Looks fine to me, but you're doing the cooking so I trust you. Thanks for the vote of confidence. I think this recipe might need some... creativity. Oh don’t worry, it’s all about improvising, right? Remember that one time where we tried to ruin a cake? Oh my god! We were like 16 and wanted to make something fancy. We ended up with a rock solid, inedible thing. But delicious in its own weird way. Yeah, we were among the first to discover that baking needs a little more precision than throwing everything together. Speaking of exploration, have you thought about exploring more culinary skills? Like maybe a cooking class or something? I saw there's a great one in this town. That's actually a brilliant idea. I feel like I'm stuck in a routine with my meals. Anyone for pasta then? You still haven't mastered pasta? I guess not. It's like the theory of relativity or quantum physics to me – I know the basics but I'd need A-levels in pasta studies to get it right. Alright, let’s focus on what we’re good at – watching a movie and eating. How about we start with that and then... see about the culinary adventures later? Sounds like a plan. I was planning to watch the new movie that came out last week, any preferences? Not really, I haven’t caught up with recent releases. You pick. Hmm, let me check what's recommended. Oh, 'The Accidental God'. It was praised for its quirky humor and unexpected twists. Sounds like just my cup of tea. After the cooking disaster, we could use some unexpected twists. Agreed. Let’s give it a go then. Speaking of which, how are you liking it up here in Cambridge? I love it. It’s surprisingly vibrant and lively for a university town. And the work-life... I do feel like there’s a better balance here compared to London, if you can believe it. That’s great to hear, I was really worried about the pace of life and stress levels for you after the job change. It’s been an adjustment, but I prefer the pace here, and the living costs are more manageable. Though, sometimes I miss the convenient central London location for everything.

So, I watched "Tenet" yesterday. Oh yeah? What did you think of it? I haven't seen it yet. It's the whole time travel thing that's put me off. It's just so confusing! But Christopher Nolan's films always are, right? Yeah, but once you understand the theme of inversion, it's really quite clever. Inversion? What's that? Oh, it's like how keeps changing backwards and forwards, and affects time in both directions. So you're telling me the future causes the past? Well, kind of. It's not just that simple, but yeah, you're on the right track. It's like "Inception" but with time instead of dreams. Does it have the same level of complex action scenes? Definitely. The central fight scene in the Oslo airport is insane. Yeah, and visually it's quite something. I mean, the negative footage? Sure, that's a new concept for many of us. I assumed that the negative of everything inverting would just look like a weird ghostly world, so it was interesting to see Nolan tackle that. So, you're saying it's worth seeing even if it's a bit confusing? Absolutely! Once you get past the initial confusion, it's really enjoyable, and the message about humanity and time. Maybe I should watch it with someone else and we can figure it out together. Good idea! You could explain it all to me when I see it next. Yeah, or try together. It could be fun, questioning each other about what’s really happening at each moment. It's definitely a film that's better with someone else and it really makes you think. Good, because it's such a unique experience and it’s one those you’ll enjoy more if you're not alone. You know what else I love about Nolan's films? They're all about the human condition. Absolutely. Each film, despite the genre, always keeps that central to the narrative. It makes them more thought-provoking and enduring. So, no spoilers for anyone who hasn’t seen it? Nope, let’s leave it at that. If anyone watches it, come back and we can discuss, argue, whatever. Awesome! Thanks for the recommendations, guys.

So, how was your weekend? Oh, it was lovely but tiring. The GCSEs are going to be a nightmare this year with all the changes. Well, at least you got some good photos, I assumed? Oh, they are good. The Eiffel Tower at sunset was the perfect shot, but apparently I wasn't carrying it carefully enough. Should've had a selfie stick. You, with a selfie stick?! I can't even imagine. Hey, it's a great tool if you know how to use it. Anyway, the real star of the show was the food. The cheese and the bread, incredible. I went to this tiny bakery and... I bet it was the fromage. You love the French cheese! Absolutely. And the variety! I discovered a new favorite — it's like a cross between brie and camembert but creamier. I really should've brought some back. We'll compensate by having a French-inspired dinner one of these nights. Let's plan for the week and see when everyone's free. Maybe Tuesday or Wednesday? I'm pretty flexible. Just let me know and I'll hobble over. You will be just fine. In the meantime, I'll prep whatever you need for dinner this week. How's... do I even know what you like already?

Yo, mate, how was weekend? Weeeeell, it was pretty chill. Decided to head down to Chichester after work. It's always a nice escape from Croydon, you know? Yeah, it's a lovely spot, isn't it? Maybe I'll join you. Definitely do. It helps to have someone to bounce ideas off. By the way, have you seen the schedule for the firework display at St. George's Day? No, but I've got some friends who are preparing for it.

Yo, I got us a voucher from that new Indian place. We have to use today though; it expires. That sounds great! Thanks, mate. You're welcome. You know, we should cook rice tonight because now I think I can cook it right – no more questions if it's mushy. Haha, yeah, the science of rice cooking! But actually, I've learnt that if you measure the water and set it for 20 minutes, it comes out perfect every time. Oh, that's actually really useful! I've heard about using a 2:1 ratio but I never stick to it. Yeah, it's 2 parts water for 1 part rice. And let it sit for a bit after switching off the heat, that helps too. Exactly, so it absorbs all the water. Exactly. Tonight, I'll make it and we can have it with this curry I found in the freezer. That sounds perfect. What's in the curry? It's Chicken Jalfrezi. The packet says it's medium spicy but I'll add some jalapenos to give it a kick. You ok with that? Absolutely! I can't handle super spicy but some extra heat is nice. But hey, be mindful of my condition though, right? Of course! We won't overdo it. Now, let's talk about the rice. What do you like about yours? Hmm, I'm simple. I like it just fluffy and not too salty or fatty. Got it. I'll do the same. Also, make sure to check the meat. Why? What's wrong with the meat? It's been in the fridge for a bit, and it smells kinda funny now. Oh no! We should probably toss it then. Yeah, it might be bad if it smells off. Better safe than sorry. Absolutely. Gosh, I thought I was going to impress you with my cooking and then the meat goes off! Haha, no pressure! Impress me with being healthy and carefree. Got it! Alright, now onto the cooking tutorial. Lay it down, chef. So here's the rice. Now, pour in two cups of water for every one cup of rice. And don't forget to rinse it first if it's Basmati, to get the starch out. I always rinse Basmati, yeah. Then boil, then let it sit for 20 minutes at low heat with the lid on. After boiling? I usually just boil and finish with the heat off.

So, how was everyone's weekend? We had a good one. Helped out at the community centre and met some new people. Yeah, the tea and cake social was great. We sold some quite a bit too. It helps now and then. I heard rumors there might be a new place opening near town that does really good German food. You ever been? Not yet, but I'm right behind you if it lives up to word. Foot-long bratwurst for dinner sounds like heaven after coming home from a day at the support centre. You get any interesting cases this week, Sarah? Yes, quite varied. One person was going through a really tough time with finances. Sent her some advice and support to seek help from local services. That’s good. It’s important they know there’s help available. Exactly, and sometimes they just need someone to talk to, you know? I sometimes volunteer at the library, there's a little group that meets there for people to just chat. It’s surprising how much it can help. That’s brilliant work. So, what about uni, Emily and Hannah? Anyone studying something particularly interesting right now? It’s interesting, but sometimes very thought-provoking, to the point I take home more than I expected. And in my work, I see a lot about life circumstances affecting people, and it’s really driven me to want to help more directly. Maybe apply for a role in social work eventually. There’s always more we can do. Speaking of which, do you remember when I was in your shoes, going through less fortunate times? More than one person stepped up to offer me a helping hand, and it’s not something I’ve ever forgotten. Oh, yeah, we were all quite concerned back then. There was a time we all chipped in for a week’s groceries for you, didn’t we? Definitely. It’s moments like those that remind us of community, and it’s good when we can do something so simple yet so impactful for someone. It's also funny to think back, like when you could barely afford to turn the TV on and just played video games all day. We had to ration who watched what.

So, how was your week? It's been alright. Got a bit of a cold, so didn't do much. Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. Take care of yourself! Yeah, will, thanks. You've been working out at home or anything? I've been trying to stick to my routine, but it's hard with the weather turning and all. Took a few walks. That's about it. Walking is good, it's something most people can do. It is. Saves money on the gym membership too. True. Speaking of money, have you considered just trying to find any kind of work, part-time or otherwise? You were saying before how you never worked. Yeah, I have thought about it. But it's hard to get out there when you've been out of it for so long. Plus, there's barely any job that can't be done from home now. It's tough. I know what you mean. But there are some jobs that can be done from home and they might help you slowly get back into the workforce. Even the council often has part-time positions for older people or for those needing flexible work. Yeah, perhaps. I should really look into it. Volunteering or part-time jobs can be a good starting point. Plus, doesn't your local community centre have free or affordable fitness classes? Yeah, they do. And you know, it's a conversation changing the world one shared dinner at a time, right? I suppose so. Seriously though, if you ever need help with looking at jobs or want to have a coffee to brainstorm or anything, I'm here. That means a lot. We're all in this together, and I believe you've got stuff to offer whether in a paid job sense or otherwise. Maybe we could even get something organised through the community centre? That sounds like a plan. Okay, so to recap: walk more, maybe look at part-time jobs or volunteer work, and let's see about those community centre activities together.

Right okay so I think it's time we started talking about school's upcoming exams. Yeah okay. You two, talked about this recently didn't you? Yeah we did mum. Daniel mentioned he's feeling quite stressed about the maths part of questions because some of his friends said the past papers were pretty hard. Ah, okay. And let me know if you need anything else, whether it's clarifying those past papers, setting up a study group, or just needing someone to talk to about anything. Mmm, thanks. That'd be really helpful.

Oh, did I ever tell you about's Dad's story when he took the tip off his car? Whole windows and everything slumped out when he went over that little bump. No, I don't think so! That’ll be some kind of story. Yep, and then there was the time we got a new sofa and somehow the moving company managed to leave it outside and it rained. Stuck in shrink wrap for ages, it was a soggy mess. Oh, I can imagine the look on your face. I bet. Might have been the moving company trying to get out of lugging it in. Probably, but they gave us a discount. That made it a bit better. But speaking of furniture... how’s that new lounge suite? It's nice, quite comfy actually. But the real test was when ANON's friend ANON came over. She brought her whole family and suddenly we needed the whole house. Like when someone unexpectedly asks, "Can we wash your clothes too?" That’s happened! Though, they were only toddlers and the clothes weren’t the problem—the problem was the volume of it all. Toddlers make the messiest clean-up side of things, for sure. More so than the fact they want to do it themselves. I know some people might see it as helpful, but personally, I’d find that a bit invasive. Yeah, and unless they are a deeply trusted friend or family, it’s crossing a line. Maybe worth having a gentle conversation about boundaries with ANON if you haven’t already. Boundaries are such a necessary part of adult life but sometimes hard to enforce, especially with family. We had that extended family issue when everyone felt like they could just show up with a present for instance. Not all presents are welcome presents. Oh, I know right? You get these unwanted, very thoughtfully chosen gifts that suit everyone but the person you’re actually giving it to. We got that pair of hideous, gaudy golf shoes from our grandparents one year.

Mum, I've got some news. I'm afraid it's not great though. Oh Jeez what is it sweetie? Well, I've just found out that my company is going to be restructuring and it looks like the project coordination team is one of the departments that's going to be made redundant. Oh no! That's awful, sweetie. I know right? I was hoping to build a career there but now it seems like my hopes are going down the drain. Well, don't lose hope too soon, sweetheart. You've had such good experience and skills. It's just the universe telling you it's time for a new adventure. I know but what about the financial side of it all? You've got enough savings to keep you going while you look for a new job, right? Yeah, for a little while, but how long can you survive on barely over two thousand a month in London? I'm sure you'll find something within the next few months. Now that you've got this experience it should be quite easy to find a new role. Plus, you can always consider taking extra courses if you want to upskill. Yeah, I'm thinking about that too. I also really need to start looking at my spending habits, spend less on shopping therapy and stuff like that. Speaking of which, how is your gym membership going? Oh actually, that’s a good point. Oh, so many topics! It's just that the summer holidays are going to be pretty long this year, and I want to make sure we have some fun, but also some structure in the day. Ah, right.
