Fractals are these shapes that look the same no matter how big or small you make them. They're very cool, just like the patterns in Snowflakes. Yes, maybe you can watch a video about it later. We could also go swimming, or visit your friends. Or, you could start learning the guitar! You've always wanted to try. That's a great idea! I'll find a kid's guitar tutorial online. We could have a go and maybe see if it's something you like. And jobs around the house, right? Maybe we can do some small chores together. Yeah, definitely, it's good for you to learn and it makes the day feel more structured. And what do you think about maybe having a picnic at the park one day? Or going to a free event in town? Oh, that sounds wonderful! There's usually something in town during the summer. And picnics are always fun. Shall we say we'll do a picnic one day and maybe even have some Japanese food? Since we're trying to be interesting adults, right? Alright, so for now, let's plan a picnic or a park day for next week and start with some guitar practice. And we can look for those fractals videos together. Sounds like a great plan. And for dinner, how about some of your favorite, like pasta with cheese? That sounds perfect! Do you want that? I don't think he understands, but he's definitely excited! So, to recap, structure with fun, successful challenges , visits, picnics, and some helpful chores around the house. Sounds like a plan! And please, help me with the fractals because I wan to seem super intelligent to our little one. I'll help you. But for now, let's enjoy dinner and maybe watch a video with Speaker_3 about Stick with Mick. Every time with Stick with Mick. [Note: Speaker_3 is a toddler and cannot articulate full sentences, so their reactions and "speech" are depicted as straightforward reactions (e.g

Oh, did I ever tell you about that time I had to explain what a hyphen was to an American colleague at work? No, you didn't. What happened? Well, it was this guy named Mark from Dallas, and he kept saying "high-fat" without the hyphen and I was like, "Mark, it’s a compound adjective, and it should be ‘high-fat’ with a hyphen." He just gave me this look like I’d just mentioned quantum physics. That sounds like a right fine Midlands to Texan culture clash. Exactly! It was one of those moments where you just let out a sigh and think, "Okay, another one for the 'Misunderstandings in English' article." And what about your writing? Any new ideas you’re excited about? Actually, yeah. I’ve been wanting to write a piece on the Liverpool accent and how it’s depicted in film and TV. It’s always so far off the mark compared to reality. Now that’s something I can appreciate. One of my students was studying how accents are stereotyped and misinterpreted in media. It’s kind of fascinating, the way certain accents are reduced to just a few stereotypical phrases or features. Absolutely. And the Liverpool accent in particular, it’s so distinctive and yet, when you see it on TV or in a film, it’s usually just a superficial version of itself. I had a student who used 'Scouse explorer' as a character in one of his pieces, and it was actually quite good the way he handled it. But yeah, the accent is far more nuanced than most people realize. More nuanced than “eh laddie, gawin doon ‘ead”? Exactly! Although, that one does pop up in most caricatures. You know, it’s interesting how we both ended up in education jobs, though in different areas. What’s your take on the standard/popular British accents in today’s media? Well, from an EFL perspective, Received Pronunciation has always been the gold standard for textbooks and teaching materials. But you know, more and more teachers are realizing the importance of teaching real-world English, including regional accents and dialects. Yeah. It’s a good thing. I mean, if you’re thinking about educating people to communicate effectively in English, it’s not just about grammatical rules or vocabulary—it’s also about understanding cultural and regional differences in how the language is used.

Oh, so many experiences! You know, as soon as you start talking about these things, it's like all my memories come flooding back. I know, right? You were just reminiscing about your first time at the Blackpool Illuminations, wasn't you? It's questions like this that make me realize how much time has passed since those days. Yes! I was only 15 at the time, and I thought I was so grown-up. Walking along the promenade, seeing all those lights and the crowds... it was magical. I just loved it. Even back then, you had a bit of a knack for making everything seem perfect. You know, I think you even convinced me to try the infamous Blackpool rock candy without my realizing it was basically just sugar on a stick, cleverly designed to look like it had a certain... "waterfall" effect. Oh, you mean the “stick of broken dreams?” Exactly! Well, that was then. I hope you're not planning any more sugar-induced revelations for me on our next trip. Where did you get that idea? You seem to have developed quite the sweet tooth of late yourself. Remember that Easter cake you made last year? It was a bit of a disaster wasn't it? I wouldn't call it a disaster! It was a unique, artistic expression of Spring. And besides, we’re talking about a dessert that tried to combine the best of Easter and India. It was a bold move, but clearly it wasn't just me who thought that rose water and cardamom were a match made in heaven, am I right? More like a match that required a fire extinguisher. But it was good it was fun, and it ended up looking like abstract art. Well, and it tasted better than it looked, I swear! You know, baking with you is always an adventure. True. I do think we need to start cultivating new traditions though. You know, family traditions. Like, did you want to make those Easter cakes for the family this year? Actually, I was thinking about that. Maybe we can turn it into a bit of a tradition for the family meetups. And since next Easter we might have little ones around, maybe a simplified version? I love that idea. And you’ve been doing well with the company at work too, I heard. You're finding your feet, aren’t you?

So, how have you been keeping busy? I haven't seen any posts on social media about your pet's antics lately. Oh, they're always keeping me on my toes. You know how it is. I've actually been working on improving our pet supply business, though. The market research is showing some promising trends towards natural and eco-friendly products. That sounds exciting! I'm a bit curious, have you ventured into cosmetics at all? Actually, we are. Our skincare range has been coming along really well, and it seems like there's a real demand for vegan, cruelty-free products. It's tough to keep up at times, but it's rewarding to see something you've worked on being well-received by customers. I totally understand that. Was it harder than you expected to expand into another product line, or has your experience with pet products given you a good foundation? It's a different ball game, definitely. But we've been fortunate to have a loyal customer base that trusts us. And it's funny because it's actually helped us engage with their human side as well, rather than just their pet side. We've gotten a lot of feedback from people who use our skincare products as well because they like the ethical stance behind them. That makes sense. It's like the synergy between the two businesses is building a stronger brand image. I used to have pets, and now my kids are at the age where they'd love to help look after pets, but we don't have the space. It's really good to know your business is growing in that area. It's been a journey, doesn't come without its hiccups, but we enjoy it. Speaking of which, have you ever considered including educational materials on your products or website? It's more of a saying. What's that from? It's a bit of a joke. It means everyone—even people who sometimes don't eat breakfast—will eat pancakes on Pancake Day. Maybe with strawberries and a tiny bit of chocolate, not too much. Well, we can certainly work on that for next year. Speaking of things we’re working on, have you checked if we're still going to Science Museum trip on Saturday? Yeah, it's all sorted. We need to make sure everyone, including Speakers 3 and 4, wash their hands before we leave, right? No eating a pancake on the way to the Science Museum! Right! No pancakes on the way to the Science Museum! No pancakes! Definitely. And hopefully we're not in a rush. I heard they have some fantastic interactive exhibits, especially something about hands-on science. Exactly. Speaking of which...Speaker_4 just had an assembly about children living in poverty who sometimes don't have enough to eat. It got me thinking. We're so lucky. Yeah, we are. It's sad to think there are kids who go to bed with empty tummies when we've got... Why don't we start a small project in the class about using leftovers creatively or even just tasting new foods as a way to make sure we appreciate what we have? I love that idea. It ties in with both teaching children about living less wastefully and understanding better the challenges of others. We can involve parents too. What about a story contest? Like, make up short stories about a character who learns to appreciate food or helps others find it? It could be really impactful, especially if we can inspire some children to share their stories with their families. Perhaps even get a local author to look at them?

I keep reading that Chinese restaurants first started popping up in the UK around the early 20th century. Do you remember the first one? Hmm, I've read that but I'm not sure off the top of my head. But yeah, wasn’t it a kind of exotic cuisine back then? Yeah, something truly exotic and rare. I mean, now it's like our fourth most popular takeaway, right? Exactly, and it’s so widespread! Even in my job as an agronomist, when discussing international trade in food stuff, Chinese produce is always a huge part of the conversation. You know, talking about international trade reminds me of the news today. Did you both catch the story about the UK's new trade deal with Australia? Yeah, I did. It's a pretty big deal, isn’t it? While we're on the topic of big things, have you guys seen the newest film that just came out? I heard it’s really good. No, I haven’t. But I'm curious, what’s it about? It's a pretty serious drama actually. I assumed we might want to watch something lightening for the dinner? Well, after a bit of sobriety, why not? But first, let’s enjoy this lovely Chinese food. Speaking of which, did you pull out the menu book as I suggested last time? Oh, no. I didn't realize you wanted that. I was thinking we would just pick a couple dishes from the menu on the wall. Actually, I thought we were adventuring today. But the book does have some interesting options, like this “Secret Szechuan” dish they always talk about. Alright, adventurer’s dive in next time. For now, let’s stick to the usuals and not scare ourselves too much. We could always add something spicy later if we dare. Agreed. And actually, I have a bit of news. A friend from our old housemate squad is coming for a visit next week. We should definitely catch up and have a night out. That sounds like a plan! We haven’t seen her since we moved into these new roles. How long has it been now? Well, I’d say almost a year. We should really reconnect. But speaking of reconnecting, did either of you attend Aunt Helen's funeral recently?... Oh, that was tough. It brought back a lot of memories, especially thinking about the times when we'd watch Bob the Builder together.

Right okay so I'm going to write down all the first things that come to mind when you think of your childhood. Well it's been talked about before but the war years had quite an impact. We used to have air raid drills at school and people used to have to share their homes with families from London. Yeah I remember my grandma telling me about that, how my great-aunt had to share her house with relatives evacuating from the cities. Oh absolutely. It was very character-building for everyone involved, I would say. Definitely, and then moving forward to when you were about our age, or just before, what's something that really stands out in your life then that we might not have experienced. One of the most defining experiences for me was when the council estate where we lived had its first properly modernized housing development. It was amazing! Central heating, its own garden—it was like a whole different world compared to the little terraced houses we all used to call home. Oh, right, I remember hearing something about that. I think even though it was before our time, it really shaped the community and the outlook on what kind of living standards people could have. Indeed, and that kind of comes up in conversations about social change in the UK, often over the importance of good housing, right? What about when the first motorways started to appear? Because driving was a very different experience back then. Oh absolutely. It wasn't all motorways at first, but the initial ones were revolutionary. I remember my father saying they were almost like "dream roads"—so wide and free of obstructions compared to the old A-roads we used to use. The only issue was the drivers, haha. Some didn’t take kindly to the speed limits of course. [laughs] Oh yeah, I've heard about that. I mean, nowadays with driverless cars on the horizon, it's quite interesting to think about how far we've come and yet, how some things remain a challenge—like teaching self-driving cars to understand human intuition on the road. For sure. Speaking of which, have you seen the headline about Google's tax deal? I feel like it's a microcosm of the challenges we have with large corporations and national tax laws. Yes, the headlines did catch my eye.

I've decided I need to get an aerial hoop for our spare room; these are all super cool hobbies you guys are developing! I love my aerial hoop classes! It's like flying, Mum! Or it's like climbing and hanging upside down while making "Pippi Longstocking" faces . Yeah! It's so much fun! I can't wait to see you progress. You're really enjoying it, aren't you? Yeah! Is that a real dragon you have drawn here? Yes, she spent hours drawing that! What do you think? I love it! It's looking really brave and strong. You should enter a contest! Maybe next year. Maybe. But for now, let's watch "Barbie and the Great Adventure". For Chinese New Year this year, we decided to see if we can make it more exciting with dragon dances and decorating. Can we decorate more today? Maybe after dinner. But first, let's eat some real Chinese food to celebrate! Good idea! How does everyone feel about trying some hand-pulled noodles and trying to make a wish on them? Tradition says that if you can eat them without breaking them, it brings you good luck for the year. Yay! Let's do it! I can try to make the wish! Me too! And, maybe we can do a family Chinese New Year wish later. Absolutely! We can write our wishes and put them on the wishing tree we'll set up in the living room. And what about the planets? Can you tell me more about them? You promised when I got my new telescope. Of course! You want to learn about Mars and Venus and Jupiter right? Or the real question is, do you want to learn about if Barbie can actually explore them . Well, that depends on if Barbie has a space suit and if she can find a rocket. In the meantime, we can do some planet drawing to help imagine it. Yeah! I can draw the rocket too! Can I draw a spaceship too, like the one in Star Wars? Absolutely! You can draw whatever you like. Just make sure it can't take off in the middle of dinner. Good point. This past term at school, did anything cool happen? Yeah! It was our term's assembly, and my class did a really cool performance about planets and space. It was so much fun to see everyone dressed up like astronauts and scientists.

So, Rome. It's colder than I expected, isn't it? Definitely. London weather would've been warmer at this time of year, wouldn't it? Are you still staying at the Air BnB you mentioned? Yeah, it's been great so far. Romantic place isn't it? I mean, for an Air BnB at least. Yeah, very quaint. I'm trying to get used to how Italian B&Bs work. Everything is backwards compared to what I'm used to. You get breakfast before dinner here, and don't even get me started on the coffee. The coffee is worth it, right? Especially with the added bit of sweet. You can't beat Italian coffee. But have you guys decided on dinner plans? I was thinking of trying that new place by the Pantheon. They have a great pasta dish... And dessert! We have to try the tiramisù. You can't leave Italy without trying their Tiramisù. Agreed. But it would be fun to explore some non-tourist spots too. Recommendations? I found this great place in Trastevere. They have good local dishes at reasonable prices and not too crowded. I've heard good things about Trastevere. But have you guys noticed the local accents? I love how they pronounce 'Rome'... For a while, I was convinced they said 'Roams'. Like, the city that roams. Coming from Australia, the accents are quite different to what we're used to, but I do love the sound of Italian. More like "Roma" with a strong emphasis on the 'O'. Exactly. Anyway, let's make a solid plan for dinner and explore that next. We should also consider visiting some friends of mine here in Rome. You have friends here? Yeah, I studied abroad here for a semester. It's actually why I reopened my café back in Birmingham, inspired by the local café culture here. That's sweet. It sounds good. Maybe you can take us there during our stay? Would be fun to meet some locals. I'd love to. Perhaps tomorrow. It's a great way to see a less touristy side of Rome, too. Perfect. I'm also curious, how do you guys find the language... learning and all that? It's a challenge, yeah. I'm really trying to pick up more phrases here. How about you, Tom? Though I studied Italian at uni, speaking it in real life is a different story.

So, I hear you’re planning a hen do? Yeah, today we finalized the venue and most of the activities. Hopefully we don't have to change anything last minute, but well who knows, right? It’s just, the bride’s so excited, she’s been questions non-stop. Which one of her friends is organizing? Her friend, Emma. She’s pretty organized, right? Erm, yeah very. Emma’s been listing out things keeps coming up with new ideas. She’s probably too enthusiastic. Hahaha, I can imagine. But at least she’s into it. Yeah. Is she considering something like the traditional English activities? Definitely. There’s gonna be a big baking session we’re planning, and maybe some crafts. Maybe a photo booth with funny props? That sounds like a great idea. We can have it done by a professional so we get good photos. And what about drinks and food? Any theme? I don’t know about theme, but we're planning it to be mostly finger foods because with crafts and stuff it'll be easier. And for drinks maybe some gin and mocktails? That’s perfect, can't have the bride getting tipsy too early. Yeah, perhaps also some healthier options, vegan or vegetarian for different dietary needs. Genius. Anytime a group is involved, you always need variety. And we thought it’d be nice to end the night with a cake, maybe even one that has a hidden theme, surprise design or something. Can the venue help with that or will Emma just order one. She said she’s checking. Some places do offer custom cake designs or can suggest someone. That would be so great! I’ve seen some amazing hen party cakes. Yeah, it’ll be a nice touch. And do you know if we’re getting a photographer or someone taking pics for us? Emma said she’d look into hiring a photographer for the day. That’s good. Nothing says ‘I’m worth celebrating’ like professional photos. Do you think we should plan a surprise for the bride or just let it be? I was thinking along those lines but I don’t know if that’s her style. She seems... over the moon anyways. Maybe we just surprise her with a really nice gift or a toast that really shows we appreciate her? I love it. Something sentimental but fun.

Bro, did you see the first ingredient's "whole chicken" today? I swear, some people's kitchens clearly use expired products. You're right though, you've really got to watch out for those, haven't you? I mean, do people not think about the tiny chance of salmonella and E. coli? Honestly, that makes me think about this one time I went to Paris and I had to deal with a very dodgy hotel. The water tank keeps coming backwards due to a clogged filter. You'd think it's some kind of practical joke when your shower started spraying water everywhere instead of just falling down. Oh man, just like the "sparkling" tap water they serve here. You can sample from the murky source - "Two euros each, or 10 euros for the entire hotel's collection." Exactly! But, man, speaking of creative water conditions, did you check out the little brochure at that last resort we stayed in Spain? They had a list of "recommendations" for the potable water. Like, "Boiling is optional, diluting with wine might make it more palatable," that kinda thing. I remember that! Their "natural spring water" had the most unnatural smell to it. It was like the essence of the sea mixed with some unknown algae. Like, what are people supposed to do, become sommeliers of water in order to stay hydrated on vacation? Or maybe humanity is finally working towards the "one weird trick" doesn't come from fitness, it's from surviving "mineral-rich" water. You make it sound all exotic and adventurous. But the truth is, no one wants to wake up in the middle of the night, questioning the safety of their water bottle. If only hotels were honest about their water treatment processes. It's less confronting than finding out you've been guzzling what amounts to natural fertilizer. I'm sure that's on the list of perks they don't advertise. "Bathing in recycled water, take advantage of local nutritional content!" You know what's the real problem, though? We could have saved ourselves from all these upsets if we just cooked our meals. There's something comforting about making your own food, no matter where you are. True that. Especially when you're thinking about recipes. I mean, I went through a phase where I obsessed over recreating the perfect spaghetti carbonara. No shortcuts, no packet sauce... just eggs, cheese, and patience.

Right okay so I need a shopping list of stuff for the flat's groceries. Onion; lentils; what's that one about tinned fish again? Sardines? Right, sardines. Still have some pasta left? Yep, I just unpacked the new batch from the charity shop and it's still quite a lot. Okay then, pasta and of course, those fractals I bought last week? They still set for decor. Yeah, still a few in reserve for decorating stuff. Okay. Sourdough’s running low, maybe just need a single loaf this week. And did I pick up any coffee like the other day? You might need another big pack if you’re running low. What about that organization stuff for your sister’s birthday? Oh, right. 58. I need a birthday card. Make sure there's a little something that doesn't mention age if it mentions at all. Twenty-seventh or thirty-seventh? For me I’m this side of fifty and it feels like no one checks these days. Exactly. I assumed we’d avoid 'you’re still looking younger than ever,' 'looks like 39 to me,' or anything like that. Should work out fine with a current theme or perhaps a neutral spiritual one, maybe something comforting? Yeah, comfort and simplicity. Something general about well-wishes or maybe artworks and they usually do a good number of theme-based cards. True. I can help with picking one up this week. Thanks, appreciate it. And let’s consider some calendar inserts or fobs, any preferences there? Personally, I like fun ones with quirky sayings or space and astronomy themes. That works for you but what about the flat's changing tastes? Let’s pick a general option that isn’t too on the nose for anyone’s habits. Maybe something with uplifting quotes or just simple dates and structure. Makes sense. Can we see if there’s a good combo set at the charity shop again? Definitely, and perhaps some art for the walls. We could put up more of those pictures we started with last month. Yes, we did. The collective art from the school, it’s really come together well. Someone actually recognized yours from the group piece I posted online. Really? That’s nice! I hadn’t heard. Yes, a comment that really enjoyed the collage with the hockey stick. They thought it looked like a memory collage across generations.

So, I hear you've seen the new neighbours who've moved in next door. Yeah, they seem alright. Strangely silent though, wouldn’t say more than five words in my two encounters. Still it's quiet compared to, shall we say, some of the neighbours we've had in the past. Haha, those were characters, weren't they? I wish I could have met Mr. Jenkins, he was always out in his garden till the crack of dawn. Oh right, the one who would let his chickens wander right up to our fence, and then complain when they interrupted his songbird observations. He's a bird lover, that's for sure. Might have been the reason why his wife was always looking so startled. Ah, yes - "Two's company, three's a couple birds." Women, children, and chickens— Mr. Jenkins’ order of priorities. Anyway, shall we give these new neighbours a bit of time to settle in? Might help with their reserved nature if we show a bit of neighbourly warmth. Good idea. Anyone fancy a walk this afternoon? I noticed there's a pretty decent trail just behind the village, great for a bit of fresh air. Perfect, I think the girls would love a bit of time outside. And I need to start exercising more anyway. After this, maybe we can plan a trip to the local bookstore. They're supposed to have a great selection, and a recommendation from Marianne would be. That sounds like a plan. Plus, it's a bit too early for gardening, even though my new plot is just begging for attention. Oh, I can already imagine the garden you'll have there. Perhaps we could create a shared gardening project for the family? You know, ease into it with some herbs and small veggies. That's brilliant! While you’re at changing the world byte by byte, I was wondering if anyone can help me with my next job – I'm trying some DIY in the house for the first time and I just bought these Ikea pieces. Ikea? Oh dear, you’ve got a holiday project ahead of you. But good on you. I used to almost faint over those instructions. I swear those instruction manuals are designed to cause mental distress. Honestly, I can't wait. It’s something new to figure out. Though, I did consider getting help from that Swedish guy down the street.

Yo, mate, did you seen any of that latest Cyberpunk's online shop story? On the interwebz. Nah, I don't really use social media much. Got too much on my hands with uni stuff. Aye, I know what you mean. But this was something else. It was all about how this new online fashion shop let people totally customize their whole outfits, real time, with AI glasses and stuff. AI glasses? That's quite a concept. Seems like a bit out there, even for cyberpunk themes. Exactly! And, you know, there was this feature where you could even try out the outfit on your face or body using the AI. Sent your selfie and it applies the clothes digital. And does it do real-time adjustments like the lighting making the colours look different or anything? Exactly! So it takes into account your body shape, skin tone, and also the environment you're in. Cool tech, right? But it's funny because it's not like anyone needs it, but it's kinda futuristic and I guess people like that. For me, it's just a bit weird, you know? Yeah, it's weird, but weird fun. Makes me think of the 'Black Mirror' episode with the social scores. It’s like if we let tech spin out of control, we'd end up with some dystopian shopping therapy. You're right! There is one Black Mirror in there somewhere, really. But you never know, maybe it'll be a thing. And what’s weird is that some people apparently pay real money for things that are just digital. It’s like the real value is kind of lost... True. It’s hard for me to wrap my head around it. Seems like the value's more in the concept or just the fact that it's a digital good. Aye, value seems to move from actual objects to ideas or experiences. That and it's another thing to spend money on when you're already in debt with all the student stuff. Definitely. I try not to dip into my laptop too much when it comes to spending. But, you've gotta admit, it's creative. Reminds me of when we tried to 3D print our own designs and it didn't go well. That stuff almost makes it look easy... Oh, I remember that! You came up with the idea to print a new phone case and it ended up looking like something from a 90s sci-fi movie.

Right okay so I've been looking at heating options for the new house. I was thinking gas central heating but I realized it's going to cost a fortune to install. Hmm, yes. Have you considered electric? There are quite a few new eco-friendly options now, and if you get a smart meter, you can really control the cost and the environment impact. Yes, and you get government subsidies for some of that now. I think you can even get help with the installation costs if you go eco-friendly. That's really helpful to know. Also, would it be too much trouble if I asked you, Speaker_3, to look at the house for me at some point? I need to check out the plumbing and electrics before we buy. Not at all! I'd be happy to but when do you plan to go? Let me see. I hope to look at the place next weekend, if its owner is okay with that. Great! Make sure you check the loft for ventilation and the ceilings for any signs of possible roof leaks or damp. Right, will do. Now, about lunch... this is a bit unusual, but I've come across these really nice local artisan bakeries. Shall we maybe plan to bring some bread and cheese along on our coastal walk? Perfect idea! I also really want to check out the seafood options along the way. If we are going to be out for a while, I think a picnic lunch sounds ideal. Sounds good! And if you guys want, we could also get a takeaway from that new pub that just opened up. They have excellent fish and chips. That's a great idea, Speaker_3! And then, we could do all three if one of us can pick the takeaway up along the way. I can pick it up. The walk will be so much fun with food stops! Oh, by the way, have you heard about those Virgin Experience Days? They've got some great ones for couples. No, I haven't. What kind of experiences do they offer? Everything from flying lessons and wine tastings to hot air balloon rides. I mean, if we ever want a fun weekend activity, it's an option. That's very romantic. And there are almost always discounts if you book in advance or use their promo codes. Yeah, sounds like a plus.

So, how was your day? It's been alright. Got through most of the report for the board meeting this week. Hopefully they don't notice the little mistake I made with the charts. You know how meticulous they can be. Did the kids have a good day? Yes, they had their usual Monday routine. But, there was a bit of a drama with the little one who had forgotten their lunch money and of course, as the primary parent, I had to deal with it. Ah, the joys of parenthood. You'll tell me if I'm any less 'mummy' because of it. Ha! I wouldn't dare say that in your presence. It just shows how busy even our children's lives are. How about your project? Any significant advancements? Quite a bit actually. We're starting to see some real patterns emerge with our data. It's looking like we might actually have something concrete to share at that conference in March. Provided we can iron out a few more wrinkles. That's great to hear! We could use a bit of good news. What about you, how was your day in the lab? Or should I say 'classroom' given your job now. Assessing and managing, that's quite the career change for you. Enjoying it? Yeah, it's nice to see the 'real world' application, you know? It gives a different perspective on the assessments I have to write and administer. Although, I couldn't wish for anything more than to be back in the lab doing my own research. True, but the skills are transferable and this role allows you a level of understanding and influence that you wouldn't have otherwise. More variables to deal with, that's for sure. More politics, less pure sciences. Just as scientific, just with more humans. True, very true. You know though, I find my time managing assessments allows me to interact with people a bit more. It’s not just numbers in a database. Stories, isn't it? And isn't that one of the most interesting things about your job? Exactly. Every student, every teacher, they all have their own story. It’s complex and messy, but incredibly rewarding. That’s something to be said for any role that deals with people. We're all stories, after all. I guess that's why I miss academia sometimes.

So, I was at the hospital yesterday and one of the patients's dogs was brought in. It nearly accelerated my healing process just seeing it and how sweet it was. Really, animals can have that effect. It's fascinating how much they can comfort us. Reminds me of when we first got our cat, questions how much it'd fit into our schedule and house but it turned out to be the best decision. I’ve always loved dogs, right? But I've been thinking of trying to get a parrot for my desk at work. keeps coming up in conversations with people in the office. You know, it's supposed to be stimulating to listen to someone chatter away. [laughs] Parrots sure do have a lot to say, but have you considered the commitment level? My brother has one, but it's a lot of work. And the noise, oh god the noise. [chuckles] It's not for everyone, I'd say. [laughs] Yeah, the noise can be overwhelming, but they're so bright and it's like having a tiny, feathered person in the house. I’ve always been interested in birds. Maybe I’ll volunteer at a bird sanctuary or something before making any decisions. That’s a great idea! The stimulation and the responsibility could be really rewarding. Speaking of stimulation, how’s everyone’s financial situation these days? It’s been... interesting. The renovation project for the house has taken longer than planned, so that's stretched us out a bit. But we're managing, and the decorator really understands our budget constraints. We’re actually considering a bit of a culinary revamp. I was thinking of taking a cooking class. It’s not the cheapest hobby, but it might be fun and, who knows, maybe even lead to something more? Seems like the right time for those kinds of changes. I've been having to be really frugal with my business. The market’s unpredictable, but we’ve had enough work lately that it’s been bearable. I’m actually changing careers from nursing to more administrative things. It’s a step, but I’m hoping it’ll make things more financially stable. Though, I have to admit, it's scary to walk away from something I know so well. It does take some courage, that's true. But it sounds like it’s the right move for you.

Oh, Dad, remember that first trip we took to Paris? When we nearly missed the Eurostar due to my forgetfulness? Oh indeed, love. It was chaos! You spent so much time queuing for the wrong ticket booth and then – of course – you left the passports at home. I've heard the story, but I wish I could have seen it! I'd almost forgotten till now. Mum nearly had a fit. She was calm as ever, but... I could tell we were in trouble. But we made it just in time and had a lovely time, didn't we? Though let me tell you, even then, I had the feeling we were in for a faster pace in Paris than we were used to! Speaking of exploration, have you thought about exploring more of Europe with family trips? It’s a great way to create lasting bonds and experiences. That’s a great idea! Maybe we could try Italy next. I heard the food is as good as the scenery. Yeah, and maybe we’ll have enough notice to plan ahead this time. You never know what unexpected adventures might come up though! Absolutely right, the best adventures are often unplanned. And with travel, it’s all about the journey as much as the destination. Speaking of journeys, any good recipes for us to try cooking from the different places we visit? That would add an extra layer of appreciation for the culture. Actually, I have a great pasta recipe that I learned from a friend who’s an Italian chef. I can share it with you guys during the next trip or just in the meantime. Oh, that would be lovely! We could have a little family cooking evening or couple of them even before we leave. That’s a brilliant idea! Because who knows, the food experiences might even inspire our next destination. Absolutely, sometimes it’s the little moments like trying local dishes that turn into the best memories. I’m all for it. Let’s plan a mini-Italian evening here at home first and then see about those tickets. Yay! And since we are close and we all love cooking and eating, this could be a fun way to connect. Especially with you both thinking about recipes and me finally learning to do it right. Well, with me... I do hope any cooking event we have involves someone else doing most of the grunt work.

So, I was thinking that for next semester we could possibly move away from the more traditional lectures and try these more interactive group discussions instead. That sounds like a great idea. What are your hopes for that? Better engagement from the students perhaps? Exactly, and also to get them to questions and answers kind of format. You know, get them thinking and discussing the topic rather than just taking notes and forgetting it all. But actually, I've been thinking, we could also try and set up a kind of project-based module. You get the students to work in groups and come up with their own little research projects. It really makes them see the relevance of what we're teaching. That's a great idea too. It just needs a bit of planning to make sure the projects are relevant and can be realistically completed within the semester. And we'd have to consider how to structure the module and what kind of support they'd need. Yeah, and we also need to talk about how we might assess their work. Right now, we're mostly on written exams and essays. But for project-based work, perhaps a presentation or a report submission could work better? Maybe a combination of both? Yeah, and maybe even have a peer review process. That can be really valuable for students to learn from each other. Absolutely, so let's also consider the logistics of organizing the groups. Do we want them to choose their own groups, or do you think it would be better for us to assign them? I've always found that when students choose their own groups they might achieve better results and they enjoy the process more. But it doesn't always work that well and sometimes the project is inconsistent across the groups. On the other hand, if we assign them, we might lose some of that enthusiasm and the different perspectives. An alternative could be a combination again, perhaps we could do base groups according to areas of interest and then allocate students to different projects within those groups. That's a nice approach, but we'd need a way for them to declare their interests. Would that be feasible? Definitely. We could build that into the first class of the semester and make it part of their introductory week. Gives them a chance to meet each other and us as well.

Oh, did I mention my first move's cost? I discovered today that the coffee machine isn't included in the removal. You'd think that's one of the first things they'd cover. Still, now you'll get to pick a new machine! That’ll be some kind of excitement. But then there's the whole thing with storage costs. It feels like they're charging an arm and a leg just for keeping a few boxes somewhere. And get this, they won’t let us negotiate. It’s like they have a set price for everything. I’ve always valued a good cup of coffee, but I never thought I’d get in an argument over a coffee machine removal. You might need that coffee now to deal with the politicians. What are your thoughts on the latest Labour leadership drama? Oh, god. It's a mess. But you know, deep down, maybe it’s a good thing. Maybe it’s forcing people to think about what they really want from politics and what they’re willing to fight for. I'm with you. I mean, it's frustrating, but at least it’s stirring up some good conversations. There’s a certain idealism still there. For sure. Especially after we've seen the reality of the last few years, people are looking for something more substantial – not just the nice sounding promises but actual action. There’s this theory I’ve been playing with about doing too much versus doing too little. It’s all about finding that balance and working towards ideals without burning out. Tell us more. That sounds like food for thought, especially for someone who’s recently retired or just planning to step back a bit. Well, it’s a bit like, if we all keep believing we can fix world problems alone, we end up overextending ourselves. But if we dive deep into our own little ins and outs, we end up missing the bigger changing the world picture. It’s a good thought. I think a bit more balance would do most of us good. Imagine having the energy and motivation to tackle something real, something truly impactful, without having to overwhelm ourselves. This theoretical model you mentioned, you think there’s a way to implement it practically in our lives or in our community? Yeah, I mean, it starts with small things – don’t take on too much, prioritize, and actually execute well.

Yo, anyone hear about that new craze using river names as pseudonyms? What are you talking about? Is this a thing now? Oh, you mean like "Tamesis" or something? Sounds like a cosplay for boat enthusiasts. Yeah, I'm not sure it’s catching on. It's pretty niche. I saw a post on some random Tumblr about it, right? They were saying how river names have this mysterious, old world vibe. But like, how is "Thame" or "Chavone" supposed to be mysterious? Haha, "Chavone." Idk, mate. I used to have a mate in London who swore by just like naming himself after his favorite pub. "The Red Lion" or something. That was his handle for years. Hehe, that’s kind of rad. But going with the river names, I thought it was more about London culture, you know? Like, there's a little bit of pride about these ancient water paths. Yeah, I get that. But I’m from Oz. Our pseudonyms? More like this side of the equator symbols or weird Aussie slang. River names wouldn't even register. You’re more likely to nickname someone after a plant or an animal here in Australia. True that. But over here, it’s all about what you’re into or how you're feeling at the time. Like, my sister once named herself “Leapfrog” because she was leaping into new adventures. I guess contexts really do vary. Anyway, did you guys catch that story about the canal boat that floated 20 kilometers and the owner still didn’t notice until it was too late? Oh yeah, that was wild. Some guy just forgot he’d hired a boat in Oxford and it just meandered all the way to Reading. Seems like either he was totally absorbed in his work or just wasn’t paying attention. But you gotta wonder, how often does that happen? It’s surprising how common it is though, especially on the larger canals. I read in a magazine that several incidents like that happen each year. The owner ends up with a £500 fine if anyone reports it. That’s crazy. But it’s one of those “only in England” kinda stories, right? Definitely. You wouldn’t see boat slip-ups like that in the US or Australia. Our canal systems aren’t as extensive or central to daily life. You’d think security cameras or sensors would trigger an alert.

So, I got a match with this guy on Tinder and he’s actually from our uni. Imagine how awkward it'll be if we're in the same class? Ha, unreal! Chester uni's pretty small, right? What if you end up having to do group projects together? That's a nightmare... Oh, isn’t that awkward? But, have you seen this guy? Is he hot or just average? I actually went through his profile. He seems alright. He’s into hiking and playing football... So keeps himself fit, maybe. Well, if it's a good-looking guy with similar interests, there's always a chance it could work out, isn't there? But then again, online dating is sketchy. Who knows if he's genuinely good or just posting perfect photos? True, true. I've had my fair share of dodgy guys on there. The language they use—it's like they're trying too hard to sound sophisticated. Right? And these people always have the most outrageous uni major or whatever. One guy said he was majoring in something like ' Forensic Accounting and Dance Therapy’. What even is that? Oh, I’ve seen that. There’s this guy who listed 'Advanced Vintage Tax Law and Amateur Stand-up Comedy'. It was clearly a joke but I ended up chatting with him and he was actually funny! Ah, but have you thought about what you'd actually say if you met up? I’m always in doubt, like, do I keep it casual, or should I be all 'intellectual and curious'? Honestly, I reckon the best approach is the 'I'm kind of awkward but trying my best to make conversation' one. We can just be ourselves, right? More or less. But, I just wish Tinder had a 'socio-economic status' filter. Some guys are really into this elite lifestyle thing and it’s just off-putting if you're not in that world. You mean like if he’s always taking about his second home in Zanzibar or his latest visit to some fancy restaurant in London? Yeah. I feel bad because I want to travel but I’m also worried about being real about my financial situation. Like, no need to lie but how much do you share? There's being honest and oversharing. Clearly, those trips and fancy places aren’t everyone’s reality. It's just... weird when they act like it's our norm.

So, I was browsing through the news yesterday and came across an article about how benefits are going to be changed again. Ah, haven't talked about that recently. What are they planning to do this time? I heard it now, the government’s talking about yet another benefit cut, isn’t it? Going to affect the disability benefits I believe. Exactly. And to make matters worse, it seems like they’re actually looking into implementing a ‘total cost of living’ cap. Which means if the government decides living is cheaper due to certain factors, benefits can be cut. That does not sound right. After all the protests and verbal commitments, they still seem to be pushing forward with these cuts. It just seems like a bit of a slap in the face for people in need, doesn’t it? What I don’t understand is how they hope this is going to fix anything? Cutting benefits isn’t going to help people get back on their feet, it’s just going to make it even harder for them. It’s like they’re punishing people for relying on what the government provides. It’s a very backwards way of thinking, if you ask me. I’ve voted with pretty much every party at some point, but the way things are going now, it’s really making me question if voting even matters anymore. You know, it does matter, but it’s disheartening when you see decisions taken that affect you directly without your input or consideration. Exactly. For instance, benefits and all that should help people in need, not kick them when they’re down. But it seems like it’s the latter happening more often now. You know, I saw this documentary about people in similar situations the other day. Seems like the government's whole strategy is to keep people in limbo. The idea is that it should be tough enough to ease them back into work but it doesn’t seem like they understand what it’s really like. True, and changing the rules every couple years doesn’t help. People can’t plan for their future or even try to improve when they’re dealing with uncertainty like that. Plus, it’s so much about making those on benefits look like the ‘problem’, when in reality it’s the system and the lack of good job opportunities.

Oh, did I tell you about the fundraiser I attended today? No, you didn’t mention it. Anything interesting? Well, it was at the local library for a new children's picture book. They had a meet and greet session with the illustrator. It turned out really well and we raised a lot more than expected. The children were absolutely captivated by him drawing their favorite characters and of course, many parents wanted to support the cause. That sounds like a keepsake for them. Good luck with fundraising. Oh, thank you. It was quite challenging because the recent cuts to community funding have had a big impact, but people are still willing to dig deep if they like the cause. Definitely. And how was the dinner earlier? Terrible. I tried this new recipe I found online and it turned out too salty. I think I need to stick to my old tried and tested recipe instead. Oh, well, it's all part of the fun of cooking, isn't it? For me, it was a long day and nothing went smoothly at work. Our new software update has some major bugs, causing endless delays. Oh no! That can be so frustrating. Did you speak with the IT department? Yeah, they're working on it, but it's like they keep saying "one more day" for weeks now. Computers. Can't live with them, can't live without them, right? Exactly. So, is the lounge room sorted? The new shelf unit we bought? Yes, it’s up and tidied. The TV's looking nice now, a bit more organized. That's a relief. I've been meaning to get that done for ages. We should maybe consider setting some time aside each month to sort out the house. It feels good to sit back and enjoy a clean and tidy space. I'm sure we can schedule that. Speaking of relaxation, I’ve been meaning to ask, what are we having on TV for the rest of the evening? Anything good? The new series about those engineers. I heard it's pretty good. Oh yeah, I saw ads for that. Maybe we should check it out. It looks interesting. Why not? It’s not too late. Great, I'll get that started. And I'll grab any snacks we might need. Perfect. You know, work like what you did today, with these new computer systems can drive anyone crazy sometimes.

Oh, did I sound so awful on that phone call to your parents? I hope I didn’t give them any reason to worry about me being unwell. No, no, it was quite clear though, the meds had a fair hold of you yesterday. Indeed, I suppose they do. But honestly, aside from that, I've been pretty well of late, just fractious I'd say. Which reminds me — have you keeps coming across any good jobs at all? Oh, yes. There was one in Lublin last week for English teaching, just had to set up a Skype interview. They're looking for someone to teach students up to C1. And did it go well? Yeah, well, they gave me some feedback. It was a bit nerve-racking but they seemed to like my approach. But Lublin, though... Lublin, Lublin? Lublin's alright. You know, for the job itself, it's a good place. But... Lublin. It just doesn't have it for me, you know? I think most of us have that one place while the 'other' ones don't quite count. For me, its Manchester. Do I ever really go 'home' now, though? Well, home is where families are, job or no jobs . Yeah, for sure. It's funny, the 'home' concept gets blurred when you're abroad for a while. But I was thinking… would you reckon you’ll ever settle for a while? Not just until the next good job, but until you feel settled? That's the recurring debate with myself, isn’t it? Settling down in, say, somewhere like Tarnow here? It’s a nice city, plenty of job prospects, but… personally, I feel more pulled back to Manchester and Bury. Family, friends… a sense of 'home', like you said. I know exactly what you mean. I spent a bit of time in London after uni. Fun, lots of opportunities, but it never felt truly mine. And now, being here in Tarnow... it’s a good city, but the job search, and health issues sometimes have me questioning my choices almost daily. Clearly, I should’ve settled into my previous flat sooner. But the joys of renting include being able to move. Well, for now, here is where I am. And while it's... it’s not entirely where I felt I was headed, it's a better place than I’d been before. But the weather, now that’s something.

So, how was your week? It's been alright. Got through the survey data analysis for my part-time job and made some good progress on my philosophy essay. Had the usual unrealistic coursework deadlines though, you know how it goes. Still, now I can enjoy this tea. A proper cup of tea in London? It's a luxury. Exactly. And to think that I used to think tea was just tea, before moving to London. Now, I truly appreciate it. I've heard it's a whole different ball game. You get used to the milk, first. Then you learn the different teas. Spot on. And pubs - did you ever think that just like the tea, you would get so much variety here? You can sample from big brands to local specials. Definitely. I never thought I'd want a fancy tea, but now I do. While we're at it, have you thought about food choices? You're heading back to work soon, should we grab something here or at your place? Hmmm... this pub has quite a view, so it's tempting. But if we're busy the rest of the day, maybe prep something at my place? What do you think? Good idea. We can cook, or just pick up something. It depends on how much time we have later. True. Maybe I’ll show you this tea spot next time. It’s just near my flat. Near Regent’s Street, actually. Neat! I need to get better at navigating central London. Just keep the river on your left and you're fine. Except for the times you don’t want to be in Soho. true enough, true enough. You want to hear about my job? We’re considering a new campaign, think it will be pretty big deal for the agency. Oh, tell me! I’m actually changing the topics of my research soon, perhaps we can link it or… maybe it’ll give you more perspective? Definitely. If it’s consumer behaviour or anything related, I want to hear all about it. The project is currently on the software for automated survey data analysis. Some of the insights could almost apply to marketing strategies. I’m sure they can. Yeah. It's amazing how often my work overlaps with marketing now. I know. You seem to enjoy it though. It's... I do. It feels productive, and you always know the end goal is to communicate a message better.

Good morning, children! It's time to wake up and start our day. Mummy, can I sleep some more? Alright, let’s give you a few more minutes to sleep in but then we’ve got a lot to do today. We’ve got a great plan that I think you’ll both enjoy! What’s the plan for today? We’re going to start with a lovely breakfast, and then we’re heading out to have circus skills training! Really? Is that like Gymnastics? Not quite, but we can definitely do somethings like acrobatics and juggling. And maybe even some tightrope walking with a safety harness! That sounds awesome! Can we eat there after training? Well, after training, we’re joining a friend at the Neon Moon event so we can have a picnic and enjoy some music and performances. It includes food, so we’ll eat there. Neon Moon? What’s that? Like a music festival at night? It is a music event, but this one’s during the day. It’s all about local music, art, and community activities. And since it’s indoors, we can enjoy it without worrying about the weather. Mum, doesn’t Neon Moon mean like a moon that’s not the real moon? Yes, it’s kind of artistic and different, just like the performances and food they have there. Can we do skills like in that circus movie? We’ll do our best! And we might learn a phrase or two from an Australian friend I met at the last one. An Australian? What’s that like? Well, they have different words and accents for things we say here. They might say "G'day" for "Good day." Or use "mate" like we use "friend." Can we say those words? We’ll learn those and more during our circus skills session. I like that. And can we try hula hooping too? We can try all sorts of things! Remember, we’re also planning a special dinner tonight, with what we learn today influencing what we eat. Maybe we can try making something Aussie-inspired, like a barbecue or a vegie burger with Australian herbs. Maybe we should invite that Australian friend for dinner. That’s a wonderful idea! We’ll see if we can make it work. And if we do good at our circus skills, can we get a prize? Well, there might not be prizes as such, but we can celebrate our new skills with a special treat.

You're pretty passionate about left-wing politics, aren't you? Oes, wrth resymu, rwy'n credu iawn yn hanfodion cydraddoldeb a chymdeithas o fewn rhwymiad cymdeithasol cryfach. Sorry, got lost in thought for a bit there. What were you both discussing? Oh, just politics. Your point about universal healthcare and education, that really resonates with our current system, doesn't it? Absolutely. Living in Britain, I think we often take for granted the benefits we have. But look at the rest of Europe, Scandinavia even more so. They've managed to balance a strong economy with comprehensive public services. But doesn't that come with higher taxes? And those taxes fund what? Healthcare, education, infrastructure. Things that benefit us all, prevent poverty, and create a fairer society. The return on investment in human capital is immense. I agree, but implementing such changes in the UK is often mired in bureaucracy and political spin. Not to mention the varying levels of local support or resistance. Aye, that's why it's tough. The resistance in Wales, for example, to things like Welsh education or the Senedd has been strong historically, but over time, it's leading to stronger socio-linguistic ties and better representation. Yeah, that kind of makes sense, but if I may interject, the problem with such large-scale reforms, especially in a post-Brexit landscape, is the question of funding. EU subsidies were significant for Wales, for instance. What will replace them? Good point. That's a pressing question. While I agree on changing the system to prioritize public goods and equality, funding is a critical challenge. Exactly. I teach in a university. Our funding has been dwindling for years, and so we rely more on student fees which, ironically, potentially excludes those who are most benefited by free education and health services. Yeah, and then there's the issue of what we prioritize in our budget. Always seems like defence or technological advancements get the bigger share. That's a particular issue with the current government's priorities. But there's another angle here: often, policy changes are seen as ideological rather than pragmatic solutions. Precisely. If we framed it as: "Investing in people's health and education now will save us money from not having to deal with the consequences later," then it might get more traction, no? I think that's a clearer way to sell it, but also, what about the local context?

So okay let's think about what we could write for the Linton Book Festival story competition. It has to be about something that would happen at a festival. Do you remember Helen Moss? She writes these really cool magical stories, right? Yeah! Like, the ones where the kids go to magical places and have adventures? Oh yeah! I'd totally want to have an adventure at a festival. Exactly! But actually, before we plan out a story, let's talk about what kind of festival we want it to be. Do we want it to be like a fairy tale one, or maybe more modern? Even like a book festival where all the books come to life and start arguing or something. Wait, like arguing? Yeah, in the best of ways, maybe like the "Two Books" by Roald Dahl but modern and at a festival? That sounds funny! Maybe the Harry Potter books are there and they're deciding whether to attend? Ooh or the Percy Jackson books and the Norse myths are at odds or something. I love this! So we have this idea of a magical but literary festival. Now what is the main plot? Do we have a main character or group of characters going on some adventure in this setting? Do we make it a place where magical animals come and talk or meet at this festival? Like unicorns and dragons? Why not?! And in our story, they all need to work together to solve a problem at the festival. Maybe there’s some disturbance or a treasure that needs to be found. What about the place? We could make it a really special place, like a hidden village in the countryside or something. Something like that could definitely work. How about we make it Linton itself but at a special time when magical things happen? Yeah, like once a year but only at the Linton Book Festival and it turns into a magical place. That's brilliant! You both are really helping me develop this. Can I be in the story? Of course! How about you're the one who accidentally discovers the secret magical part of the festival. Or perhaps you're there to help solve the problem. We could also have creatures from different books working together. Do you remember how in the Magic Tree House books Jack and Annie can go into different books?

So, I was browsing on Instagram yesterday and came across an advert for plant-based ‘shmeat.’ Have either of you seen that? Yeah, talked about that recently. Haven’t had a chance to try it yet. Still researching and trying to decide, but essentially artificial meat created in labs right? Yeah, something like that. Like companies are using science to produce meat without harming animals. It’s supposed to taste the same, and I read somewhere that it could be more sustainable. Right, I’ve heard about it too. There’s also this stuff called ‘synthetic meat’. Seems like a more scientific name for the same thing. Yeah, it’s basically trying to replace traditional meat. But does it taste the same? What’s wrong with traditional sources if we ensure they're cruelty-free? Well, it's about pollution and resources too. Animal farming uses a lot of water, land, and it's a big CO2 producer. Shmeat, or whatever we call it, could potentially reduce that footprint. Definitely. Also, from an animal welfare standpoint, it’s promising. Even the most humane farming practices can't eliminate suffering entirely. True. I'm all for cruelty-free food, but there's also an oddness to consuming something lab-grown. It feels like a Frankenstein's monster of food. Hey, if it isn't in itself unhealthy, why not? It could be revolutionary for the environment and animal welfare. Plus, it's like we're finally getting close to that 1980s sci-fi vision of meal pills or tubes. Except, we're on the path of edible shmeat instead of pills. Seems fitting. Curb Your Enthusiasm had a similar joke. Larry David keeps asking whenever meal replacement pills will arrive. "When are these pills coming out already?" Oh, absolutely! I watched that episode recently. It's funny how he brings up common sci-fi promises and then mocks them. Right. But for shmeat and synthetic meat, it's not sci-fi anymore. And it's not just for the meme of it either; it's becoming a viable product. That's almost upsetting. There's something deeply unsettling about having a lab-grown burger. I mean, isn’t there a certain connection with food we’re losing here? Connection to what, the animal that had to die for it? Or to the soil it grew in? For some, that's exactly the connection they don’t want to have.

Right okay so I'm going to make homemade pasta first and then while that's cooking I'll make these chicken breasts and vegetables. Ooh sounds good. You're making pasta from scratch? That's so nice of you. Yes, I do love making it. It's something my wife used to do quite a lot but I think it's brilliant. I've always wanted to try. Do you have a recipe for it? Yeah, it's really not complicated. You just need flour, eggs, and a bit of salt. You need to make sure you have the right kitchen tools though. Indeed. I have a pasta maker, actually. Makes it much easier. What's that like to use? It's quite fun, actually. You just roll the dough through it and out comes your pasta. Right. And you can make it in all sorts of shapes and sizes. Exactly! Tonight it's going to be fettuccine. That sounds lovely. You know, I saw a great new TV show last week. It's a comedy-drama. Oh, which one is that? It's called "Scales and Scandal." I've heard of it. It's quite popular, isn't it? Yeah, it is. And it's pretty funny too. I might have to check that out. I haven't seen any good new shows lately. Except for maybe that one with the time-traveling detective. "Leverage"? Yeah, that's good too, isn't it? Exactly. Speaking of time-travel, next New Year's Eve should be really interesting. Why's that? Well, we're planning to go to a family friend's party. Their house is in a new build and I heard there's going to be a fancy new soaking tub. Sounds exciting! You know, we were just thinking about the washing machine. Yours almost gone this week, right? Yeah, it's been making funny noises. Do you think it's the belt again? Could be. But I remember your wife saying it's been doing that for a while now. Yeah, but it's clunking more and more. Maybe I should Google troubleshooting tips for washing machines. That's a good idea. They have some great videos on YouTube showing you how to fix common problems. Yeah, if it's going to save us money we might as well try to fix it ourselves. I have found that so much of life's problems can be fixed with a bit of internet research.

Oh, did I ever tell you about the time I was called by someone claiming to be from the water board and they told me they could fix my 'leakage' if I paid them? Right after that, I got the most creepy chain email, asking me to forward it on to all my contacts or else... But how did you know they weren’t serious? I've heard about those right? Yeah, but like how can they even do that? It's so weird. Exactly! It's all those spam calls and scam emails – it's like they try every method to get into people's lives. But then again, we’ve just been speaking about proper phone etiquette. Do you remember that one time we tried following a recipe step by step and the instructions wanted us to use a 'butterfly fork?' Yeah! What even is that? Was that a typo or something? Someone should make a video game out of these calls and emails. Like, For a moment of Silence, it would be fun to play a game where all you do is stand in silence with the most weird foreign accents for 2 minutes. You know, I used to have quite the technology set-up – firewall, all that – and even then I'd get those calls. Yeah, but really, if they tried to pull the ‘wrong phone number’ trick, we’d always know better. Right, Mum? But it's the ones that pretend to be from real organizations – those are the scariest because you don't want to just hang up in case it's real. Ah, but the best ones are the ‘your prize is waiting’ ones. Just this week, someone claimed I’d won a holiday to Russia because of an old competition I never entered! Can you imagine? Going to Russia by accident because of a scam call? That’s something! A week in Moscow thanks to a spam call! Can we see if there’s a prize for getting the most spam calls? Oh, if only! But the point is, no matter how convincing they sound, we all need to be cautious. Even the most gullible of us could fall for something. So, just to be clear, if someone calls and says they're from the government or a utility company and it’s not an appointment we already made, it's a scam, right?

So, kids, what do you think of our holidays last year? We have some options today. Or we could try something different, maybe head to the V&A and then the nearby Science Museum? Adventure Island! Can we please go back? It was so much fun and the theme park was so cool! Right, let me think... okay, Cornwall we know, and it's a great lazy beach holiday with a few day trips. But, going to a city for a museum visit is also educational, just like the Sports Day activities preparation. And can we do some beach activities like the sandcastle competition? And build a den again? On the beach? Definitely. Now, let's talk food. We need to make sure we have enough food for [Youngest Child]'s intolerance. Someone should make a list of safe foods we can get at the supermarket. Oh, on that note, I've been reading these books that have great recipes for kids who are gluten-free. Maybe we can plan some of those meals. And can we have sandwiches, please? I like those at Cornwall. Ah, sandwiches for you, perhaps, but we need to check if they are safe for [Youngest Child]. Can you remember which shops had safe options for you last time? There was a deli in town that made really nice sandwiches with gluten-free bread. Right, good memory. And for lunch, we can make sure to bring things from home or grab some from the delis. And, mum, can we also plan a little fun trip around Cornwall? Like to [place couple visited or wants to visit]. Absolutely! We should definitely plan some day trips. Maybe we can go on a treasure hunt one day or a ranger-led nature walk? Yeah! And we could go and see if there are any pop-up adventure zones we can visit. Great ideas. And can we take those books about Adventure Island and read them at the beach again? Maybe set up a little reading retreat with blankets and a little reading nook? That sounds lovely. How about we plan our trip to include a reading day just like that.

Yo, mate, did you finish that history coursework last night? Nah, man, didn't even start it. Didn't feel like it, you know? Had the whole day off on Saturday, and still couldn't be bothered to crack open the books. Dude, you're gonna regret this. Mr. Green isn't gonna let anyone off with a bunch of excuses. He's the worst when it comes to deadlines. I know, I know. I'll try and set aside an hour this evening to get it done. Hopefully, something else doesn't come up. Maybe he’s got any new ones we weren’t expecting, you never know with him. If he does, it'll be a game changer. So you heard about the party, but what about the prefect meetings? And then add the pressure of being a prefect. It’s like almost as much work as the teachers. I mean, I was pretty sure I'd enjoy it but now I'm not so sure.
